# Phase 3 script: Act II, Hubris, from the Kithairon road to the empty house

Owner: Narrative. Source of truth for Phase 3's scene dialogue, NPCs, trainers, encounters, the three temple rites, the dungeons and item placement. Map and script agents implement from this file. It continues `design/phase2/SCRIPT.md` from beat 26. Where it conflicts with `design/PITCH.md`, the bible wins; where it touches `design/STORY.md`, `design/SYSTEMS.md` or `design/LABYRINTH.md`, those specs win on story and mechanics and this file supplies the words. STORY.md §7.2 (Kleon joins the Titans) and §7.3 (the Akropolis) are master texts, staged here word for word except where a note says otherwise. Every deviation is listed in Open questions.

## How to read this file

Phase 1's and Phase 2's conventions hold (`design/phase2/SCRIPT.md`, "How to read this file"). In short:
- Each line is one text box, about 2 lines of 36 characters. A blank line separates boxes. `NAME:` opens a speaker's turn.
- `[brackets]` are stage directions. `{PLAYER}` is the player's name and `{STR_VAR_1}` is set by the script.
- Choices are `?? YES/NO` or a multichoice, then `> YES:` and `> NO:` branches.
- The charmap has no em dash and no straight double quote. Dialogue uses `…`, `-` and “ ”.
- **Species are the Aethos dex** (`design/dex/species/*.yaml` on `claude/aethos-dex-a7c73a`), Aethos-only until the League (dex decision D5). Constants are written `SPECIES_<NAME>`. The starters are the Aethos three, in the slice's `VAR_STARTER_MON` order: 0 Nebrel (Grass), 1 Kynder (Fire), 2 Hipling (Water). Kleon leads with the starter that beats yours.
- **"Per SYSTEMS.md"** marks a system that SYSTEMS.md specifies. The text here says what the player sees; the rules, numbers and engine notes are SYSTEMS.md's.
- **Engine calls** (relics, rites, herms, the flag bank, IchorSave) are `design/ENGINE_API.md`'s, on `claude/ichor-engine-systems-5a55eb` until it merges.
- **Maps** are named in the slice's style (`MAP_THYRSA_CITY_TEMPLE_OF_DIONYSUS`). Route numbers continue Phase 2's (Routes 1–6) in story order; `design/AETHOS_MAP.md` is being revised, and the chains below are the parts to reconcile with it (Open questions 1).
- **Flags** are written by name and not claimed yet. Act II's ranges (`tools/ichor/claim_ranges.md`): IchorSave bank flags at offsets 0x100–0x1FF (256 flags), daily flags 0x4C–0x57 (12), bank vars 6–11 (6), and vanilla flags for hidden items once the Hoenn cut's batch 2 frees them. Systems with reserved runs in IchorSave (herms, prophecy tablets, pages, braziers, altars, digs, gifts, prayers, laurel trees) use those runs, not this range (ENGINE_API.md §1). Always use flag constants, never raw numbers (the Hoenn cut moves `SYSTEM_FLAGS`).
- **Trainer ids** are written by name, `TRAINER_ICHOR_<NAME>`. Act II's range is ids 160–319 (the Hoenn cut, batch 1): define them only in the world-act2 block of `include/constants/opponents.h`, set `TRAINERS_END_ACT2` to the highest id plus one, and put the parties under `/* Ichor: world-act2 */` in `src/data/trainers.party`.

## Act II in one paragraph

Chloe's sickle opens the vines on Route 6, the Eleutherai road, and it climbs north past the old border fort onto Mount Kithairon, the mountain where Pentheus was torn apart, where Aktaion was turned into a stag, and where a shepherd once gave away a baby with pinned ankles because a prophecy said he'd kill his father. Maenads dance in the firs. On Route 7, where the road comes down to Thyrsa's plain, the Titans have pitched the Kronia, a feast that never closes: free bread, masters pouring wine for their servants, and masked readers handing out better fates. Kleon is at the long tables, eating, with a third laurel he won before you got there. Thyrsa is the city of seven gates and the god's own birthplace, and its Hierophant, Thespis the Masked Player, has had his masks stolen out of the skene. You learn his rite, the Three-Act Play, and the Mask Laurel, and then the whole of Aethos fills the great theater for the Dionysia. The play is new, by an author with no name: *The Unwoven*. A chorus leader in a white tragic mask tells the story of a blind hour, a bee-woman who stole a thread, and a child born cursed, who will carry a sickle to the Loom while a gold-masked king weeps. The stolen masks hold the whole theater in a trance. Thespis hands you the satyr mask, and you break the spell the way the Greeks always ended a tragedy, with a joke. The program is signed with a little hook. In the empty theater that night Kleon fights you, because the Titans wrote you a play and nobody has written him anything. Silenos, the theater's old drunk, loses Herakles's girdle to you over knucklebones and riddles, and Thyrsa lets you go west. Route 8 follows the reeds of Lake Kopais to Lebadeia, where pilgrims go down into the earth to Trophonios; Route 9 passes the split road under Parnassos where Oedipus met his father, with Delphoi hanging on its cliffs above, closed. At Kirrha a ferry crosses the gulf. South of Aigion the girdle shifts the fallen drums off the gorge road, and Route 11 climbs to the falls of the Styx, the black water the gods swear by; Route 12 goes on over Kyllene's shoulder, where Hermes made the first lyre, into Arkadia's cypresses. Kallisto the Huntress beats Kleon six to nothing under the new moon without once looking at him. A man in the white mask steps out of the trees with a better thread, and Kleon takes it. Alethea tells him it's forged, and nobody listens. A storm-hound comes out of the dark chasing a vixen it will never catch, and stays with her; she takes her list of hooked forgeries to Astyra, to the one official who can read a forgery, the Archon's Keeper of Records. You win the Moon Laurel in Artemis's garden of endless night. Then the long road east: down out of the highlands past Hera's hill to Nemea, where Zeus's columns stand over a lion's cave nobody enters, and where a healer on the road remembers a gentle student called Phaedon; back across the Isthmus to Emporion, where the Archon's council has risen and Kerykos runs ahead to open the road of the Mysteries, closed since Act I. From Eleusa it passes the salt lakes to Daphni, Apollo's laurel grove, and goes over the pass to the capital's west gate. Astyra is the capital. A Kronist on a cart tells the Agora what every seer has found, that every thread in Aethos ends on the same day, and the herald reads the Archon's answer: if it is written, meet it with dignity. A kind healer mends your team. His sick daughter hums a song that never ends, holding a clay bull. Daphne is in the Library, trying to unwrite her book. Then the Keeper of Records answers Alethea's evidence with forged proof that she forged it, and the city votes her into exile. The decree is signed with a little hook. That night, outside the walls, Alethea tells you her real reading. The Titans go up the Akropolis on an order the Archon never sealed. You climb beside her in double battles, Kleon waits on the Parthenon steps in a Titan helmet, a woman in a closed bronze helmet tears up Athena's olive, and the second fragment goes down the old spring stair. Kleon tells you the truth he wasn't supposed to: they don't want the pieces. They want you. Under the rock, Poseidon's salt well gives you the Conch, and Alethea walks away from the city. The sacred ship *Paralos* carries you and a seasick Daphne round Sounion and through the Cyclades, to Delos, where no one may be born and no one may die, and past home at night, where a ship with no lights is turning in toward Akti. Off the main road, Euboia lies over the Euripus from Thyrsa and Marathon and Sounion are a walk from the capital; with the Conch, every island from Skyros to Lesbos opens too, all of them optional. At Kaldera, Talos the Bronzesmith tests you with clockwork and gives you the Forge Laurel, then takes you to the Telchines' sea-cave forge and tells you why the Titans want you: the Harpe cuts what the Fates have woven, and anyone woven who holds it comes apart. You're not woven. Hyperion takes the third fragment and sets the caldera off behind him, and you beat him in the eruption's glare. Talos gives you the wings an old man once threw in his fire, and every herm you anointed wakes. Then a gull from Halia lands on the harbor wall with a letter from Kydippe. The helmets came to Elaia at dawn. Your mother was gone by midnight.

**The dread,** one line each, building on Phase 2's:
- The Kronia's readers can read anyone's thread, except yours: they ask where you're from, and go to fetch someone.
- Manto, last of Thyrsa's seers, is blind as her great-grandfather was, and lately "blind in the other way too".
- At Lebadeia, pilgrims come up out of Trophonios's cave and all say the same thing: the cloth runs out.
- Seers across Aethos find that every thread ends on the same row, and the Archon tells the city to meet it with dignity.
- Off Kalliste at night, a ship with no lights turns in toward Akti.

## What Act II must do, and must not

**Must** (STORY.md §3, Act II's spine): make the Titans more seductive and the truth less believed at every beat, until the hero learns they are the Titans' key and loses everyone who kept them steady. The midpoint is "They want you" (beat 55). The low point is the letter (beat 65).

**Must not** (STORY.md §2 and §4):
- say why the hero has no thread (Delphoi, Act III), or let any reading of the player succeed;
- reveal that Phaedon is Kronos (Knossa, Act III), or let the Titans name their master's face;
- reveal that Rhea is Kleon's mother (Lakonia, Act III). Her lines are STORY.md's and no more;
- reveal the Archon's secret (Olympus). He gets "You're from Kalliste." "…Hm." and an unsealed order he never denies;
- give the Titans all three fragments before Kaldera, or let Hyperion be caught;
- give away the third krater (the epilogue, STORY.md S9).

Iapetos is named in Act II, by himself, in Arkadia (STORY.md §7.2). In Thyrsa he is only the CHORUS LEADER in a white tragic mask with an ink-dark right hand, and in Astyra only KEEPER LYKOPHRON. The player can join the two by the tic, "May I tell you something true?", and by the hand; Alethea joins them at the Akropolis gate.

## The route plan

The geography is `design/AETHOS_MAP.md`'s revised map (main, 7e6f4123cf), which the director has said to build against while it waits for the user's final approval. Route numbers, waypoints and `MAPSEC_*` names are that doc's and `include/constants/region_map_sections_ichor.h`'s. Emporion is at Corinth, on the Isthmus.

MAP_DESIGN §5: Act II opens into hubs. Act I was one long corridor. Act II is a loop with the capital at its far side: north over Kithairon to Thyrsa, west under Parnassos to the Gulf, south through the Arkadian mountains, back east through Nemea to the Isthmus, and along the road of the Mysteries to Astyra, the hub, whose spokes run to its harbor, to Marathon and to Sounion. Then a voyage through the Cyclades to Kaldera. With the Conch at the end of the act, the whole Aegean opens: every painted island can be visited. The user's brief holds throughout: "it should feel like we are traveling farther". Every stretch between laurels is two or three routes with a waypoint between them.

**The chains**
- **The Kithairon crossing:** Eleusa Village → Route 6, the Eleutherai Road → **Mt. Kithairon** (the border fort of Eleutherai at its foot, then the maenads' pass) → Route 7, down past the Kronia grounds → Thyrsa City.
- **The road west:** Thyrsa City → Route 8, the Kopais Shore → **Lebadeia**, the oracle of Trophonios (optional cave below) → Route 9, the Split Road → **Kirrha**, Delphoi's harbor → Route 10, the Gulf ferry → **Aigion**.
- **The Arkadian climb:** Aigion → Route 11, the Krathis Gorge (the drums: the Girdle) → **Styx Falls**, with the village of Nonakris → Route 12, the cypress road over Kyllene's shoulder → Arkadia → the Cypress Wood → the Pool of Mnemosyne.
- **Back to the Isthmus:** Arkadia → Route 13, down out of the highlands → **Nemea** → Route 14 → Emporion City.
- **The road of the Mysteries:** Emporion → Act I's Route 4, Hecate's Hollow and Route 5 → Eleusa → Route 15, the road of the Mysteries (closed since Act I): the Rheitoi salt lakes, the jesters' bridge and the hamlet of **Thria**, all moved here from Phase 2 → **Daphni**, Apollo's laurel grove → Route 16, over the pass → Astyra's Kerameikos and the Dipylon.
- **Astyra's spokes:** the Kerameikos (west, the arrival), the Akropolis (above), the salt well (under the Akropolis), Phaleron (south-west, the harbor). Optional: Route 17 to **Marathon** (north-east) and Route 18 down the coast past the salt hamlet of **Halai** and its cliffs (moved here from Phase 2) to **Cape Sounion** (south-east).
- **The voyage:** Phaleron → the *Paralos*, round Sounion on Route 3 and east on Route 2 → **Delos** → past Kalliste at night → Route 19, home waters → Kaldera's old port → the caldera road → Kaldera → the Telchines' forge → Nea Kameni.
- **Optional, on foot:** Thyrsa's east gate → the Teumessos Road → **Aulis** → the Euripus bridge (a tide gate) → **Chalkis**, on **Euboia** → the Lelantine Road → **Amarynthos**.
- **Optional, with Poseidon's Conch** (AETHOS_MAP: "the Conch opens ten islands at once", tuned for Act III): **Paros** beside Route 19; Route 20, the north Aegean from Marathon (**Skyros**, **Lemnos**, **Samothrake**); Route 21, the east Aegean from Akti (**Ikaria**, **Samos**, **Chios**, **Lesbos**). **Delos** stays open after the voyage.
- **Optional, by ferry:** **Aigina's interior** (the Aphaia Road, the Temple of Aphaia and Mount Oros), moved here from Phase 2's Act I detour. From beat 46 Nausikles's ferry stops at Aigina Town and its north gate opens (`FLAG_ICHOR_FERRY_TO_AEGINA`).
- **Detours, optional:** Eleusa's Maiden's Well (Demeter's theoxenia, after Laurel 5); Elaia (the empty house, after the letter).
- **Onward:** Kaldera's harbor → Route 22 past Melos to Kythera (Act III). Arkadia's south road → Route 27 to Lake Stymphalia (Act III, closed). Kirrha's north road → Route 28 to Delphoi (Act III, the Horn). Arkadia's west road → Route 32 to Olympia (post-game).

**Real geography behind it.**
- Eleusis to Thebes crossed Kithairon by the fort of Eleutherai, the home of Dionysus Eleuthereus, whose wooden image was carried to Athens for the first Dionysia. Kithairon is the mountain of Euripides's *Bacchae*, of Aktaion, and of the baby Oedipus.
- Thebes had seven gates. Its Kadmeia was the citadel of Kadmos, and Dionysus was born there to Kadmos's daughter Semele. East of it, the Euripus strait to Euboia reverses its current through the day; Aulis on its shore is where the Greek fleet waited for a wind.
- West of Thebes lay Lake Kopais, a marsh lake the Minyans drained with dikes, and Lebadeia, where pilgrims went down into the earth to consult Trophonios after drinking from the springs of Lethe and Mnemosyne. Beyond it, under Parnassos, the Schiste, the split road where three ways meet, where Oedipus killed Laius.
- Kirrha was Delphoi's harbor on the Krisaian gulf. Across the gulf of Korinthos, Aigion was an Achaean port. South of it the Krathis gorge climbs into the Aroania mountains, where the Styx falls down a black cliff above the village of Nonakris. Arkadia beyond is the Peloponnese's mountain heart: Pan's country, Kallisto's and Lykaon's.
- Out of Arkadia the road drops toward Argos and Nemea, where Herakles strangled the lion and the Nemean Games were held at Zeus's temple. Corinth sits on the Isthmus beyond.
- The real Sacred Way ran from Athens to Eleusis by the Rheitoi salt lakes and over Mount Aigaleos at Daphni, where a laurel grove gave the place its name. It entered Athens through the Kerameikos, the potters' quarter and cemetery, at the Dipylon. Phaleron was Athens's old harbor. The *Paralos* was Athens's sacred trireme, which carried the city's embassies to Delos; while it was away, no one in Athens could be put to death.
- Marathon's burial mound covers the Athenians who fell in the battle; Cape Sounion's temple of Poseidon stands where Aegeus watched for his son's sail.
- Delos was Apollo's and Artemis's birthplace. After its purification no one was allowed to be born or to die on it. Theseus danced the crane dance there, round the altar of horns, after the Labyrinth.
- Thera is a drowned volcano: a ring of cliffs round a lagoon, with the black islet of Nea Kameni in the middle. The Telchines were the first smiths, sea-daemons of the islands.

## Pacing and levels

About 6 hours on a first run, against Phase 2's 3, because Act II has three laurels, the capital and the midpoint. The optional lands (Euboia, Marathon, Sounion, Trophonios's cave, Paros and the open Aegean) add two to three hours, most of it in Act III's levels.

Levels follow `design/BALANCE.md`. Each stage starts near the previous boss's ace minus 4, no map's wild band is wider than 5, the bands rise along the road, and no wild Pokémon appears evolved below its evolution level (BALANCE.md, 2026-11-14). The rows used:
- **Thyrsa** (wild 21–28, trainers 24–30, Thespis 30–32): Route 6, Mt. Kithairon, Route 7, Thyrsa.
- **Arkadia** (wild 26–33, trainers 30–35, Kallisto 35–37): Routes 8–12 and their waypoints, the ferry, Arkadia. Euboia, optional, is tuned here too.
- **Astyra** (wild 30–36, trainers 33–38, Kleon 38–40): Routes 13–16, Nemea, Daphni, Astyra and its spokes, the salt well; Routes 17–18, Marathon and Sounion, optional.
- **Kaldera** (wild 34–40, trainers 37–42, Talos 41–43): the voyage, Delos, Route 19, Paros, Kaldera, the forge, Nea Kameni.
- **The open Aegean** (Routes 20–21 and their islands, optional): tuned for Act III, as AETHOS_MAP says, at wild 38–44 and trainers 40–45.

Ichor's curve is steeper, by BALANCE.md's design: the main fully-evolved forms arrive in Laurels 4–6, and the post-game sits higher still. Hyperion's ace sits one level above Kaldera's boss band because he fights after the Forge Laurel, as he fought after Chloe's in Phase 2; Silenos's 35 sits above Thespis because his battle is one of three contests and the other two need no battle at all (Open questions 6).

**Evolved forms from Astyra on** (BALANCE.md, the director's ruling): lines whose evolution level sits below the area's band appear evolved, at the band's levels. Their first stages turn up only at small, lower-level spots the dex names: Obolorn at the Kerameikos's paupers' graves (night, 28), Kaminoo in Kaldera's warm hollow (31). Glaukoin, Telpup and Kapnub are at the edge of their bands and are capped instead (dex DECISIONS).

# Part 1. Scenes, beats 26–67

The beats run in story order. Each region's maps and households are in Part 2, its trainers in Part 3, its encounters in Part 4, its rites and dungeons in Part 5.

## Beat 26. The Eleutherai Road: the vines, and the herald

Per STORY.md §3, Act II item II-1 (the road), and Phase 2 beat 25's close.

**Setup.** Phase 2 left the vines on `MAP_ROUTE6_ELEUTHERAI_ROAD`'s south end, with Alethea waiting beside them ("ALETHEA: Ready when you are. Truthfully, I've been ready since breakfast."), and a herald's barrier across the road beyond. The player may already have cut the vines at the end of Act I. If not, the relic prompt (per SYSTEMS.md §1, ASK by default):
```text
A wall of old vines, thick as rope, grown right across the road.

Cut them with Demeter's Sickle?
```
?? YES/NO
```text
> YES:
{PLAYER} cut the vines with Demeter's Sickle.

> NO:
The vines stay where they are. They look pleased about it.
```
[YES: set `FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_ELEUTHERAI_VINES` (Phase 2's flag). The vine metatiles swap to cut stumps.]

**The herald.** A coord trigger two tiles south of the barrier runs once, with `FLAG_ICHOR_ACT1_COMPLETE` set and `FLAG_ICHOR_ACT2_BEGUN` unset. The herald stands behind his pole with a horn. Alethea walks up from the vines and stops beside the player.

[The herald blows his horn. A long, cracked note. A Lophops flies out of the vines in disgust.]
```text
HERALD: Hear me! Hear me, road! Hear me, vines!

HERALD: The Dionysia begins in Thyrsa! The god comes home to his city!

HERALD: The play is ready! Every road to Thyrsa is open!

HERALD: Go up, go up, and bring a cup!
```
[He lifts the barrier pole and shoulders it like an oar.]
```text
HERALD: You two. Thyrsa's over the mountain. Two days' walk.

HERALD: One, if you're Lakonian. One went by yesterday at a dead run.

ALETHEA: Kleon. Of course.

ALETHEA: Truthfully, I'm relieved. I thought he'd broken his neck on the vines.

HERALD: There's a new play this year, they say. Nobody knows who wrote it.

HERALD: A tragedy. Thyrsa loves a tragedy. Then it loves the satyrs more.
```
[He walks off south toward Eleusa. From offscreen: "HERALD: The god comes home! Bring a cup!" Hide him; set `FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_HERALD_BARRIER`.]
```text
ALETHEA: A new play by nobody. My favorite kind of mystery.

ALETHEA: I'll walk with you as far as Thyrsa. I want to dig in the Kadmeia.

ALETHEA: Kadmos's own city. They say his house is still under it. Somewhere.

ALETHEA: I'll go ahead and read the stones. I read slower than you walk.
```
[Alethea walks north and is hidden (`FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_ALETHEA_ROUTE6`). Set `FLAG_ICHOR_ACT2_BEGUN`.]

**Design note.** The herald replaces Phase 2's barrier line ("The road opens when the play's ready"), so Act I's build and Act II's join without a seam. Alethea walking ahead is how she "travels with" the player through region A: she is shown at Eleutherai's plinth, at the Kronia's tables, on the Kadmeia and in the theater, and nowhere between.

## Beat 27. Eleutherai: the plinth of the god who left

**Setup.** The first step into `MAP_ELEUTHERAI` sets `FLAG_ICHOR_VISITED_ELEUTHERAI`. The fort stands on its rock above the road, all towers and old walls. Below it, beside the road, is the god's old temple: roofless, swept, with a stone plinth and nothing on it. Alethea stands at the plinth. Oinoe, an old woman with a broom, sweeps the step. Talking to Alethea runs the scene once.

[The plinth, as an object:]
```text
A stone plinth, swept clean. Nothing stands on it.

Cut into the front: DIONYSOS ELEUTHEREUS. HE WHO SETS FREE.
```
```text
ALETHEA: The god's statue stood here. Wood, very old. A face like a happy dog.

ALETHEA: Thyrsa borrowed it for the first Dionysia. To carry in the procession.

ALETHEA: That was three hundred years ago. They never brought it back.

OINOE: They will. When he's ready.

OINOE: I sweep his step every morning. My mother did. Her mother did.

OINOE: A god likes to come home to a clean step.

ALETHEA: In three hundred years, has anyone asked Thyrsa to return it?

OINOE: Ask a god to come home? You don't ask. You sweep.
```
[Oinoe goes back to sweeping. Alethea turns to the player.]
```text
ALETHEA: “He who sets free.” Eleutherai means free. Did you know?

ALETHEA: A free town, with an empty plinth. I like that more than I should.

ALETHEA: I'll see you at the camp below Thyrsa. The herald says you can't miss it.

ALETHEA: You can smell it from the pass, apparently.
```
[Alethea walks north and is hidden (`FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_ALETHEA_ELEUTHERAI`).]

Oinoe's garland errand, the fort's cook and the twins are in Part 2 (Eleutherai).

## Beat 28. Kithairon: the mountain of the Bacchae

Mt. Kithairon's pass (`MAP_MT_KITHAIRON`) has no single cutscene. It has three places that each tell a story when the player stops: the maenads' dancing floor, Pentheus's fir and Aktaion's spring (Part 2), and the shepherds' fold, which is the route's rest point and its set piece.

**The dancing floor.** A coord trigger at the glade's edge, once (`FLAG_ICHOR_SAW_MAENADS`). Drums. Five maenads dance in a ring on the trampled grass, fawnskins over their shoulders, ivy in their hair. Two Botrykit circle with them. [Movement scripts: the ring turns twice. A drum SE on each beat.]
```text
MAENAD: Euoi! Euoi! The god is coming down the mountain!

MAENAD: Dance, stranger! Nobody on Kithairon walks. We run, or we dance.
```
[The ring breaks and scatters into the firs, laughing. Euia and Bromia stay (Part 3).]

**The shepherds' fold.** A stone fold at the top of the pass, a spring trough and a lean-to. Phorbas, an old shepherd, sits on the wall. Talking to him the first time plays this; afterward he only heals.
```text
PHORBAS: Sit. Kithairon's long. My fold's the halfway.

PHORBAS: Here. Milk, warm from the ewe. Your Pokémon too.
```
[Heal the party, with the heal jingle.]
```text
PHORBAS: My grandfather's grandfather kept this fold. Summer pasture.

PHORBAS: The Thyrsa flocks came up this side. The Korinthos flocks, the other.

PHORBAS: Two shepherds, one spring. They got on.

PHORBAS: One summer the Thyrsa shepherd came up with a baby in his cloak.

PHORBAS: Feet pinned together. King's orders. Leave it on the mountain.

PHORBAS: There'd been a prophecy. The child would kill its father.

PHORBAS: He couldn't do it. So he gave the baby to the Korinthos shepherd.

PHORBAS: The boy grew up a prince over there. Then he heard the prophecy too.

PHORBAS: So he ran. As far from Korinthos as his legs would go.

PHORBAS: Met an old man at a crossroads, under Parnassos. They argued about the road.

PHORBAS: You know the rest. Everyone does.
```
?? I DON'T / GO ON
```text
> I DON'T:
PHORBAS: Then I won't spoil it. Ask at the split road, west of Thyrsa.

PHORBAS: They'll show you the stone.

> GO ON:
PHORBAS: He ran from his fate, and straight into it.

PHORBAS: Ran from the one place it couldn't happen, to the one place it could.

PHORBAS: My grandfather said that's what prophecies are for. Making people run.
```
[Set `FLAG_ICHOR_PHORBAS_STORY`.] Afterward:
```text
PHORBAS: Sit a while. Milk's free. Prophecies, I don't do.
```
[He heals the party each time.]

**Design notes.**
- Oedipus is a hindsight seed for STORY.md's second twist (a father makes a prophecy true by fleeing it). It names no one in the story and has no daughter in it; the player should only remember it at the Frozen Hour.
- "Ask at the split road" points to Route 9, the crossroads under Parnassos, where region B1 can show the stone.

## Beat 29. The Kronia grounds: the feast that never closes

Per STORY.md §3, II-1, and §5 (the Kronia grounds: Titans, public face 2, "a movement, not a gang").

**What the player sees.** Route 7's lower half (`MAP_ROUTE7_KRONIA_GROUNDS`) is the Asopos meadow below Thyrsa's Elektran Gate, at the foot of Kithairon's north face. The road runs straight through the middle of the camp: long trestle tables under awnings, a great domed bread oven, tents in a ring, a raised wooden stage hung with gold cloth, children running, a Kronist speaking from the stage, and over everything a huge painted banner. The smell reaches the top of the pass. Play `MUS_ICHOR_KRONIA`: warm, golden, unmistakably lovely.

[The banner, as an object:]
```text
A painted banner: a golden field, people dancing, no one old.

In the corner, a water clock lies smashed, its water running into the grass.

```

**The greeting.** A coord trigger at the camp's south edge, at the foot of the mountain, once. A Kronist in a plain tunic, with a sickle pin and a smiling clay half-mask, steps into the road with a basket of bread.



**Design notes.**
- The camp must feel good. Everyone in it is happy, fed and kind, and nobody battles the player unless the player asks (Part 2, the tables). The only cold note is the reader.
- Kleon refuses a reading here, so that taking Iapetos's in Arkadia (beat 42) is a fall, not a habit.
- The reader recognizing "Elaia's island" is how the play's knowledge of the hero gets a face, without saying who wrote it.

## Beat 30. Thyrsa: the city of seven gates

**Setup.** The first step through the Elektran Gate sets `FLAG_ICHOR_ARRIVED_THYRSA` and `FLAG_ICHOR_VISITED_THYRSA` (fly). Ivy hangs from every wall. Festival garlands cross the street. The gatekeeper, an old man with a staff wound in ivy, steps out of the gatehouse.
```text
GATEKEEPER: Seven gates, stranger, and you came in by the Elektran. Good choice.

GATEKEEPER: It's the one with the bread smell. Thanks to that lot outside.

GATEKEEPER: Asclepeion's by the spring, there. The Agora's under the awnings.

GATEKEEPER: The theater's on the east hill. The god's temple is right at the top.

GATEKEEPER: Thespis is our Hierophant. The Masked Player.

GATEKEEPER: Though he's short of masks this week. Somebody robbed the skene.

GATEKEEPER: Every mask in the place. Three nights ago. Right before the festival.

GATEKEEPER: Play's going on anyway. Thyrsa doesn't cancel a Dionysia.

GATEKEEPER: West gate's shut till it's over. By the god's order.

GATEKEEPER: Everyone stays for the play. Even the people who'd rather not.
```

**Manto on the wall.** Manto, a very old blind woman, sits on a stool on the Kadmeia's wall walk, head tilted to the sky. She is Thyrsa's augur (per SYSTEMS.md §6: the daily omen, in Part 2). The first time the player talks to her:
```text
MANTO: Footsteps. Small ones. And a Pokémon walking proud beside them.

MANTO: Come here, child. I'm blind. I'm not rude.

MANTO: My great-great-grandfather was Teiresias.

MANTO: Blind as a stone, and saw everything.

MANTO: I've been blind sixty years. Lately I'm blind in the other way too.

MANTO: The birds still fly. I listen to them. They've started flying the wrong way.
```
[She turns her face toward the player. Hold 60 frames.]
```text
MANTO: …Hm. You're there. I can hear you breathing.

MANTO: But when I listen for what comes after you, there's nothing.

MANTO: Like a doorway with no room behind it.

MANTO: Don't fret. Most days I can't hear what comes after my own breakfast.
```
[Set `FLAG_ICHOR_MET_MANTO`. Then the day's omen, as Part 2.]

**Alethea on the Kadmeia.** Until `FLAG_ICHOR_ALETHEA_WENT_WEST`, Alethea kneels by Semele's chamber with a trowel.
```text
ALETHEA: Semele's chamber. Zeus came to her as lightning. She didn't survive it.

ALETHEA: The baby did. That was Dionysus. And the room's been smoking ever since.

ALETHEA: Truthfully, it's probably a hot spring. Don't tell the priests I said so.
```
If the player carries an unread prophecy tablet, she reads it (tablet #3 below; the others are their regions' text).

**Tablet #3, the soldier of Thyrsa** (per SYSTEMS.md §5's table). It is a fixed dig under the fig tree in Eudora's courtyard (Part 2). Alethea's reading, wherever she reads it:
```text
ALETHEA: A lead tablet. People scratch their questions on these, for the Oracle.

ALETHEA: “Hippias, son of Eudora, soldier of Thyrsa. Will I come home?”

ALETHEA: And the answer, over it: “You'll die in the next war.”

ALETHEA: …Tilt it to the light. See the scratches underneath?

ALETHEA: Someone scraped the first answer off and wrote a new one. Neatly.

ALETHEA: The old one says: “You'll come home from the next war.”

ALETHEA: And at the end of the new one, a little hook.

ALETHEA: Another one for my list. Truthfully, I'm not enjoying this list.
```

## Beat 32. The Dionysia: *The Unwoven*

Per STORY.md §3, II-3, and the set piece, §6.3, whose staging this follows to the letter.

**Setup.** Entering `MAP_THYRSA_THEATER` with `FLAG_BADGE04_GET` set and `FLAG_ICHOR_DIONYSIA_DONE` unset. Before the laurel, the theater's gatekeeper turns the player away: "THEATER KEEPER: Seats open for the play, and not before. Win your laurel. The Masked Player likes his audience educated." Set `FLAG_ICHOR_DIONYSIA_BEGUN`.

The scene doesn't read the clock: the torches round the orchestra are lit metatiles and the sky layer is drawn at dusk, whatever the hour.

**The theater.**
- **The audience** is drawn into the seating metatiles: every tier is full, in six blocks of seats. A slow purple palette pulse runs on the audience tiles once the trance begins (per §6.3; one palette, cycled by the expansion's palette animation).
- **On stage,** as objects: the actor in a petasos and a traveler's cloak, carrying a sickle (Borboros, a Titanborn); the bee-woman, veiled, with a clay jar; the three Fates in black-figure costume, as three objects; the gold-masked king, kneeling; and the CHORUS LEADER in a white tragic mask. His right hand is black with ink to the wrist.
- **In the seats:** the player and Alethea on the lowest tier, center, with the program in Alethea's lap; Kleon in the front row to the left, a fixed object. A herald in the orchestra opens the play.
- Seven objects on stage, three in the seats, the herald: eleven. Thespis and Silenos appear later, in the skene.

[Fade in. The crowd's noise as an SE. The herald raps his staff.]
```text

```
[The god's procession leaves the theater; that night its cart drops a drum in the Neistan Gate (Part 2). Thespis returns to his temple. Silenos's contest opens in the skene (beat 34). Prosomime now appear backstage in the evening and at night (Part 4).]

**Music** (per STORY.md §6.3): the tragedy is the Titan theme slowed into a Phrygian processional. The trance cuts the instant the first laugh lands. The satyr play is a fast 9/8 aulos romp, from the third entrance to the battle.

**Design notes.**
- The play lies about two things, on purpose: the bee-woman *stole* a thread, and the gods *cursed* her child. It never says why the hero has no thread. It names no one, and the gold-masked king has no name and no face.
- "Hid it under a tree" and "the edge of the sea" are true. That is how a good lie is built, and it pays off at Delphoi.
- The masks can't find the player, as the gods in the play can't. Nobody explains why.
- The honey jar on stage is the prop the bee-woman carries; Silenos drinking from it is the joke that breaks the spell. In hindsight it is Mom's jar.
- The CHORUS LEADER is never named in Thyrsa. He has the white tragic mask and the ink-dark hand that region B2's Iapetos has in Arkadia.

## Beat 33. Kleon's third battle: the empty theater

**Setup.** After `FLAG_ICHOR_DIONYSIA_DONE`, the next time the player enters the theater. Everyone has gone. The torches are guttering. Kleon sits on the edge of the stage with the petasos actor's hat in his hands, turning it round and round. Approaching him runs the scene. Play no music until the battle.
```text
KLEON: Did you like it? Your play?

KLEON: Four scenes. A chorus. A gold mask crying over you. Very moving.

KLEON: Before the trance, I turned round. Did you see? I turned round.

KLEON: I wanted to see if you knew. You didn't. You looked like a goat in a storm.

KLEON: The whole of Aethos sat in those seats looking at you.

KLEON: Nobody's ever put me on a stage. I've been trying since I was seven.

KLEON: I asked Pindaros for an ode. The poet. He writes them for winners.

KLEON: He said he doesn't write in advance.

KLEON: In advance! I've got a prophecy! It's all in advance!
```
[He drops the hat and stands.]
```text
KLEON: Battle me. Here. Where the stage was.

KLEON: If anyone's left in the seats, they can watch this instead.
```
[Set `FLAG_ICHOR_NO_WHITEOUT`. Battle `TRAINER_ICHOR_KLEON_3_<STARTER>`, chosen by `VAR_STARTER_MON` (Part 3). Clear the flag afterwards. Defeat text: "KLEON: No. Not here. Not on a stage." Win text: "KLEON: Ha! There! Somebody write that down!"]

[After a win by the player (`FLAG_ICHOR_WON_KLEON_3`):]
```text
KLEON: …Fine. You're the hero of the play.

KLEON: I'm the friend. The one who loses in the second act so you look good.
```
[After a loss:]
```text
KLEON: See? Nothing in my reading about you. Not a word.

KLEON: …It didn't feel like anything. Winning. Isn't that odd.
```
[Either way:]
```text
KLEON: There's a Huntress in Arkadia. Kallisto. Nobody's beaten her this month.

KLEON: Not one trainer. Not one.

KLEON: If I beat her, someone'll write it down. Even Pindaros.

KLEON: Don't follow me. You'll only get a play about that too.
```
[He walks up the cavea steps and out of the top gate. Hide him (`FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_KLEON_THEATER`). Set `FLAG_ICHOR_KLEON_BATTLE_3_DONE`.]

**Design notes.**
- "Don't follow me" here is what makes STORY.md §7.2's "Don't follow me. I mean it this time." land in Arkadia.
- Kleon keeps every one of §7.2's lines for Arkadia: nothing here says "a story about you" or "one that's mine". This scene is the crack; Arkadia is the break.
- He is about to walk into the one trainer in Aethos whose fate has been rewritten to break him (STORY.md §2, Kallisto). Nobody here knows that.

## Beat 34. Silenos's contest: the Girdle of Herakles

Per SYSTEMS.md §1, myth-quest 5, "Herakles Lost a Drinking Game".

**Setup.** After `FLAG_ICHOR_DIONYSIA_DONE`, Silenos sits on a costume chest in the skene's prop room, in front of a great leather girdle studded with bronze, hanging on a peg. He is bald, round, red-nosed and very old, with a wineskin he never puts down. The first time:
```text
SILENOS: Ah! The goat-door hero. Sit. Mind the lion. It's a costume. Mostly.

SILENOS: You want the belt. Everyone who sees it wants the belt.

SILENOS: Herakles's own. He bet it on a drinking match with the god himself.

SILENOS: Herakles drank a river. The god drank the sea. Herakles lost.

SILENOS: Lost his shirt too, but that's another play.

SILENOS: I've kept it since. I keep everything. Ask the actors.

SILENOS: Win it off me. Two out of three. Bones, a riddle, or a fight.

SILENOS: Pick one. Lose, and pick again. I've nowhere to be. Ever.
```

[Each contest won is removed from the menu. `FLAG_ICHOR_SILENOS_WON_BONES`, `_RIDDLE`, `_FIGHT`.]

**Bones** (per SYSTEMS.md §9, Silenos's personality). His bones are loaded: a 6 comes up 30% of the time. After he throws two 6s or more in each of two throws running, a fifth choice, LOADED!, appears in the throw menu. Calling it wins the match at once.

```text
SILENOS: My bones. Old and lucky. Don't look at them too closely.

> LOADED!:
SILENOS: …Ha! Ha ha! You caught me! Nobody catches me!

SILENOS: Your point. Fair's fair. Well. Unfair's unfair.

> a fair win:
SILENOS: Beat loaded bones, fair and square? The god's looking after you.

> a loss:
SILENOS: The bones love me. They always have. Again?
```
**A riddle.** Three tries, and a new riddle after each miss, per SYSTEMS.md.
```text

SILENOS: She sat on a rock outside this city and ate everyone who got it wrong.

SILENOS: I just take your belt. Much nicer.
```

|---|---|---|---|

| 2 | "The more of me you take, the more of me you leave behind." | WINE / YEARS / FOOTSTEPS / BREAD | FOOTSTEPS |
| 3 | "What gets wetter, the more it dries?" | THE SEA / A TOWEL / SILENOS / THE SUN | A TOWEL |

```text
SILENOS: Ha! Clever thing. Your point.

> wrong, with tries left:
SILENOS: Wrong! Have another. I've hundreds. Mostly about wine.

> three wrong:
SILENOS: Three wrong! Come back when you're sober. I mean when I am.
```
[A loss resets to riddle 1.]

**A fight.**
```text

```
[Battle `TRAINER_ICHOR_SILENOS`. Defeat text:]
```text

```
**The second win.**
```text

SILENOS: Herakles won't mind. He's a constellation now. Very hard to reach.
```
[He lifts the girdle off its peg and buckles it round the player. It is far too big. Then it isn't.]
```text
{PLAYER} received the Girdle of Herakles!

SILENOS: Put your back into a thing with that on, and the thing moves.

SILENOS: Fallen drums, old columns. Thyrsa's full of them. So's the road west.

SILENOS: There's one in the west gate right now, I hear. The god's cart.

SILENOS: He drives like he drinks.
```
[Set `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_GIRDLE`.]

```text
SILENOS: And take this, will you? It's pinned to the crane.
```
[He unpins a sheet of old, finely ruled parchment from the god-machine's arm. It is a drawing of the crane itself, with notes in a tiny, crabbed hand.]
```text

{PLAYER} received Daedalus's page III!
```
[Set `FLAG_ICHOR_DAEDALUS_PAGE_3` (LABYRINTH.md, the pages table: page III).]
```text

SILENOS: Asked if it was true, what they say I said once. To King Midas.

SILENOS: “Best of all is never to be born. Second best is to die young.”

SILENOS: I told him I was drunk when I said it. He didn't laugh.

SILENOS: Odd boy. Most people laugh.
```


**Alethea goes west.** When the player has pushed the gate's drum aside (`FLAG_ICHOR_NEISTAN_DRUM_MOVED`, Part 2), Alethea runs up under the arch, once (`FLAG_ICHOR_ALETHEA_WENT_WEST` unset).
```text
ALETHEA: You moved it! Six guards and a donkey couldn't. I watched.

ALETHEA: The gate's open. The whole city's going home.

ALETHEA: Nobody's talking about anything but the play.
```

**Design notes.**
- The Girdle is the main-path gate twice. Here, the drum in the Neistan Gate is its first use, in a safe place. Beyond the gulf, the column drums on Route 11 (the revised map) block the way into Arkadia. Nobody leaves Thyrsa westward without it, so the order Laurel → the Dionysia → Silenos → the west gate is fixed by flags.
- Silenos's "best is never to be born" is the old wisdom of Silenus (he told it to Midas). Kleon asking about it is the reason his Arkadia scene doesn't come from nowhere.
- Silenos's battle is 33–35, above Thespis. It's one of three contests, and the other two need no battle (front matter, Pacing).

## Beat 35. The Kopais and Lebadeia: the oracle in the earth

### 35A. Route 8: a trail of holes

**Setup.** Thyrsa's Neistan Gate opens once the player holds the Girdle of Herakles (`FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_GIRDLE`, beat 34), so everyone who reaches Route 8 has it. Alethea went ahead after the Dionysia to dig along the lake road, and left a trail: five notes pinned to reeds along the road, a running joke that leads west. Notes 1 and 2 stand beside two of the route's daily dig spots, already dug and flattened when the player first arrives; they work as ordinary daily spots from the next day (SYSTEMS.md §5). Notes 3 to 5 are only notes. They read in order, east to west:
```text
[1, by the east sign]
A neat hole, filled back in. A note is pinned to a reed.

“DUG HERE. A BUTTON. NOT EVEN A NICE ONE. -A”

[2, on the dike]
“DUG HERE. AN EEL. IT BIT ME. I PUT IT BACK. -A”

[3, at the foot of the Sphinx's rocks]
“DID NOT DIG HERE. A SIGN SAYS A SPHINX LIVES UP THERE.

I DON'T ANSWER RIDDLES. I DIG UNDER THEM. -A”

[4, by the lake islet, across the water]
“CAN'T REACH THE ISLAND. THERE'S A WALL ON IT. OLD. YOU TRY. -A”

[5, at the west sign]
“LEBADEIA. WAITING AT THE SPRINGS. BRING BREAD. -A”
```
[Note 4 points at the islet of Gla, a Conch gate (Part 2). Set `FLAG_ICHOR_READ_ALETHEA_NOTES` on note 5; it changes one line of hers in 35B.]

**Design note.** The notes keep Alethea in the act while she is off the map, and they teach the player that the islet is worth coming back for.

### 35B. Lebadeia: between the two springs

**Setup.** The first time the player enters `MAP_LEBADEIA` with `FLAG_ICHOR_VISITED_LEBADEIA` unset, an `ON_FRAME` script runs. Set `FLAG_ICHOR_VISITED_LEBADEIA` (`MAPSEC_LEBADEIA`; a healer hamlet and fly target). The precinct is at the west end of the hamlet: two springs side by side under a rock face, one dark and still (Lethe), one bright and running (Mnemosyne), a stone chair between them, and the cave mouth behind a bronze grille. Alethea sits on the rim of the bright spring with her satchel open. Pilgrims in white sit in a row on the steps, wrapped in blankets.

[The camera pans from the hamlet's gate to the springs and back. Alethea stands and waves.]
```text
ALETHEA: There you are! Did you bring bread?

> with FLAG_ICHOR_READ_ALETHEA_NOTES:
ALETHEA: You read my notes. Good. The eel was a bad day.

> without:

ALETHEA: This is Lebadeia. The oracle of Trophonios.

ALETHEA: You don't ask him a question. You go down and find out.

ALETHEA: Into the earth. On your back. Feet first, through a hole.

ALETHEA: Truthfully, it's the least dignified oracle in Aethos.
```
[She turns to the springs.]
```text
ALETHEA: First you drink from that one. Lethe. Forgetting.

ALETHEA: So you go down empty. Nothing you know gets in the way.

ALETHEA: Then that one. Mnemosyne. Memory.

ALETHEA: So you remember whatever you find down there.

ALETHEA: My name comes from this, you know. A-letheia.

ALETHEA: Not-forgetting. That's all truth is, really. Not forgetting.
```
[Hold 30 frames. She looks at the dark spring.]
```text
ALETHEA: I'm not drinking from Lethe. Not even a sip.

ALETHEA: …Some days I'd like to. Truthfully. Then I'd be wrong about things.

ALETHEA: People like you better when you're wrong about things.

ALETHEA: Anyway! Look at them.
```
[She nods at the pilgrims on the steps.]
```text
ALETHEA: Every one of them went down this week.

ALETHEA: And every one came up saying the same thing.

ALETHEA: The priests won't tell me what. Go and ask. They might tell you.
```
[Alethea waits by the springs until the player leaves Lebadeia westward (beat 36A).]

**The pilgrims on the steps.** Each is one object; the three say it in their own words:
```text

FARMER: I came up and said, “The cloth runs out.” I don't know why I said it.

SAILOR: Asked about a voyage. Came up saying the cloth runs out.

SAILOR: I'm a sailor. I don't even own any cloth.

OLD WOMAN: I've been sitting here two days, waiting to understand it.
```

**Saon, the eldest priest,** stands at the grille. He is named for the man who found the oracle by following a swarm of bees into the rock.

```text
SAON: Everyone who goes down this month comes up with the same words.

SAON: Farmers. Sailors. A goat, nearly. It got as far as the hole.

SAON: “The cloth runs out.” We don't know what it means.

SAON: So we do what priests do. We write it down.

SAON: Would you go down? Trophonios will see you. He sees everyone.
```

```text
SAON: Take this. For the snakes below. They prefer it to pilgrims.
```

[Give `ITEM_HONEY` ×1 if the player has none. Saon unlocks the grille: `FLAG_ICHOR_TROPHONIOS_GRILLE_OPEN`. The descent is the optional dungeon, `MAP_TROPHONIOS_CAVE_B1F` (Part 5). Saying NO leaves the grille open to come back.]

### 35C. The throne of Mnemosyne

**Setup.** When the player reaches the oracle's chamber at the bottom of B2F (Part 5) and answers YES at the hole in its floor, fade to black. No music. Hold 120 frames of black with no text. Then warp the player to the stone chair between the springs, facing south, with Saon, a second priest and Alethea in front of it. Set `FLAG_ICHOR_TROPHONIOS_READING`.
```text
SAON: Sit. Don't stand yet. Everyone falls over.

SAON: You were down there a long time.

SAON: Now. What did you see? What did he say?
```
[Hold 60 frames. The player's sprite turns left, then right, as at the Klotheia.]
```text
SAON: …Nothing?

SAON: No cloth? No voice? Not even the snakes?
```
[The two priests look at each other. They turn back. Neither speaks for 60 frames.]

```text
SAON: Write it down.

PRIEST: Write what?

```
[The priests walk back to the grille.]
```text
ALETHEA: Everyone else came up with the same four words. You came up with none.
```

**Design notes.**
- No reading of the player succeeds (STORY.md, Act II's rules). Halia saw nothing; Trophonios says nothing. The priests' silence is the scene, and nobody explains it.
- The descent is optional. A player who skips it misses the scene but nothing else; the cloth line is already on the steps.
- The spring of Mnemosyne is a quiet seed for Arkadia's Pool (beat 41), where the memory of Aethos is kept. Nobody says so.

### 36A. Where three roads meet

**Setup.** The first time the player steps onto the crossroads tile with `FLAG_ICHOR_SCHISTE_ARRIVED` unset. The crossroads is a paved triangle with an old boundary stone in the middle and the great herm beside it. North-west, a goat path climbs the flank of Parnassos toward two great cliffs, to a lookout. South-west, the road drops toward the sea and the far shore of the gulf. East, the way back to Lebadeia.

```text
ALETHEA: Kleon will have gone that way. To the ferry. Arkadia's across the water.

ALETHEA: The road up to Delphoi starts at Kirrha. This path only goes to a lookout.
```

[The player is free. The north-west fork is optional and ends at a lookout (36B), with no way on. The south-west road is the main path, down to Kirrha; a side path off it climbs to the treasury ruin (36C, optional).]

**Setup.** At the end of the north-west fork, `MAP_ROUTE9_SCHISTE`'s top corner: a dead end, with no map connection. The goat path ends on a ledge with a stone bench, a cairn of pilgrims' stones, and a sheer drop into a ravine. Across the ravine and high above, Delphoi's two cliffs, the sanctuary's roofs between them, and the Kastalian falls coming down their gorge. Xenodike, a pilgrim, sits on the bench with a bundle (her household quest is in Part 2). A visible Max Revive lies at the ledge's tip, past the bench. The first time the player reaches the bench, Alethea walks up beside them.

```text
ALETHEA: Nobody's sacrificing. Nobody's asking anything.

ALETHEA: Truthfully, it looks like a house where everyone's holding their breath.
```
**The falls** (a bg event at the ledge's edge; the Horn of Achelous, Act III):
```text
High above, the Kastalian spring falls down its gorge in a white rope of water.

A path climbs beside it from the valley below Kirrha, toward the temple.
```
**The cairn**

[The Max Revive at the tip is the dead end's reward (MAP_DESIGN §1); a hidden Ether sits at the cairn's foot (Part 6). Delphoi itself waits for Route 28 from Kirrha (beat 37A) and Act III.]

### 36C. The treasury ruin (optional)

**Setup.** The south-west road drops through a cutting toward Kirrha and the sea. On the slope above the cutting stand the ruins of an old Phokian treasury, brought down by an earthquake: broken walls, a scatter of Doric pieces, and its column drums. A side path climbs to it from the cutting's top, and three of the drums lie across the path. The main road below is clear.
```text
Column drums from a fallen treasury, stacked across the path up to the ruin.

They're far too heavy to move by hand.
```
[With the Girdle, which every player on Route 9 holds, the drum takes the relic prompt (SYSTEMS.md §1, ASK):]
```text
A column drum from a fallen treasury.

Push it with the Girdle of Herakles?
```
The ruin teaches the Girdle plainly (MAP_DESIGN §3), three pushes on a short side path:
1. **Drum 1** is on the path's edge. Pushed west, it rolls off into the gully below with a long rumble and a shake. "The drum rolls over the edge. It's still rolling."
2. **Drum 2** sits behind it. Pushed south, it stops against the rock: drums stop at walls.
3. **Drum 3** then has a clear lane west into the same gully.

The path is open. Set `FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_SCHISTE_DRUMS` (the three drum objects hide; the gully below shows three drums at rest as metatiles). A failed arrangement never traps the player: a drum can always be pushed back the way it came, and walking off the map resets the three.

**The reward.** The ruin's floor holds a visible TM Rock Slide and a Hard Stone, and the best view on the route: the gulf, Kirrha's quay, and the mountains of Arkadia across the water.
```text
The treasury's floor is still paved. Somebody's city kept its gold here once.

Across the water, the mountains of Arkadia stand up out of the haze.
```
**Design notes.**
- The Girdle's main-path gate is the drum-blocked pass on Route 11, past Aigion (region B2). This ruin comes first on the road, so for most players it is the Girdle's first push: optional, short, and impossible to get stuck in. Route 11 then tests the verb.
- The crossroads carries the Oedipus touch in one sign (Part 2). Kithairon already told his story.

## Beat 38. The Krathis Gorge: the drums

Per STORY.md §3: the road climbs into Arkadia. Alethea walks with you from Aigion (beat 37C). Region B2's map is `MAP_ROUTE11_KRATHIS_GORGE` (`MAPSEC_AETHOS_ROUTE_11`), Aigion to Styx Falls, and it carries **the Girdle's main-path gate** (`design/AETHOS_MAP.md`). Thyrsa's west gate opens only once the player holds the Girdle (region A), so nobody reaches these drums without it.

**Setup.** At the foot of the gorge, a few screens south of Aigion, the road crosses a level shelf where an old temple of Artemis once stood above the river. It came down in a winter of earthquakes: three Doric column drums lie across the road between the cliff and the drop to the Krathis, and the rest of the temple is a slope of tumbled stone. A muleteer sits by them with three mules and a row of empty clay jars, waiting. The first time the player reaches the drums, a coord trigger runs with `FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_ROUTE11_DRUMS` unset. Alethea stops beside the player.
```text
MULETEER: Road's shut. Has been since the snows. The old temple came down on it.

MULETEER: I've been waiting for it to move itself. It hasn't.

ALETHEA: {PLAYER}. The belt. Silenos's belt.

ALETHEA: Herakles moved whole mountains in that. Truthfully, a mountain. Allegedly.
```
[The drums take the relic prompt (SYSTEMS.md §1, ASK):]
```text
A column drum from a fallen temple, as tall as you are.

Brace it with the Girdle of Herakles?
```
?? YES/NO

The drums are the Girdle's first use on the main path, so the three of them teach its three rules, one push each (MAP_DESIGN §3: teach, then test):
1. **Drum 1 rolls over edges.** It sits at the road's lip. Pushed east, it rolls off the shelf into the gorge with a long rumble and a camera shake. "The drum goes over the edge. You hear it hit the river. Then the river carries it off."
2. **Drum 2 fills gaps.** Behind it, the shelf's edge has broken away in a one-tile gap. Pushed into the gap, the drum drops in and sits flush, and becomes road. "The drum drops into the gap and wedges there. You could walk on it." The hawk spur on Route 12 uses this rule again, optionally.
3. **Drum 3 stops at walls.** It blocks the road itself. Pushed west, it rolls along the road and stops against the cliff, clearing the lane. "The drum rolls until the cliff stops it."

The road is open. Set `FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_ROUTE11_DRUMS`: the three drum objects hide, and the map shows drum 2 as road and drum 3 at rest against the cliff, as metatiles. A wrong push never blocks the road: a drum can always be pushed back the way it came, and leaving the map resets any drum not yet in its place.
```text
MULETEER: Ha! Herakles's belt, on a kid. I've seen everything now.

MULETEER: Here. I was keeping it for whoever moved the road.

MULETEER: Mules, jars and a hoof-cup. I carry the black water down for oaths.

MULETEER: Only a hoof holds it. It eats clay. It eats bronze. It ate my last jar.
```
[Give `ITEM_HARD_STONE`. The muleteer leads his mules on up the gorge and is hidden (`FLAG_ICHOR_ROUTE11_MULETEER`). He is next seen at Styx Falls, filling hoof-cups at the pool.]
```text
ALETHEA: Black water. He means the Styx.

ALETHEA: It's at the top of this gorge. Come on. I want to see it up close.
```
[Alethea walks on south and is hidden (`FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_ALETHEA_ROUTE11`). She waits at the falls (beat 39).]

**Design notes.**
- The drums replace region B1's Split Road drums, which moved here with the revised map. The muleteer's hoof-cup is the Styx's first seed, and a true one: ancient writers said Styx water dissolved every vessel but a horse's hoof.
- Drum 2's rule, drums fill gaps, is the one the optional hawk spur on Route 12 tests, and the one Talos's Bronze Servants combine with automata at Kaldera (SYSTEMS.md §12).

**Design note.** The falls are the waypoint's centrepiece and a seed for the post-game Underworld's Styx and Charon (`design/UNDERWORLD.md`): the black water, the muleteer's hoof-cups, the obols on the pool's floor (Part 2), the Oath Stone. Nothing here explains them. The Oath Stone's YES sets no flag and gives nothing; it is a choice the game simply lets you make.

**Design notes.**
- The words are STORY.md §7.2's. The stage directions add only what the engine needs: the blend, the picture window, the hide flags, the music cue, and the mask's link to the Dionysia, which is how Alethea knows a Titan when she sees one.
- **Six Poké Balls.** "Six to nothing" needs six. Kleon left Thyrsa with five (Part 3, region A) and caught a sixth on the road; it goes to the Titans' pens with his old life, and his Akropolis team is five again (Open questions 5).
- The tablet's close-up shows the hook. Alethea doesn't mention it here, because §7.2 doesn't; she says it in beat 43, once he's gone.

```text
{PLAYER} received TM Dark Pulse!

KALLISTO: Artemis takes the first of every hunt. The first feather from the first bird.

KALLISTO: Leave her one at her altar, and she'll keep an eye on you at night.

{PLAYER} received a Pretty Feather!
```
[Give `ITEM_PRETTY_FEATHER` ×1, the Hierophant's free loved offering (SYSTEMS.md §3). Set `FLAG_ICHOR_KALLISTO_RITE` and `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_TM_DARK_PULSE`. Artemis Favor +15 for the laurel. Then she looks past the player, toward the garden's gate, toward the Cypress Wood.]
```text
KALLISTO: There was a boy here at sunset. Lakonian. Red cloak.

KALLISTO: I fought the new moon, as I was told. I didn't see his face.

KALLISTO: …

KALLISTO: Go on. The east road is open now. My huntresses will let you through.
```
[Set `FLAG_ICHOR_HUNT_DONE` (if not already set by the trial) and clear the cordon: the two huntresses on Arkadia's east road are hidden (`FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_ARKADIA_CORDON`). Start the Skylaps and Kerdovix roamers (Part 4). Philoxenos in Emporion has a new story to hear (Phase 2's laurel flags, `FLAG_ICHOR_PHILOXENOS_LAUREL_5`).]

**Talking to Kallisto again** (she stays on her rock)
```text
KALLISTO: My reading said, show no mercy at the new moon. So I didn't.

KALLISTO: A reading is a reading. You don't argue with Delphoi.

KALLISTO: …Do you?
```
> with prophecy tablet #5 in the Bag (Part 6), once:
```text
KALLISTO: Where did you get that? I buried that. At my own tomb. As a joke.

KALLISTO: Lead doesn't lie. That's what they told me, when they brought it.
```
> and if Alethea has read it (`FLAG_ICHOR_PROPHECY_5_READ`, beat 43):
```text
KALLISTO: Your friend, the one who digs, she read it? What's underneath?

KALLISTO: …“Show mercy.”

KALLISTO: Keep it. I don't want to look at it. Not yet.
```
> otherwise:
```text
KALLISTO: Keep it. I don't want to look at it again.
```
> at Artemis Favor 30, once (SYSTEMS.md §3, gift I):
```text
KALLISTO: Artemis is pleased with you. She asked me to give you this.

{PLAYER} received TM Night Slash!

KALLISTO: She put a hunter in the sky for less. Look up tonight.
```
[Set `FLAG_ICHOR_GIFT_ARTEMIS_I` and place **Orion** (SYSTEMS.md §8).]

**Design notes.**
- Kallisto's line is STORY.md's exactly. Her reading was revised to make her merciless the night Kleon came ("KALLISTO OF ARKADIA. Revised." in the Knossa archive). She doesn't know that, and she doesn't learn it here. The tablet exchange is optional and only shows her doubt.
- "As a joke": the real Tomb of Kallisto stood in Arkadia (Pausanias 8.35), a mound with a shrine of Artemis Kalliste on top. A huntress named Kallisto burying her reading on the tomb of her namesake is the kind of joke a person makes when she's ashamed.
- She promises to look at the player, which is the thing she didn't do for Kleon. Her apology to him waits for the post-game Golden Hind (STORY.md, the post-game spine).

## Beat 45. Down out of Arkadia: the Argive Road and Nemea

Per STORY.md §3, Act II, and the revised `design/AETHOS_MAP.md` (Act II, step 8): Routes 13 and 14 lead back through Nemea to Emporion. The Moon Laurel lifts the huntresses' cordon on Arkadia's east edge (beat 44), and the road goes east over the Parthenion pass and down out of the highlands. Alethea is not with you: she went ahead to Astyra in beat 43. The leg is three cells on the map: Route 13, Nemea, Route 14.

### 45A. The Parthenion pass

**Setup.** The first step onto `MAP_ROUTE13_ARGIVE_ROAD` (`MAPSEC_AETHOS_ROUTE_13`) from Arkadia. No scene plays; the route's first moments are Pan's. At the top of the pass a cave shrine of Pan sits above the road with a syrinx carved over its mouth. RUNNER Ageus waits in plain view below it (Part 3).

**Pan's shrine** (an object; Pan is not one of SYSTEMS.md's fifteen gods, so it is lore, not a rite)
```text
A cave shrine of Pan. Someone has left a goat's horn of milk.

There's a carving over the mouth: a syrinx, seven reeds long.
```
[The first time, when the player steps onto the coord tile in front of the cave, play a single syrinx phrase SE from the left edge of the screen. No one is there.]
```text
Somewhere up the hill, someone plays seven notes on a pipe.

Then nothing. Even the cicadas stop.

…Then the cicadas start again.
```
[Set `FLAG_ICHOR_HEARD_PAN`. Ageus, after his battle, explains it (Part 3).]

**Design note.** Pan met the runner Pheidippides on this pass, called him by name and asked why Athens never honored him. Nobody calls the player's name: Pan plays and stops, the way the world does around the Unwoven. The player can read it as a joke or a chill.

### 45B. The Argive plain: Kleobis and Biton

**Setup.** Where the road crosses the Argive plain and climbs a low rise toward the Heraion's hill, an ox-cart blocks the road. Its yoke is empty. Two big young men stand between the shafts with ropes over their shoulders, and their mother sits in the cart under a parasol with a basket in her lap. This is the route's set piece. The two are RUNNERS Kleobis and Biton, a two-trainer double battle across the only path (Part 3). Before the battle:
```text
KLEOBIS: Mother wants to see Hera's feast. The oxen are late.

BITON: So we're the oxen.

KLEOBIS: You're blocking the oxen.
```
[After the battle, the brothers lean into the ropes and the cart creaks forward three tiles, off the road onto the Heraion spur, and stops again. The road is clear. Their mother waves the player over.]
```text
MOTHER: Aren't they good boys? Ten miles. Not a word of complaint.

BITON: Several words.

MOTHER: Hera's priestess says I should pray for the best gift a mortal can get.

MOTHER: For my sons. As thanks.

MOTHER: You know what she says the best gift is?

MOTHER: To die young. In your sleep. At your very best.

MOTHER: …

MOTHER: I said no thank you. I'll take them old and lazy.

KLEOBIS: Mother.

MOTHER: Hera can keep her best gift. Pull, boys. Slowly.
```
[Set `FLAG_ICHOR_KLEOBIS_BITON_SPOKE`. The cart stays on the spur below the Heraion for the rest of the game. Talking to the mother again: "MOTHER: Old and lazy. That's what I prayed for. Let's see her argue."]

**Design note.** In Herodotus, Hera granted the prayer and both brothers died in the temple that night, and Solon called them the happiest men alive. Here their mother turns down the glorious early death that Kleon is racing toward, and nothing in the scene says so. Act II's argument is about writing yourself a better fate; she just refuses the one on offer.

### 45C. Mycenae, from the road

**Setup.** Past the Heraion spur, the road bends north along the dry bed of the Inachos toward Nemea. On a hill to the east, out of reach behind the route's tree line, the Lion Gate shows as a large metatile landmark: two stone lions over a dark doorway. An old woman sits at a roadside shrine below it, shelling beans.
```text
OLD WOMAN: That's Mycenae up there. The king's house. Empty now.

OLD WOMAN: He came home from Troy with a prophetess, the old songs say.

OLD WOMAN: She told everyone what would happen. Nobody listened.

OLD WOMAN: It happened.

OLD WOMAN: People don't like a true thing said too early. They like it after.
```
**Design note.** Cassandra, unnamed. The player knows Alethea's tic and will hear her reading in beat 54; this is the echo before the scene, and it never names her.

### 45D. Nemea

**Setup.** The first step into `MAP_NEMEA` (`MAPSEC_NEMEA`) from Route 13 sets `FLAG_ICHOR_VISITED_NEMEA`. Nemea is a waypoint, not a town: a vine valley under Mount Tretos, where Zeus's temple stands with only three columns still up, the stadium of the Nemean games lies in the hillside, and above the valley the Lion's cave is shut with a great stone. It has no Asclepeion. The rest point is the **athletes' hostel**, where the games' runners and wrestlers sleep and bathe (Part 2).

No scene plays on arrival. The village is busy: the healers from Epidauros have stopped here on their way to the capital, and their wagon stands outside the hostel.

**The healers from Epidauros.** Epione, head of the healers' school at Epidauros, is traveling to Astyra with two of her students, Machaon and Akeso. They sit in the hostel's courtyard with their wagon of bandages. Epidauros itself lies off the map, down the coast; the healers are the sanctuary on the road. The first time the player talks to Epione:
```text
EPIONE: A traveler. Not sick, by the look of you. Just tired. Sit.

EPIONE: We're going up to Astyra. Half the capital's sick with worry, I'm told.

EPIONE: Worry fills an Asclepeion faster than a plague. Somebody's got to help.

EPIONE: The Asclepeion there? Phaedon keeps it. Best hands we ever trained.
```
[Set `FLAG_ICHOR_HEARD_OF_PHAEDON`.]
```text
EPIONE: He was a student of mine. Quiet. Never dropped a thing.

EPIONE: He used to say, “Every hurt closes, if you let it.”

EPIONE: We all say it now. Half my students don't know where it came from.

EPIONE: He came back to Epidauros once, after his wife died.

EPIONE: He slept three nights in our abaton. The god didn't come to him.

EPIONE: Some hurts don't close. I told him so. He didn't like it.

EPIONE: He has a little girl. I hope she keeps him busy.
```
[Then she gives the Eviolite (Part 2). Repeat visits: "EPIONE: Tell Phaedon that Epione says he's to eat more. He won't, but tell him."]

**Design note.** Two things land before the player meets him: his saying, and his grief. Neither points past a good man who lost his wife. At the unmasking in Act III the player will remember that the god didn't come to him, and that he didn't like being told some hurts don't close. Nothing here suggests the Titans.

**The Lion's cave.** Above the village a path climbs Mount Tretos to a cave mouth closed by a great stone. It is shut until the post-game's first Labor (STORY.md §3, LABORS); it is shown now and opened then.
```text
A cave in the side of the mountain, two mouths wide. A great stone closes it.

Somebody has scratched on the stone: HERAKLES WAS HERE.

Underneath, in another hand: SO WAS THE LION.

You put your ear to the stone. Something on the other side is breathing.

Slowly. Like something very large, asleep.
```
[A static Nemecub, Lv 29, sits on the slope below the cave the first time (`FLAG_ICHOR_NEMEAN_CUB`): "A lion cub, sunning itself on the rocks. It looks at the stone, then at you." It is a first stage below the band, in the kind of special spot BALANCE.md allows.]

**The stadium.** In the hillside south of the temple, the stadium of the Nemean games: a long track with its starting line of grooved stones, and a vaulted tunnel the athletes walk through to enter. The games are held at Nemea's festival, but the judge will run a contest any day for anyone who asks (Part 2, Part 3).
```text
[the tunnel's wall]
Scratched into the stone by athletes waiting to go out:

“AKROTATOS IS BEAUTIFUL.”

Underneath, in another hand: “SAYS WHO?”

Underneath that: “SAYS AKROTATOS.”
```

### 45E. Route 14, back to the Isthmus

**Setup.** `MAP_ROUTE14_KLEONAI_ROAD` (`MAPSEC_AETHOS_ROUTE_14`) runs north-east from Nemea over the Tretos pass and down through Kleonai to the Isthmus, entering Emporion from the south-west. No scene plays; its moment is Molorchos's hut at Kleonai, where a poor man's great-great-grandson still keeps one ram for a guest (Part 2).

## Beat 46. Emporion: the council rises

Phase 2's Open questions 14 asked what opens the road to Astyra. On the revised map it is the road of the Mysteries, out of Eleusa's east gate, closed in Act I by the Archon's council. Here the council rises, and Kerykos, the voice of every proclamation and a son of Eleusa's herald clan (Phase 2's Open questions 13), runs to open it.

**Setup.** The first time the player enters `MAP_EMPORION_CITY` from Route 14 with `FLAG_BADGE05_GET` set and `FLAG_ICHOR_COUNCIL_RISEN` unset, a coord trigger at the Route 14 entrance runs the scene. Kerykos comes running down the street toward the player with his herald's staff, and stops, out of breath. People in the street behind him are packing baskets.

[A salpinx call from the direction of the Agora, the herald's trumpet SE.]
```text
KERYKOS: {PLAYER}! There you are! Five laurels! Five! I counted twice.

KERYKOS: Kallisto's? Nobody gets Kallisto's. She doesn't look at them.

KERYKOS: Listen. The runners came in at dawn. The Archon's council has risen.

KERYKOS: It took them all spring. The road of the Mysteries is to open.

KERYKOS: Everyone's called to Astyra's Agora, to hear the Archon's word.

KERYKOS: And who opens the road? The herald of Eleusa's herald clan. Me!
```
?? Multichoice: WHAT'S THE WORD? / WHERE'S ALETHEA?
```text
> WHAT'S THE WORD?:
KERYKOS: Can't tell you. A herald reads a thing once, in the place it's for.

KERYKOS: Twice and it's gossip. Three times and it's a song.

> WHERE'S ALETHEA?:
KERYKOS: Daphne's girl? She came through here yesterday with a satchel.

KERYKOS: Asked when the Eleusa gate would open. I said when I open it.

KERYKOS: She said she'd wait at it. She said “truthfully” four times. I counted.
```
```text
KERYKOS: Right. Eleusa by dawn, if I run all night. Heralds do.

KERYKOS: Don't race me. You'd lose, and I'd talk about it all week.
```
[Kerykos runs off up the street toward Route 4 and is hidden (`FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_KERYKOS_EMPORION_ACT2`). Set `FLAG_ICHOR_COUNCIL_RISEN` and `FLAG_ICHOR_FERRY_TO_AEGINA` (world-act1's flag): with the council risen, Aigina takes passengers again, and Nausikles's ferry adds the stop. While Kerykos is away, the Temple of Hermes's guide, Angelos, says: "ANGELOS: The master's gone to open a road. He'll be back hoarse."]

**Nausikles, on the quay,** the first time after the scene (his ferry multichoice gains AIGINA from now on):
```text
NAUSIKLES: Council's risen, so Aigina's open to strangers again. I'll put in there now.
```

**The walk back.** The player retraces Act I's roads at their own pace: Route 4 over the Isthmus, Hecate's Hollow, Route 5 along the Skironian cliffs, to Eleusa (`design/AETHOS_MAP.md`). Those maps are Act I's and keep their Act I levels; the player is far stronger now, and the walk is quick. Nothing new plays on them.

**Emporion in Act II.** The other changes to the map (the dread lines, the Kronist, the Girdle stair, the two tablets, the knucklebone link) are in Part 2, "Emporion in Act II".

## Beat 46B. Optional: Demeter at the Maiden's Well

Per STORY.md II-5 and SYSTEMS.md §10, "Theoxenia", the core tier. **Opens after `FLAG_BADGE05_GET`**, on any visit to `MAP_ELEUSA_VILLAGE`. On the revised map the player walks through Eleusa on the way to the road of the Mysteries, so most players meet her. The test, the gift and every rule are SYSTEMS.md's; the reveal below is SYSTEMS.md's text, word for word. This beat adds the staging, the lines before the reveal, and what changes in Eleusa afterward.

**The pointer.** After `FLAG_BADGE05_GET`, the first time the player talks to any town's augur (Halitherses at Emporion, or the augurs of Thyrsa, Arkadia, Astyra and Kaldera), the augur says this before the day's omen. It is a one-time line, not one of SYSTEMS.md §6's omen kinds; the Stranger omen opens only after all three core visits.
```text
AUGUR: Something odd. The cranes came over Eleusa a month early.

AUGUR: Circled the well three times, low, and went on.

AUGUR: Cranes mean sowing. In this season? Someone ought to go and look.
```
[Set `FLAG_ICHOR_DEMETER_OMEN_TOLD`.]

**Setup.** Show Cami on the Maiden's Well's worn bench (Phase 2's seed object) when `FLAG_BADGE05_GET` is set and `FLAG_ICHOR_THEOXENIA_DEMETER` is unset: clear `FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_THEOXENIA_DEMETER`. She is a young woman in a gray shawl, sitting on the seat stone just south of the Kallichoron well and facing it (`OBJ_EVENT_GFX_ICHOR_CAMI` with `MOVEMENT_TYPE_FACE_UP`: her north-facing frames are the seated pose; the user named her and gave the photo she is drawn from, SYSTEMS.md §10). While she should stay seated, her script never uses `faceplayer`. Her sprite's palette tag, `OBJ_EVENT_PAL_TAG_ICHOR_THEOXENIA`, costs Eleusa's map one more OBJ palette slot. Eleusa's sign by the well still says an old woman sat on this bench: that is the song's version, and her reveal answers it.

**The tells** (SYSTEMS.md §10). She has **no shadow**. Within 3 tiles, the player's follower **bows**. With the Augur's Eye open on this map, its screen adds "Something here is watching you." And her shawl:
```text
[the shawl, examined from behind her]
Her shawl is worn and gray. Caught in its fringe is a single ear of wheat.

Ripe. In this season.
```
**The well.** From Act II on, the Maiden's Well can be drawn from once a day (`FLAG_DAILY_ICHOR_MAIDENS_WELL`):
```text
The Maiden's Well. The rope is wet. Draw some water?
```
?? YES/NO. YES gives 1 Fresh Water: "You draw up a jar of cold water." After the day's draw: "Someone's drawn today already. You, by the look of the rope."

**Talking to her.**
```text
CAMI: …

CAMI: Oh. A traveler. Sit, if you like. The bench is long.

CAMI: I'm Cami. I've walked a long way looking for someone. My daughter.

CAMI: She went down somewhere I can't follow. Picking flowers.

CAMI: I'm thirsty. That's all. And tired of being sad.

CAMI: Have you anything to drink, friend?
```
[A multichoice built from what the player carries: WINE (if they hold Wine), WATER (if they hold Fresh Water), BARLEY WATER (if they hold Fresh Water and a Barley Cake: her *kykeon*), NOTHING. `VAR_TEMP_1` records the drink.]
```text
> WINE:
CAMI: No. Not wine. Not today. Not for a long time.

CAMI: Have you anything else?
```
[Return to the multichoice without WINE. This is SYSTEMS.md's refusal; it is not a failure.]
```text
> WATER:
[Take 1 Fresh Water.]
CAMI: Water. Thank you, friend. That's kind.

> BARLEY WATER:
[Take 1 Fresh Water and 1 Barley Cake.]
CAMI: Barley, and water, and… is that mint? Where did you learn that?

CAMI: Someone taught you very well. Someone old.

> NOTHING:
CAMI: Never mind, friend. Never mind.

CAMI: I'll be here. I'm always here, lately.
```
[NOTHING ends the visit; she stays on the bench and the test can be retried at once (SYSTEMS.md: "No permanent failure").]

**The joke.** After WATER or BARLEY WATER:
```text
CAMI: There. That's better.

CAMI: Now. A girl here made me laugh once, when I'd forgotten how.

CAMI: Do you know any jokes? Tell me one. A bad one, if you've got it.
```
?? Multichoice: THE GOAT / THE FIG-SELLER / THE HARVEST
```text
> THE GOAT:
You tell her the one about the goat who paid a seer for a reading.

“You'll be eaten,” said the seer. “Everyone says that,” said the goat…

…and it ate the seer's scroll.

> THE FIG-SELLER:
You tell her the one about the fig-seller who sold a snatcher a fig…

…and then sold it back the same fig, still wet. Twice.

> THE HARVEST:
You tell her about a year the harvest failed. It's very sad.

CAMI: …That's not a joke, traveler. That's a harvest.

CAMI: Never mind. Never mind. Come back another day.
```
[THE HARVEST ends the visit kindly. She stays on the bench and the visit can be tried again once you have left the well-yard and come back (a temp flag, `FLAG_TEMP_1`, cleared on the map change), with the same test, per SYSTEMS.md's "no permanent failure". THE GOAT and THE FIG-SELLER both land: the reveal follows.]

**The reveal** (SYSTEMS.md §10, word for word).

[Cami laughs, a cracked sound, then a real one.]
```text
CAMI: Ha. Oh, that's terrible. Tell it again.

CAMI: I haven't laughed since my daughter went away.
```
[She stands: `applymovement` her object with `nurse_joy_bow` and `waitmovement` (her rise, `ANIM_ICHOR_RISE`, 56 frames, ending facing down). Then she is taller than she was: swap her for `OBJ_EVENT_GFX_ICHOR_DEMETER`, her revealed form (two objects swapped by hide flags, as Act II does it; BUILD.md). Gold light fills the well-yard: a fade to white over 16 frames and back. The dry stalks around the well turn green and heavy (the well-yard's dry-grass metatiles swap to ripe wheat), and the dry fig over the well bursts into leaf (its metatile swaps to the fig in leaf, with fruit).]
```text
DEMETER: I sat at this well once before. The song says I was an old woman.

DEMETER: People remember what they expect. Nobody expects a god.

DEMETER: A girl brought me water. Another made me laugh. I never forgot them.

DEMETER: You did both. Hold out your hands.
```
[`givemon SPECIES_SNIVY` with the gift's touches (table below). The theoxenia reveal cue plays (Part 9).]
```text
{PLAYER} received a Snivy from Demeter!

DEMETER: It grows where it's tended. So do you.

DEMETER: Don't tell anyone Cami was me. They'll feed every stranger in Eleusa.

DEMETER: …Actually. Tell everyone.
```
[She walks to the edge of the well-yard and is hidden between one step and the next. Set `FLAG_ICHOR_THEOXENIA_DEMETER` and `FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_THEOXENIA_DEMETER`. Demeter Favor +15 (SYSTEMS.md §3). If the drink was BARLEY WATER, Demeter Favor +5 more: it was her loved offering.]

**The gift** (SYSTEMS.md §10's table and shared touches).

| Gift | Lv | Held | Nature | Ability | God-taught move | Perfect IVs | Touches |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Snivy | 35 | Miracle Seed | Timid | Contrary (hidden) | Leaf Storm | HP, Sp. Atk, Speed | Cherish Ball; the Xenia Ribbon; fateful encounter; met location "a guest-gift of Demeter" |

Snivy is past Servine's level (17) and one short of Serperior's (36), so its next two level-ups bring Servine and then Serperior: the blessing unfolds (SYSTEMS.md).

**Eleusa afterward.**
- The fig over the well stays in leaf. Once a day it gives a Figy Berry (`FLAG_DAILY_ICHOR_WELL_FIG`): "The fig over the well is heavy with fruit. In this month." The bench reads: "A stone bench by the well. Still warm."
- **Metaneira**, at the house of Keleos, after the visit:
  ```text
  METANEIRA: The fig by the well's in leaf. In this month. The wheat's ripe.

  METANEIRA: My great-grandmother said this happened once before.

  METANEIRA: …Was it her? Don't tell me. No. Tell me.

  METANEIRA: No! Don't. I'll feed everyone either way.
  ```
- **The water-carrier**:
  ```text
  WATER-CARRIER: A young woman sat on that bench all week. Nobody spoke to her.

  WATER-CARRIER: Then the fig came out in leaf. I'm speaking to everyone now.

  WATER-CARRIER: You never know. You never know.
  ```

**Design note.** The *Hymn* has the goddess come as an old woman; here she comes as Cami, and the song remembered her wrong. Eleusa's sign still tells the song's version, and the reveal's "People remember what they expect" answers them. Two of the three jokes land, as SYSTEMS.md says. The failing choice is a sad story, not a crude one, so the lesson is the Hymn's: she needed laughter, not sympathy. The drink accepts water, as SYSTEMS.md has it, and loves the *kykeon*, whose makings Metaneira gave the player after Laurel 3 in Phase 2. Prophecy tablet #4 is in the well-yard too (Part 2, "Eleusa in Act II").
