## Beat 47. The road of the Mysteries

The revised map's Act II, step 8: from Eleusa, Route 15 (the road of the Mysteries, closed in Act I), Daphni, and Route 16 over the pass to Astyra. Four maps in four cells (Route 15 with Thria, Daphni, Route 16): the last walk before the capital, with the rest of Aethos walking it too.

### 47A. Eleusa's east gate

**Setup.** The first time the player is in `MAP_ELEUSA_VILLAGE` with `FLAG_BADGE05_GET` set and `FLAG_ICHOR_ROUTE15_OPEN` unset, a coord trigger two tiles west of the east gate runs the scene. Kerykos stands on the gate's step, between the gate's two hoplites (Act I's, who kept it shut for the council). A crowd of villagers and initiates (four townsfolk objects) stands in front of him.

[A salpinx call. The crowd turns to face the gate.]
```text
KERYKOS: HEAR! HEAR, Eleusa! Hear the Archon's council!

KERYKOS: The council has risen! The road of the Mysteries is open!

KERYKOS: Every citizen, every guest, every stranger on every road…

KERYKOS: …is called to the Agora of Astyra, to hear the Archon's word!

KERYKOS: At noon. Bring a hat. It's a long word.
```
[The two hoplites lift the gate's bar and stand aside. The crowd walks east through the gate and is hidden. Kerykos sees the player and hops down from the step.]
```text
KERYKOS: You came the long way! Over the Isthmus, through the Hollow? Good.

KERYKOS: I came the long way too. I'm a herald. There isn't a short way.
```
[Whatever the player asked in beat 46:]
```text
KERYKOS: Daphne's girl was sitting on this step when I got here at dawn.

KERYKOS: First through the gate. Said she had something for the Keeper of Records.

KERYKOS: Very serious. She didn't even say goodbye. She said “truthfully”.
```
```text
KERYKOS: Right. Daphni, the pass, the Agora. Noon. I'll be the loud one.
```
[Kerykos runs east through the gate and is hidden (`FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_KERYKOS_ELEUSA_GATE`). Set `FLAG_ICHOR_ROUTE15_OPEN`. For the rest of the game the hoplites stand either side of the open gate:]
```text
HOPLITE: The council's risen. Took them all spring. Go on.

HOPLITE: Everyone's on the road today. Mind the initiates. They walk slowly on purpose.
```
**Design note.** The gate opens on the fifth laurel, not on anything the player does: the council rose because the seers' news can't be kept in a room any longer. The player arrives in Astyra with the rest of Aethos, to hear the countdown read aloud (beat 48, region C2, where Kerykos says "I ran. Heralds run."). Alethea is a few hours ahead, as region C2's beat 52 needs: she files her evidence that morning.

### 47B. Route 15, the Rheitoi, and Thria

**Setup.** `MAP_ROUTE15_ROAD_OF_THE_MYSTERIES` (`MAPSEC_AETHOS_ROUTE_15`) runs east from Eleusa's east gate across the edge of the Thriasian plain: the first wheat, the Rheitoi (two salt streams sacred to Demeter and the Kore, and the bridge over the larger), to the hamlet of **Thria** (`MAP_THRIA`, inside the same section), the first bed after Eleusa and the last before the pass. Phase 2 wrote these places for Act I's Sacred Way; on the revised map they are Act II's, and this beat brings them over (Part 2, Part 3). It is the road the procession walked to the Mysteries in the autumn of Act I, and today everyone is walking it the other way.

The first time the player enters, a column of walkers (four or five townsfolk objects) heads east ahead of them and is hidden at the first screen's edge. More of the crowd is drawn into the metatiles: people resting on the verges, a family eating on a blanket, a donkey with baskets.

**The crowd** (four walkers, ambient, the first time only; one line each if the player catches them)
```text
WALKER: My seer says the same as everyone's seer. I want to hear why.

WALKER: The Archon will say something calm. He always says something calm.

WALKER: I don't care what he says. It's a day off.

WALKER: They say there's a play about it. In Thyrsa. A whole play.
```
**The jesters' bridge.** Iambe and Thersites still keep the Rheitoi bridge, as they did for the procession: the *gephyrismos*, the insults at the bridge. They mock everyone now, walkers and Kronists alike. The mandatory double battle at the only crossing is Phase 2's, re-levelled (Part 3). While the player approaches, a Kronist object crosses ahead of them and the jesters have a go at him:
```text
THERSITES: A Kronist! Forever young, is it? Have you SEEN yourself?

THERSITES: Forever isn't helping, friend.

IAMBE: Leave him. He's walking to the city to hear he's right. Let him walk.

KRONIST: …May your thread never be cut.

IAMBE: Nor your beard, by the look of it.
```
[The Kronist hurries east and is hidden. Then the jesters spot the player.]

**The Kronists at Thria.** On Thria's threshing floor, two Kronists have pitched tents and are handing out bread to the walkers. One of them speaks the Titans' pitch, a beat before the cart in Astyra's Agora says it to the whole city:
```text
KRONIST: Bread for the walk! Free! Take two. Nobody's counting.

KRONIST: You're going to hear the Archon? Good. Listen to what he doesn't say.

KRONIST: He'll tell you it's written. He won't tell you who's writing.

KRONIST: May your thread never be cut, friend.
```
?? Multichoice: NOR YOURS / NO, THANKS
```text
> NOR YOURS:
KRONIST: Ha! There you are. You'll pick it up.

> NO, THANKS:
KRONIST: Fair. Take the bread anyway. Bread's not a creed.
```
[Either answer gives 1 Barley Cake, once (`FLAG_ICHOR_KRONIST_BREAD_THRIA`).]

**The sisters who won't cast.** In Thria, the three old sisters of the round house try to cast their pebbles for the player, and the pebbles won't fall (Part 2). It is the act's quietest dread line: even the Titans' readers can't read you, and neither can the oldest seers on the road.

**Design note.** The Kronist's "you'll pick it up" is the line Iapetos says to Kleon in beat 42; the player may have answered "Nor yours" without thinking, which is how a creed spreads. The jesters were the Mysteries' joke on the way to the holiest night of the year; now they are the only people on the road laughing at the Titans out loud.

### 47C. Daphni

**Setup.** `MAP_DAPHNI` (`MAPSEC_DAPHNI`) is a waypoint where the road of the Mysteries enters the pass: a sanctuary of Apollo in a grove of laurels, Daphne's namesake, with a pilgrims' halt for a rest point. The first step in sets `FLAG_ICHOR_VISITED_DAPHNI`. No scene plays; the grove is quiet even with the road full, because people lower their voices under the laurels.

**The quiet line.** Apollo's priest, under the oldest laurel (Part 2), the first time:
```text
PRIEST: Apollo's grove. Every laurel here is a girl who ran from him.

PRIEST: That's the story. I prefer to think they just like it here.

PRIEST: A scholar came through, a few weeks back. From Kalliste.

PRIEST: She wouldn't sit under the laurels. Wouldn't even stand under them.

PRIEST: She said she'd been one long enough.
```
**Design note.** Daphne, in Astyra's Library by now (beat 51), passed this way after Act I. The player knows exactly who it was and why the line is funny, and why it isn't.

### 47D. Route 16, the Aigaleos pass

**Setup.** `MAP_ROUTE16_AIGALEOS_PASS` (`MAPSEC_AETHOS_ROUTE_16`) climbs east from Daphni over the shoulder of Mount Aigaleos and comes down through Athena's sacred olives to the Kephisos and the capital's west side: the Kerameikos and the Dipylon (region C2). Its moment is the first sight of the capital.

**The first sight of Astyra.** At the top of the pass, a coord trigger the first time. The camera pans six tiles north-east, holds, and pans back.
```text
From the top of the pass, the whole plain opens below you.

Olive groves, a river, walls, and more roofs than you can count.

And in the middle of it all, a rock, with temples on it, white in the sun.

Astyra.
```
[Set `FLAG_ICHOR_SAW_ASTYRA`. A walker beside the player, the first time: "WALKER: First time? Everyone stops there. I still do."]

**Arrival.** At the foot of the pass the road crosses the Kephisos and runs to the Dipylon through the Kerameikos. The arrival in the Agora is beat 48 (region C2). Route 16's people, Procrustes's inn and the owl stele are in Part 2.

**Design note.** The road of the Mysteries is the act's last corridor before the hub: one road with everyone on it, going to hear the same news.

## Beat 48. Astyra: the Agora

Per STORY.md §3, II-6.

**The arrival.** The player comes over the pass from Daphni on Route 16 and enters the capital the way every pilgrim of the Sacred Way did: through the Kerameikos, the cemetery outside the walls, along a street of tombs to the Dipylon. The first step into `MAP_ASTYRA_KERAMEIKOS` from Route 16 shows the walls and, above them, the Akropolis with the Parthenon on it; no text. The first step through the Dipylon into `MAP_ASTYRA` runs a coord trigger: set `FLAG_ICHOR_ARRIVED_ASTYRA` and `FLAG_ICHOR_VISITED_ASTYRA` (fly). The Panathenaic Way runs from the gate straight across the Agora to the rock. It is full. People are walking toward the Agora in twos and threes, all in the same direction, the way a city walks to a fire. An ARCHER at the gate:
```text
ARCHER: Agora's straight on. Everyone's going. The herald's in.

ARCHER: Asclepeion's at the end of the street, under the rock. Most need it.
```
[The Agora opens just inside the gate. At the far end of the Way, under the Akropolis's cliff, the Asclepeion's door is lit. The rock stands over everything, its ramp guarded.]

**The Agora.** On the first step into the Agora's square, an `ON_FRAME` script runs. The square is drawn full of citizens in the metatiles. Six objects matter: Euthyphron the Kronist on his cart by the Kairos statue, a seer, a woman with a child, Kerykos at the herald's stone, a second Kronist at the statue's foot, and (from the north) Alethea, hidden until the end. Play `MUS_ICHOR_ASTYRA`, quietly, under the crowd.

[Euthyphron stands on a two-wheeled cart, a sickle pin on his plain chiton, his arms open. The crowd hushes for him.]
```text
EUTHYPHRON: Friends! Ask any seer in this city. Go on. Ask.

EUTHYPHRON: Every thread ends on the same day.

EUTHYPHRON: Yours. Mine. That baby's.

EUTHYPHRON: They won't tell you why. We will.
```
[The camera pans to the seer, an old man with a lamp who has been reading threads at a table under the stoa.]
```text
SEER: …It's true. I read sixty threads this month.

SEER: Every one stops on the same row. Like a cloth that runs out.
```
[The woman with the child, by the fountain:]
```text
WOMAN: Mine and my boy's. The same day. He's four.

WOMAN: I paid two seers. I wanted one of them to be wrong.
```
[A bronze staff rings on stone, three times. Kerykos stands on the herald's stone, dusty to the knees, a scroll in one hand. He is breathing hard.]
```text
KERYKOS: HEAR THE ARCHON!

KERYKOS: Sorry. One moment. I ran here. All the way.

KERYKOS: I ran. Heralds run.

KERYKOS: Hear the Archon, Aristeides, son of Lysimachos!
```
[He unrolls the scroll and reads in his herald's voice.]
```text
KERYKOS: “The seers of Aethos report that every thread ends on one day.

KERYKOS: “The Archon has consulted the laws of the Fates and of the city.

KERYKOS: “If it is written, meet it with dignity.”
```
[He turns the scroll over. Then back again.]
```text
KERYKOS: …That's all of it. I checked twice. Both sides.

KERYKOS: I asked him if there was more. There wasn't.
```
[The crowd breaks into noise: a crowd-murmur SE, no text. Euthyphron raises his hands again.]
```text
EUTHYPHRON: Dignity! You heard him. He wants you to die with dignity.

EUTHYPHRON: We want you not to die.

EUTHYPHRON: Come to the stall by the old spring. Bread's free. So's the truth.

EUTHYPHRON: May your thread never be cut!

CROWD: Nor yours!
```
[Half the square answers him. The crowd thins: walk the citizen metatiles' "busy" variant back to the quiet one in one swap, offscreen. Alethea runs in from the north side of the square, her satchel bumping.]
```text
ALETHEA: {PLAYER}! You came! Truthfully, I was starting to worry.

ALETHEA: Five laurels? Oh, that's- no, later. I've done it.

ALETHEA: I've filed everything. The notice. The program. The hooks.

ALETHEA: With the Keeper of Records himself. Lykophron.

ALETHEA: He read every page. He was very kind about it.

ALETHEA: He's putting it before the Assembly. A real hearing!

ALETHEA: If anyone in Aethos can read a forgery, it's the Archon's Keeper.
```
[If the player carries any prophecy tablets she hasn't read (SYSTEMS.md §5), she reads them now, one box each (Part 2, the Stoa), and adds them to her case.]
```text
ALETHEA: Daphne's here too. Staying with a friend of hers. A healer.

ALETHEA: The Asclepeion, under the rock. His house is next door.

ALETHEA: She said to bring you the minute you arrived. So. Go.

ALETHEA: I'll be at the Stoa. Being patient. Truthfully, badly.
```
[Set `FLAG_ICHOR_HEARD_PROCLAMATION`. Alethea walks to the Stoa of the Archon and is hidden (`FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_ALETHEA_AGORA`); she reappears inside the Stoa. Kerykos stays at the herald's stone.]

**The two statues.** Both stand at the square's crossing, in plain view, and read when the player faces them.
```text
[Statue of Kodros]
A king in a peasant's cloak, walking forward. No crown. No spear.

The plinth: KODROS, THE LAST KING.

“He walked into the spears for his city. The Oracle asked it.”

[Statue of Kairos]
A young runner on tiptoe on a razor's edge. Wings at his heels.

Long hair falls over his face in front. The back of his head is bald.

The plinth: SEIZE HIM AS HE COMES.

Someone has scratched a sickle across his face. Deep.
```
A Kronist sits on the plinth's step, eating bread:
```text
KRONIST: Kairos. The god of the right moment. The one chance.

KRONIST: Grab his hair as he comes, or he's gone. Bald behind, see?

KRONIST: Who needs him? No more moments. Only the hour.
```
**Kerykos,** afterwards:
```text
KERYKOS: You again! Five laurels! I said you'd go far. I say that a lot.

KERYKOS: I'm the voice of the Archon's word. All of it. Even this.

KERYKOS: I don't write them. I only read them. That's the job.

KERYKOS: …Some days I'd like the other job.
```
**Design notes.**
- The Archon is a name on a scroll here, and a fatalist. That is STORY.md's deliberate misdirection; he is seen in person only at the urn (beat 53).
- Kairos's statue is the Moment's first seed (STORY.md §2, the Moment). Kodros's is Medon's original sin, unexplained.
- Alethea's "If anyone can read a forgery" is the act's cruelest line in hindsight. It is set up here so the hearing (beat 52) lands.

## Beat 49. The Asclepeion: the healer

Per STORY.md §3, II-7, and LABYRINTH.md seed 9.

**Setup.** `MAP_ASTYRA_ASCLEPEION` (the room is in Part 2). A man in a plain white chiton stands behind the counter, gray-streaked beard, kind tired eyes. A small clay bull hangs from his belt. A Panacoil is coiled round the counter post. He is the nurse: every heal in Astyra is his. Play the usual Asclepeion theme; nothing here hints at the lullaby, which the player first hears in Elpis's room (`design/MUSIC.md` §2). From `FLAG_ICHOR_MET_ELPIS` on, Astyra's Asclepeion plays `MUS_ICHOR_PHAEDON` instead: the hum's lyre verse alone, for the healer.

**First visit.** The first time the player talks to him, before the heal:
```text
PHAEDON: Welcome. You've walked a long way. I can tell by the feet.

PHAEDON: Yours and theirs. Let me see them.
```
[He takes the party's balls one by one and holds each a moment. Buffer the lead Pokémon's nickname into `STR_VAR_1`.]
```text
PHAEDON: And who's this? {STR_VAR_1}. Hello, {STR_VAR_1}. Good name.

PHAEDON: Easy now. There.

PHAEDON: Every hurt closes, if you let it.
```
[Heal the party, with the heal jingle. Panacoil uncoils and touches each ball with its nose. Set `FLAG_ICHOR_MET_PHAEDON`.]
```text
PANACOIL: Hss.

PHAEDON: She checks my work. She's usually right.

PHAEDON: Kalliste? Then you'll know Daphne. Everyone on Kalliste does.

PHAEDON: She's at my house, next door. Reading to my daughter.

PHAEDON: Go up, if you like. Knock loudly. They'll both be asleep.
```
**Every later heal** rotates through three closings after "Easy now. There.":
```text
PHAEDON: Every hurt closes, if you let it.

PHAEDON: There. Good as they were. Better, maybe.

PHAEDON: How's {STR_VAR_1}? Eating? Good. Make sure.
```
The Pithos stands in its niche at the back (`setvar` and `special` as every Asclepeion; ENGINE_API.md).

**The hearth.** A household altar of Hestia stands by the inner door, its ash gray and cold. Facing it:
```text
A hearth altar of Hestia. The ash in it is old and cold.

Nobody has asked her for anything here in a long time.
```
With Phaedon in the room, he answers from the counter:
```text
PHAEDON: I don't use it. I'm sorry. It isn't hers I'm angry with.

PHAEDON: I've stopped asking.
```
[The altar still works for the player. If the player prays, Phaedon watches, and says nothing.]

**Design notes.**
- LABYRINTH.md seed 9 is exact: "Easy now. There." and "Every hurt closes, if you let it." He says the same words to Asterion at Knossa, and he asks after the player's Pokémon by name at the unmasking. That is why he learns the lead's name here.
- Nothing he says is false, and nothing points at the mask.

## Beat 50. Phaedon's house: Starry

Per STORY.md §3, II-8, and LABYRINTH.md seeds 8 and 17.

**Setup.** `MAP_ASTYRA_PHAEDONS_HOUSE`, next to the Asclepeion. The first entry with `FLAG_ICHOR_MET_PHAEDON` set (or, if the player skipped the heal, the first entry at all; then Phaedon's arrival below is his first meeting and sets the flag). A small, clean two-room house that smells of herbs. In the back room a girl of about seven sits up in a bed too big for her, under a shawl too big for her, holding a clay bull. An Ophidrop sleeps in a coil at her feet. Daphne sits on a stool beside her with a scroll, in her sandals. A little bronze music box sits on the shelf over the bed. Play `MUS_ICHOR_ELPIS_LULLABY` only when Elpis hums; otherwise there is no music, only a dog barking far off.

```text
DAPHNE: {PLAYER}! You're here. You're really here. Come in. Quietly.

DAPHNE: Elpis, this is my friend from Kalliste. The one I told you about.

ELPIS: The one with no shadow?

DAPHNE: No, dear. Everyone has a shadow. The one with the questions.

ELPIS: Oh. Hello.
```
[Elpis holds up the clay bull with both hands.]
```text
ELPIS: This is Starry. Papa brought him from an island.

ELPIS: There's a real one. He's sad all the time.

ELPIS: Papa's going to make him better.

DAPHNE: Her papa can make anything better. It's a terrible habit.
```
?? Multichoice: HE'S A GOOD BULL / WHERE'S THE REAL ONE?
```text
> HE'S A GOOD BULL:
ELPIS: He is. He's the best bull. He doesn't moo. He's polite.

> WHERE'S THE REAL ONE?:
ELPIS: Under an island. In the dark. Papa says he's very far away.

ELPIS: When I'm better I'm going to see him. And the sea.

ELPIS: I've never seen the sea. Daphne says it's mostly wet.
```
```text
ELPIS: Are you going to have a reading? At home they do it for big girls.

ELPIS: I had one when I was a baby. I know what it says.

ELPIS: I'll go when the hours stop.

ELPIS: Papa says hours don't stop. So I'll never go.
```
[Daphne looks down at her scroll. Hold 40 frames.]
```text
DAPHNE: …That's right. Now. Where were we?

ELPIS: The song. You said I could do the song before the story.

DAPHNE: I did say that. Go on, then.
```
[Elpis hums. Play `MUS_ICHOR_ELPIS_LULLABY` (627, built): her hum over a lyre rocking the cradle, stopping on the half cadence, the eighth bar the lyre alone rocking on A (`design/MUSIC.md` §2). This is the first time the player hears the lullaby anywhere. Elpis yawns.]
```text
ELPIS: …I always fall asleep before the end.

ELPIS: I don't know how it ends. Nobody does. Papa doesn't either.

DAPHNE: Then it's a very good song. Lie down.
```
[Elpis lies down with Starry under her chin. The Ophidrop shifts and resettles. The front door opens: Phaedon comes in, setting down a bag of herbs. Set `FLAG_ICHOR_MET_PHAEDON` if it isn't set.]
```text
PHAEDON: Is she asleep? She's always asleep when I get home.

PHAEDON: Oh! The traveler. Hello again. Hello, {STR_VAR_1}.

PHAEDON: Daphne. Still being wrong?

DAPHNE: Constantly. You?

PHAEDON: Never, lately.
```
[Phaedon sits on the end of the bed, very carefully, so as not to wake her. He straightens the shawl.]
```text
DAPHNE: Phaedon. That book I sent you. Years ago. Have you still got it?

PHAEDON: I read it until the binding broke.

DAPHNE: Burn it.

PHAEDON: …I'll think about it.

DAPHNE: Think quickly. I'm going to the Library. I've a book to unwrite.

DAPHNE: {PLAYER}, come with me. Tomorrow. The Library opens at dawn.

DAPHNE: Truthfully, it opens when the librarian wakes up. Dawn-ish.
```
[Daphne leaves; she is hidden here and shown in the Library (`FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_DAPHNE_PHAEDONS_HOUSE`). Set `FLAG_ICHOR_MET_ELPIS`.]

**Talking to Phaedon afterwards:**
```text
PHAEDON: Her mother had the same laugh. Gone five years now. A fever.

PHAEDON: Best healer in Astyra, they call me. And a fever.

PHAEDON: …Every hurt closes, if you let it. Almost every.
```
**The music box,** on the shelf:
```text
A little bronze music box. A clever thing, all tiny gears.

On the lid, in a child's letters: FROM PAPA'S FRIEND UNDER THE ISLAND.

Wind it?
```
?? YES/NO
```text
> YES:
[Play `MUS_ICHOR_ELPIS_LULLABY_BOX` (628, built) once through: the comb an octave up, the escapement ticking, and in the eighth bar only the tick. Then the room returns to 627.]

The tune stops one note short. You wait for the last note.

It doesn't come.
```
If Elpis is awake (any later visit, by day):
```text
ELPIS: It always does that. So do I. We're the same.
```
**Elpis, on later visits** (before the raid):
```text
ELPIS: Papa has to go away sometimes. To fix things.

ELPIS: He always comes back. He brings me things. Starry, and the box.

ELPIS: He looks sad when he thinks I'm asleep. Is that because of me?
```
?? Multichoice: NO / I DON'T KNOW
```text
> NO:
ELPIS: Good. I'll tell him you said so. He listens to travelers.

> I DON'T KNOW:
ELPIS: Daphne says that too. She says it's the most honest thing there is.

ELPIS: I think it's the most annoying.
```
**Design notes.**
- Elpis's "I'll go when the hours stop. Papa says hours don't stop." is STORY.md's exact line, with its child's ending, "So I'll never go." It reads as comfort now. At the Frozen Hour it reads as the whole tragedy.
- "Never, lately." is Phaedon's certainty, said as a joke between old friends.
- "I read it until the binding broke." is true. He doesn't lie to Daphne, and he doesn't promise to burn it.
- The music box's label is STORY.md §2 and LABYRINTH.md seed 17. The player hears the lullaby here first, so the workshop's prototype at Knossa and Phaedon's theme at the unmasking land as something already known.
- "The one with no shadow?" is a child's mix-up between the theoxenia's tells and Daphne's stories about the player. It costs nothing, and it is wrong in an interesting way.

## Beat 51. The Library: a book to unwrite

Per STORY.md §3, II-9, LABYRINTH.md seed 10 and page V.

**Setup.** `MAP_ASTYRA_LIBRARY`, on the Agora's north side. The first entry with `FLAG_ICHOR_MET_ELPIS` set. A long hall of scroll niches from floor to ceiling, reading tables down the middle, a courtyard with a fig tree at the far end. Daphne sits at the last table under the window, behind a wall of wax tablets. The librarian, Apellikon, an old man with a magnifying crystal on a cord, shelves scrolls on a ladder.
```text
DAPHNE: You came. Sit. Mind the tablets. That pile's chapter three.

DAPHNE: Every copy of my book that I know of, the Archon's office burned.

DAPHNE: Except one. And the one I didn't know of. The one they have.

DAPHNE: I can't unwrite a book. I've tried. Words don't come back.

DAPHNE: So I'm writing another one. With every place wrong.

DAPHNE: If they ever read it, they'll go and dig up the sea.
```
?? Multichoice: GOOD PLAN / WILL IT WORK?
```text
> GOOD PLAN:
DAPHNE: It's a terrible plan. It's the only one I've got.

> WILL IT WORK?:
DAPHNE: No. They have the real one. But it gives my hands something to do.
```
```text
DAPHNE: The last chapter is Kaldera. The Telchines' forge.

DAPHNE: The third piece. I wrote that it was there. I wrote the door.

DAPHNE: I've never seen it. I wrote it from an old man's description.

DAPHNE: …Go on. Look around. Apellikon has been waiting all morning.

DAPHNE: He has a page for you. He won't tell me what's on it.
```
[Set `FLAG_ICHOR_LIBRARY_DAPHNE`.]

**Apellikon, the librarian, and page V.**
```text
APELLIKON: Ah. Daphne's traveler. She says you collect odd pages.

APELLIKON: A fisherman brought me one. Drawings. Wings, gears, a bell.

APELLIKON: I filed it under Birds. Most of it's birds.

APELLIKON: But a page must go on the right shelf, next to the right thing.

APELLIKON: Tell me what belongs beside it, and it's yours.

APELLIKON: What did the boy Perdix become, when he fell?
```
?? Multichoice: A PARTRIDGE / AN OWL / A SPIDER / I DON'T KNOW
```text
> A PARTRIDGE:
APELLIKON: A partridge. Yes. Low, quick, brown, and alive.

APELLIKON: Birds, then. I was right. I'm always right about shelves.

{PLAYER} received Daedalus's page V!

APELLIKON: It says “bronze bell” in the margin, and “he lies down”.

APELLIKON: Whatever lies down for a bell, I don't want to meet it.

> AN OWL:
APELLIKON: The owl is under Birds, I grant you. But it's Athena's.

APELLIKON: The plaque on the rock's south wall. Read it, and come back.

> A SPIDER:
APELLIKON: That's Arachne. Weaving, not Birds. Two shelves down.

APELLIKON: The plaque on the rock's south wall. Read it, and come back.

> I DON'T KNOW:

APELLIKON: There's an old plaque by the Asclepeion's garden. Come back.

[Give `ITEM_DAEDALUS_PAGE_5`; set `FLAG_ICHOR_DAEDALUS_PAGE_5` (in `FLAG_ICHOR_PAGES_START`'s range). The answer needs no flag: anyone who knows the myth can answer. The plaque itself is in Part 2, on the city map.]

**The Pandora amphora** (SYSTEMS.md §5, amphora #7). A painted jar stands on a plinth by the courtyard door, cracked and mended. A scholar copies it:
```text
SCHOLAR: Pandora's jar. Not a box, whatever the sailors say. A pithos.

SCHOLAR: Everything flew out. Disease, toil, grief. Then she shut the lid.

SCHOLAR: One thing stayed in. Hope. Elpis.

SCHOLAR: We argue whether that was mercy or the cruelest one of all.
```
Daphne, from her table, if the player talks to her again:
```text
DAPHNE: Elpis. Phaedon named her. I told him it was a lovely name.

DAPHNE: And a heavy one, for something so small.

DAPHNE: He said she'd carry it. She does. She carries him, mostly.
```
**Leaving the Library** with `FLAG_ICHOR_LIBRARY_DAPHNE` set runs beat 52.

**Design notes.**
- STORY.md II-9 names three things here: Daphne unwriting her book, page V, and amphora #7. "Every place wrong" makes her unwriting a deed, not a mood.
- "I wrote the door" is a seed for Kaldera (beat 62), where she sees the forge and gets the door wrong.

## Beat 52. The Stoa of the Archon: the hearing

Per STORY.md §3, II-10 (its first half).

**Setup.** As the player steps out of the Library, Kerykos runs past across the square with his staff up.
```text
KERYKOS: TO THE STOA! A petition is heard! Citizens to the Stoa!

```text

> NOT LIKE THAT:

**Design notes.**
- The Keeper's proof is made out of the truth: her own comparison notes. It is the act's argument in one move. A better story is built from real pieces.
- The tic and the ink-dark hand are given to the player and to Alethea, and nobody says them aloud. Alethea names the forger by the hook at the Akropolis gate (beat 55), as STORY.md has it.
- The Archon says only "So be it." here. His STORY.md lines are saved for the urn.
- The hearing needs no tablets. Each tablet the player brings adds a box and changes nothing, which is the point: evidence doesn't win this one. All eight matter later, at the trial after the climax (STORY.md L-2).

## Beat 53. The Ostracism

Per STORY.md §3, II-10, and §6.5's staging exactly.

**Setup.** The next time the player enters the Agora after `FLAG_ICHOR_STOA_HEARING` (the script advances the story to noon; the day's tint is set to day). The square is drawn full of citizens in the metatiles around a wooden fence. Inside it stands a great clay urn. Kerykos stands on the herald's stone beside a wooden board on a post. The Keeper stands by the urn with a tablet. The Archon sits on a stool by the Stoa's steps. Alethea stands alone at the fence's gate. The six named voters wait in a line: Euthyphron, Xanthippe, Kritios, Praxagora, Kephalos and Lysimachos. Phaedon is not here.

Play `MUS_ICHOR_OSTRACISM`: a dry frame-drum pulse, nothing else.
```text
KERYKOS: Citizens of Astyra! Each of you, one shard. One name.

KERYKOS: Six thousand shards, or no one goes.

KERYKOS: Write the name of the one the city no longer wants.
```
[One by one, the six walk to the urn, hold up a shard, and drop it in. Each drop is a clay-clink SE. Each says one line on the way, then walks back.]
```text
EUTHYPHRON: For the golden age. And the truth, which is ours.

XANTHIPPE: Everyone says she lies. Everyone can't be wrong.

KRITIOS: I carve what the city wants. Today it wants this.

PRAXAGORA: My boy's in a helmet because nobody tells the truth.

PRAXAGORA: They say she's one of the ones who don't.

KEPHALOS: …I'm sorry. I'm told it's for the best.

LYSIMACHOS: Same as always.
```
[Lysimachos's shard turns as it falls. It reads ARISTEIDES.]

**The farmer.** An old man in a straw hat, from outside the walls, tugs the player's sleeve. In Plutarch, a farmer who couldn't write asked Aristeides himself to scratch a name on his shard.
```text
FARMER: You, with the young eyes. Can you write?

FARMER: I can't. Scratch a name on this for me. “Alethea.”

FARMER: Never met her. Everyone says she lies. I came in for the vote.
```
?? Multichoice: WRITE “ALETHEA” / WRITE YOUR OWN NAME / SAY NO
```text
> WRITE “ALETHEA”:
FARMER: Good. Thank you. Who is she, anyway?

[He drops it in. Clink.]

> WRITE YOUR OWN NAME:
[The player scratches {PLAYER} on the shard. The farmer can't read it.]

FARMER: Good. That's the one. Thank you.

[He drops it in. Clink. Set `FLAG_ICHOR_WROTE_OWN_NAME`.]

> SAY NO:
FARMER: Fine. I'll find someone who can spell. Takes all sorts.
```
[On the Stoa's steps the Archon watches the farmer's shard all the way into the urn. He doesn't move.]

**The count.** The drum stops. Clerks tip the urn and sort the shards on a cloth. The board on the post is shown as a sign window, three times, with Kerykos calling each one.
```text
KERYKOS: The count!

ALETHEA, 1,204
```
```text
KERYKOS: …The count.

ALETHEA, 3,977
```
```text
KERYKOS: The count.

ALETHEA, 6,000+. Others: 389.
```
[Hold 60 frames, no text. Kerykos lowers his staff.]
```text
KERYKOS: Six thousand. That's the quorum.

KERYKOS: I only read them. I don't have to like them.
```
**The decree.** The Keeper steps up beside the urn and reads from his tablet.
```text
KEEPER LYKOPHRON: “By the vote of the people of Astyra,

KEEPER LYKOPHRON: “Alethea of Kalliste is sent out of the city for ten years.

KEEPER LYKOPHRON: “She may not pass the walls. She may keep what she owns.

KEEPER LYKOPHRON: “She will be gone by sunset.” Sealed by the Archon.
```
[He hands Alethea the decree. Show it close up as a picture window, 64×64: a wax tablet in a neat hand, the Archon's owl seal pressed into the wax at the bottom, and under the seal, small and perfect, a little hook. Play nothing at all.]

[Alethea looks at the decree. Hold 90 frames, no text.]
```text
ALETHEA: They believed the better story.
```
[The Archon stands. He speaks to the square, not to her.]
```text
ARCHON: The people have voted. It is written.
```
[He turns to go. Then he stops beside the player and looks at them, too long. Hold 45 frames.]
```text
ARCHON: You're from Kalliste.

ARCHON: …Hm.
```
[He goes into the Stoa. Two ARCHERs walk Alethea out of the square toward the Dipylon and are hidden. The crowd disperses. Play Alethea's theme (`MUS_ICHOR_ALETHEA`), once, alone, on a lyre, then return to `MUS_ICHOR_ASTYRA`. Set `FLAG_ICHOR_OSTRACISM_DONE`. Hide Alethea in the city for good (`FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_ALETHEA_ASTYRA`).]

**Kerykos, afterwards:**
```text
KERYKOS: I've read nine of these. In my life. Nine.

KERYKOS: I've never once read one for someone who didn't want to be Archon.

KERYKOS: She went out by the Dipylon. The cemetery road. Go on.
```
**Phaedon,** at the Asclepeion, if the player goes there before the Kerameikos:
```text
PHAEDON: I heard. I don't vote. I'm a healer. I don't cut anyone out.

PHAEDON: The Keeper says she forged them. He'd know. He knows everyone's.

PHAEDON: …I'm sorry. I know she's your friend.
```
**Daphne,** at the Library:
```text
DAPHNE: I heard the drum from here. I couldn't make myself go.

DAPHNE: They voted on the story. Not on her. They never met her.

DAPHNE: At their age, I'd have done the same. That's what frightens me.

DAPHNE: Go after her. I'll be here. Writing the wrong places.
```
**Design notes.**
- §6.5's staging is followed exactly: six named NPCs to the urn, three updates of the board, the decree's close-up, 90 frames of silence, then the line. The 6,000 was the real quorum.
- Every voter is someone the player meets in the city (Part 2), and each has a reason that sounds reasonable. Kephalos, who feeds everyone, votes too. That is what an ostracism was.
- Lysimachos's shard among the 389 is his running joke (SYSTEMS.md §5), and in hindsight the Archon's father telling the truth about his son in the only way he can.
- The farmer is Plutarch's. Writing your own name echoes Aristeides, who wrote his own name on that farmer's shard. The Archon's long look gains a second reason if the player did it, and nothing in the text says so.
- Phaedon doesn't vote. "I don't cut anyone out" is true, and the word "cut" is the Cutter's.

## Beat 57. The salt well: Poseidon's Conch

**Setup.** The first entry into `MAP_ASTYRA_AKROPOLIS` by day after `FLAG_ICHOR_AFTER_RAID`. The rock is open; the Propylaia is unguarded. The olive lies across the Old Temple's court, its roots in the air, the split under it full of rubble. Alethea sits on the trunk. An old caretaker in a sea-blue cloak, Boutes, waits by the Erechtheion's north porch.
```text
ALETHEA: You came back. Good. I didn't sleep. The owls are very loud.

ALETHEA: Boutes wants to show us something. He's been waiting since dawn.

BOUTES: I keep the porch. My family has kept it since there was a porch.

BOUTES: Look here, at the floor. And up, at the roof.
```
[Under the porch roof a square hole opens to the sky. Directly beneath it, three deep marks are cut into the rock floor, side by side.]
```text
BOUTES: Three marks. A trident's. Poseidon struck the rock here.

BOUTES: When he and Athena quarreled over who'd have the city.

BOUTES: Athena gave an olive. Poseidon gave a spring. Salt water.

BOUTES: The city chose the olive. Last night they tore it up.

BOUTES: …And this morning the sea is roaring under the floor.
```
[A roar comes up through the marks, and a puff of spray. Hold 40 frames.]
```text
BOUTES: It does that when the south wind blows. It's blowing now.

BOUTES: There's a stair. Nobody goes down. I'm too old to argue.

ALETHEA: The sea is under the Akropolis. Technically, it's not the city.

ALETHEA: Technically, I'm allowed.
```
[A grate in the porch floor lifts on its hinge. Set `FLAG_ICHOR_SALT_WELL_OPEN`. Alethea travels with the player through the well; she is shown as an object at fixed points (Part 5) and comments, but doesn't battle.]

**Boutes, after the dungeon is open:**
```text
BOUTES: The tree came up with a stone in its roots. Green. Leaf-shaped.

BOUTES: Athena's, I'd say. She'd want it used for growing things.

{PLAYER} received a Leaf Stone!
```
[`FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_LEAF_STONE`. A Leaf Stone evolves Elapling into Hierolive, Daphne's own olive.]

**The bottom of the well** (`MAP_SALT_WELL_B1F`). Past the last pool, a sea-door opens in the rock: a natural arch, and beyond it daylight on water. A deep pool lies under it, very still. When the player steps to its edge:

[The water humps. A dolphin surfaces, sleek and gray, with a white spiral conch held crosswise in its mouth. It looks at the player with one eye.]

[It says nothing. It swims to the edge, lifts its head, and nudges the shell into the player's hands. Hold 40 frames.]
```text
{PLAYER} received Poseidon's Conch!

A sea-shell, white and spiraled, cold from the deep.

Hold it to your ear: the sea, and something under the sea, listening.
```
[Give `ITEM_POSEIDONS_CONCH` with the item-get icon. Set `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_POSEIDONS_CONCH`. Place **Delphinus** (SYSTEMS.md §8): the Star Chart's chime, then one line.]

A new shape glows on your Star Chart: Delphinus, the dolphin.
```

```text
ALETHEA: Poseidon's dolphin. It found him a wife, once. Amphitrite.

ALETHEA: He put it in the sky for that. It's still there. Look.

ALETHEA: Blow the shell by the sea, and it comes. That's how it works.

ALETHEA: The sea-door goes out to Phaleron. The harbor. Daphne's ship.
```
[Alethea doesn't step toward the water. She looks up at a cleft in the rock, where a goat path climbs toward daylight.]
```text
ALETHEA: I'm not coming.

ALETHEA: Not to Kaldera. Not anywhere with a wall round it.

ALETHEA: I can't help you in a city. They'll never let me finish a sentence.

ALETHEA: But there are ruins nobody's read, all over Aethos.

ALETHEA: And somebody should find out who taught the Keeper to write.

ALETHEA: Don't look at me like that. I'm not crying. It's the salt.
```
?? Multichoice: WHERE WILL YOU GO? / COME WITH US
```text
> WHERE WILL YOU GO?:
ALETHEA: Wherever the road goes. I'll write. Badly. But often.

> COME WITH US:
ALETHEA: Ask me again somewhere without walls. I'll say yes.
```
[If the player carries Kephalos's Cloak (Part 2, Kephalos's house):]
```text
ALETHEA: From Kephalos? He voted against me.

ALETHEA: …It's a very good cloak.

[She puts it on. Remove `ITEM_KEPHALOS_CLOAK`; set `FLAG_ICHOR_DELIVERED_CLOAK`.]
```

ALETHEA: Everywhere's outside the walls if you walk far enough.
```
[She climbs the goat path into the light and is gone. Set `FLAG_ICHOR_ALETHEA_LEFT`; hide her everywhere until Kythera (Act III).]

**The ride out.** Facing the dolphin:
```text
The dolphin waits, half out of the water. Ride it out to sea?
```
?? YES/NO (Surf always asks, per SYSTEMS.md §1)
```text
> YES:
{PLAYER} blew Poseidon's Conch. The dolphin dipped its head.
```
[The player mounts the dolphin (the Surf sprite on a dolphin) and rides out under the arch: warp to `MAP_ASTYRA_PHALERON`, the sea off the beach, surfing. Play `MUS_ICHOR_SURF` for the first time. From now on the Conch works on any shore (SYSTEMS.md §1).]

**At Phaleron.** The *Paralos*, the Archon's sacred trireme, lies at the quay with its sail furled, garlanded for the embassy to Delos. Daphne stands at the gangplank. Region D's beat 58 begins when the player speaks to her.

**Design notes.**
- The Conch comes from a dolphin that never speaks, as SYSTEMS.md has it. The only words are the item's and Alethea's.
- Alethea leaves by the one road that isn't the city's: a goat path out of the sea. "Everywhere's outside the walls if you walk far enough" is STORY.md's line, last.
- The Leaf Stone from the olive's roots means Athena's tree, torn out, still grows something: Daphne's own Hierolive, if the player raised an Elaleaf.

## The optional lands: Euboia, Marathon, Sounion and Halai

These lands have no beat numbers (the front matter's rule): nothing in them is required, and each is written as a place in Part 2, with its set pieces in Part 5. They are where Act II's themes turn up without anyone saying them aloud.

| Land | Opens | What it adds to the act |
|---|---|---|
| **Euboia** (Teumessos, Aulis, Chalkis, the Lelantine Road, Amarynthos) | The Mask Laurel; Thyrsa's east gate | Two stones on a hill, a hound that catches everything and a fox nothing can catch, frozen by Zeus because neither could win: the chase Alethea's storm-hound and the Titans' vixen will run in Arkadia, and the Frozen Hour's answer to it. A seer's family who read the price of a wind once and stopped reading threads. A bridge you can only cross when the water agrees. |
| **Route 17 and Marathon** | Reaching Astyra | A mound of names with no titles. A runner's road and a race. A blind keeper whose ancestor saw a bronze giant and "didn't mind" being blind ever after. A battle you can only hear. The harbor for the north Aegean. |
| **Route 18, Halai and Cape Sounion** | Reaching Astyra | Phase 2's salt hamlet, moved here (the director's ruling). Pan's cave, the silver mines that pay for the city's owls, and the cape where a father read his son's fate in a sail and read it wrong. An old man nobody sees come or go fishes off the rock below Poseidon's shrine: Act III's theoxenia, seeded twice. |

**Tuning.** Euboia sits on BALANCE's Arkadia row, so it suits a detour between Thyrsa and the Gulf. Routes 17–18, Marathon, Halai and Sounion sit on the Astyra row.

**What these lands must not do** (the front matter's rules): no reading of the player, nothing about why the hero has no thread, nothing that points at Phaedon or at Mom. Kerinthos's bees hum before a visitor comes, and Epizelos's ancestor went blind and was glad; both are hindsight echoes that read as local color the first time.

## Beat 58. The *Paralos*, and Delos

Per STORY.md §3, the voyage between II-12 and II-13. Daphne sails with you, because she wants to see the Telchines' forge she once wrote about (STORY.md §2, Daphne, arc 5).

**Setup.** The *Paralos* is moored at Phaleron's quay from the start of Act II, garlanded at the stern, with a hoplite at the gangplank: "The *Paralos* sails for Delos with the sacred embassy. Passengers by the Archon's leave only." The trierarch, Peisias, takes passengers once `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_POSEIDONS_CONCH` is set: the Archon's office has emptied the ship of everyone but the embassy since the raid, and an exile's friend on board is no one's business. Daphne waits on the quay with a cloth bag, already pale.

```text
DAPHNE: There you are. I'm coming with you.

DAPHNE: There's a forge on Kaldera I wrote a whole chapter about.

DAPHNE: I've never seen it. I wrote it from a sailor's description.

DAPHNE: Also, I don't want to be in this city tonight. Not after this morning.

DAPHNE: Don't tell Elpis I left. Phaedon will say I've gone to buy figs.

PEISIAS: The Professor's friend? Good. Up you come. Mind the garlands.

PEISIAS: Round Sounion, then east to Delos with the embassy.

PEISIAS: Then the tribute round, south past your Kalliste to Thera.

PEISIAS: Every island owes the Archon something.

PEISIAS: Thera owes him pumice and complaints.
```
?? Board the *Paralos*? YES/NO
```text
> YES:
PEISIAS: Cast off! Gently. We carry the god's own people this trip.

> NO:
PEISIAS: We sail when the omens are good. They're good all day. Take your time.
```
[YES: fade out, warp to `MAP_PARALOS_DECK`. Set `FLAG_ICHOR_BOARDED_PARALOS`. Play `MUS_ICHOR_TRIREME`'s hymn variant (Part 9).]

**The deck.** `MAP_PARALOS_DECK` is a trireme like the *Euploia* but older and finer: a painted eye at the bow, garlands of laurel along the rails, a bronze tripod lashed amidships for Apollo, and a chorus of boys rehearsing round it under the envoy Nikias. Daphne sits on a coil of rope by the stern with her head in her hands. The player can fish from the rail (Part 4) and battle two crewmen (Part 3).

**Daphne at sea**
```text
DAPHNE: Thirteen years on an island. Now I can't get off boats.

DAPHNE: The sandals don't help. Nothing helps at sea.

DAPHNE: Talk to me about something solid. Rocks. Tell me about rocks.
```
**Nikias, the envoy** (with the chorus boys)
```text
NIKIAS: Again! From the turn! Boys, you are cranes, not ducks!

NIKIAS: I'm the Archon's envoy to Delos. I take the city's hymn to Apollo.

NIKIAS: And while this ship is away, no one in Astyra may be put to death.

NIKIAS: That's the law. It's older than the Archons. Older than the walls.

NIKIAS: So we sail slowly. Some years, very slowly.

> after:
NIKIAS: Theseus danced this dance on Delos, out of the Labyrinth.

NIKIAS: My boys dance it like they're still in it.
```
**Daphne, after Nikias**
```text
DAPHNE: No one dies while the ship's away. Hm.

DAPHNE: Then let's take the long way.
```
[Talking to Peisias at the stern moves the voyage on: "PEISIAS: Round the cape, and Delos by noon. Everyone, decently dressed. Apollo's particular." Fade. The ship sails Route 3 (sea) round Cape Sounion and Route 2 (sea) east, both Act I's lanes, by the scripted voyage, as the *Euploia* sailed them. Warp to `MAP_DELOS` (`MAPSEC_DELOS`), the sacred harbor. Set `FLAG_ICHOR_VISITED_DELOS`. The region map gates Delos by the Conch, which the player holds by now, so from here on they can also surf to it from Route 2.]

**Delos.** The island where Apollo and Artemis were born: a low granite island with one hill, Kynthos, a sacred harbor, a round dry lake, a terrace of marble lions facing it, an old palm walled round with stones, the temples, and an altar built entirely of horns. The merchants' quarter by the harbor is busy and loud. There is no grave anywhere on the island. Play `MUS_ICHOR_DELOS`. Daphne walks off the gangplank and sits straight down on the quay.
```text
DAPHNE: Solid. Thank you, Apollo. Thank you, whoever.

DAPHNE: Go on. Look around. I'll be here, being grateful to a rock.
```
**The law.** The high priest Anios stands at the head of the sacred way, greeting the embassy. Talking to him plays this once:
```text
ANIOS: Welcome to Delos. Be careful where you're born.

ANIOS: That's a joke. It's also the law.

ANIOS: No one may be born on Delos. No one may die here.

ANIOS: When a woman's time comes, we row her across to Rheneia.

ANIOS: When an old man's time comes, the same boat. It's half an hour.

ANIOS: The island's been clean since the god was born. Nothing begins here.

ANIOS: Nothing ends.

ANIOS: Pilgrims say they feel lighter. Their thread goes slack, they say.

ANIOS: Like a rope that's been let out. It can't end here, so it stops pulling.

ANIOS: Most of them weep. It's the first time it's stopped pulling in years.
```
[Anios turns to look at the player. Hold 60 frames.]
```text
ANIOS: …You don't feel it, do you.

ANIOS: Nothing at all. You look like you're waiting for a boat.

ANIOS: Hm. Apollo keeps odd guests.
```
[Anios walks back to the embassy. Daphne has come up behind the player.]
```text
DAPHNE: There's nothing on you for it to let go of.
```
[She says nothing more about it. Set `FLAG_ICHOR_DELOS_ANIOS`.]

**The altar of horns.** A girl from Nikias's chorus is practicing alone at the Keraton, the altar built of goats' left horns. The light Labyrinth seed: she shows two steps and no more.
```text
DANCER: It's the crane dance. Theseus danced it here, round the horns.

DANCER: He'd just come out of the Labyrinth. So he knew the way.

DANCER: Watch. You go in toward the horns. Left, and left.

DANCER: Then you turn back on yourself, like a thread round a spool.

DANCER: The rest goes in and in. I always get lost in the middle.

DANCER: Master Nikias says the middle is the point.
```
[She gives a Pretty Feather once: "DANCER: Here. A crane's. It fell off the costume." `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_DELOS_FEATHER`.]

**Leto's palm** (an object, walled round with stones)
```text
An old palm, walled in stone. Leto held it when the twins were born.

The island floated, once. It stopped for her.
```
**The Terrace of the Lions** (objects)
```text
A row of marble lions, mouths open, facing the empty lake.

They've been guarding it so long they've forgotten what from.
```
**The round lake**
```text
A round lake bed, dry and cracked. The swans that circled it are gone.

A priest has left a bowl of water at its edge, just in case.
```
[The player is free on Delos: the households and Mount Kynthos are in Part 2. Talking to Daphne on the quay, or to Peisias at the gangplank, sails on: "PEISIAS: Thera by morning, if Poseidon's kind. Aboard?" ?? YES/NO. YES: fade, warp to `MAP_PARALOS_DECK` for beat 59.]

**Design note.** Delos is the one place in Aethos where everyone else's thread goes slack. The player feels nothing, because nothing is there. Anios notices; Daphne, who knows, says one line. Nobody explains it further, and nobody says "thread" about the player in any other way.

**Design note.** The dark ship is the Titans' night crossing to Kalliste. Nothing here says so, and no one learns it until the letter (beat 65), when a player who remembers this night will understand. Daphne's squid is her own small lie, and she doesn't believe it either.

## Beat 61. The Temple of Hephaestus

The rite is in Part 5 (the Bronze Servants); the acolytes are in Part 3. This beat is the entrance, Talos, and the laurel.

**The entrance.** Talos's apprentice, Kalamis, stands inside the door by a rack of tools and a bronze lever.
```text
KALAMIS: Mind your feet! The servants don't stop for anyone.

KALAMIS: Not for the Master. Not for the mayor. Not for goats.

KALAMIS: The Master's up on the forge floor. You get there through the servants.

KALAMIS: They walk where they're told. Turn the dials, and they're told.

KALAMIS: Get each one standing on its plate, and the next door opens.

KALAMIS: If you get them tangled, pull this lever. They'll all walk home.
```
**Daphne,** in the first hall, watching a servant go round:
```text
DAPHNE: Hephaestus built golden maids to help him in his forge. Homer says so.

DAPHNE: I thought it was poetry. It's worse. It's engineering.
```
[Daphne stays by the entrance until beat 62.]

**Talos** waits at the great anvil on the raised forge floor, hammering, with his back to you. He is broad and quiet, in a scorched leather apron, his forearms marked with old burns. He doesn't turn until the third servant is on its plate.

TALOS: You put things where they're needed. That's all smithing is.

TALOS: I'm Talos. The Hierophant. I'd rather be the smith.

TALOS: Hephaestus is a god who limps. He doesn't like fast talkers.

TALOS: Neither do I. Show me with your hands.
```

## Beat 63. Nea Kameni

Per STORY.md §6.7. `MAP_KALDERA_NEA_KAMENI` is the black islet in the middle of the caldera's lagoon: a cone of black lava and cinders, steaming vents, a crater rim, and on its north shore the Titans' camp, tents and a dark trireme moored with no flag. The climb from the landing to the rim passes two Titanborn and the slice's two grunts (Part 3).

**The climb.** [On landing. Ash falls lightly. `WEATHER_VOLCANIC_ASH`.]

AMATHOS: You keep turning up. Like a cough.

HYPERION: You know why I love it? It's never dark. The mountain's always burning.

HYPERION: Kapnub! All of you. Wake it up.

The lava-channel metatiles on the cone begin their animation and start to flow, and from here the screen shakes once every 60 frames until the battle ends.]

HYPERION: That'll cover our boat. And it's the best light in Aethos.

HYPERION: Come on, kid! Fight me in the glare!

As he sends out his ace, the screen fades to white and back in 8 frames: the glare (STORY.md §6.7). A normal battle: a loss whites out to Kaldera's Asclepeion, and on return the rim scene starts again from "There you are." with the eruption already running. Defeat text:]
```text
HYPERION: HA! Good! Even in the light! Who ARE you?
```
[After the battle. A lava channel breaks toward the path where Petros and Amathos stand with the shard.]
```text
HYPERION: Petros! Behind me!
```
[Hyperion steps between his grunts and the lava, arms out. The flow parts round the rock he stands on. Petros and Amathos scramble down the cone with the shard and are hidden.]

The shakes stop. The lava channels slow and cool to black (swap to the cooled metatiles). The ash stops falling. The red tint lifts over 30 frames. Set `FLAG_ICHOR_HYPERION_2_DONE` and `FLAG_ICHOR_ERUPTION_DONE`.]

**Design note.** Hyperion fights where he can see: in the glare of his own eruption. "Petros! Behind me!" is STORY.md's line, and the act of a man who calls his crews his kids. He doesn't know why the Titans want the player, and says so. Talos has told the player already.

## The open Aegean, after the Conch (optional)

The open Aegean has no story beats. Its seven islands and two sea routes are places to explore (Part 2), each with one activity of its own (Part 5), opened by Poseidon's Conch at beat 57 and tuned for Act III. Nothing in them touches the main story's flags, and no main character appears there. The one thread they share with the story is small and deliberate: on the Titan supply islet off Euboia, a water cask has "KNOSSA" written on it and scratched out.

# Part 2. NPC rosters

Lines are listed by condition, earliest first; a later condition replaces earlier lines. Unnamed NPCs are fine as roles. Walker sprites are in Part 10. Per MAP_DESIGN §2, every door opens onto a home with someone in it and something happening, and no two rooms share a layout; each town starts with a table of its buildings.

## Route 6, the Eleutherai Road (`MAP_ROUTE6_ELEUTHERAI_ROAD`)

`MAPSEC_AETHOS_ROUTE_6`. Per the revised `design/AETHOS_MAP.md`, Route 6 runs from Eleusa to Mt. Kithairon; the vines stay at its south end.

**Layout.** About 56×28 tiles. The road leaves Eleusa's north edge through the cut vines, then climbs the terraced foothills of Kithairon in long zigzags: east along a terrace of vine rows, up a stair of terraces, west again, then north into scrub oak to the north edge near the east side. Every terrace is walled with dry stone. Vines on trellises, a few old olives, a stone wine press with its treading floor, a wine-cart with a broken wheel. Up on the north skyline, the towers of Eleutherai on their rock. Halfway, a spur runs east along the hillside to the mouth of Antiope's cave.

**Rhythm:** the vines and the herald (beat 26); Ikarios among the vine rows (first trainer, in plain view); a forced band of grass between two terrace walls, 3 deep; the terrace stair with ledges; Pythodoros at the gap in the wall where the road turns west; the great herm at the spur fork; a second forced band, 4 deep, right after Pythodoros's gap (he faces it, so there's no healing between him and the grass); the wine-cart; Astylos at the cutting below the fort; the fort in view.

**Ledges.** The terraces drop south, back toward Eleusa: three one-way ledges along the zigzag let a player hop home in a few steps, and they make a loop round Botrys's vine rows.

**The spur** (optional): a goat path east along the hillside through optional grass (the route's densest), past Botrys, to Antiope's cave, a dark cave (Hecate's Torch). A visible Super Potion halfway along.

**Relic gates you can see:**
- A fallen column drum from an old roadside shrine (the Girdle of Herakles, beat 34), lying across the steps down to a sunken wine cellar. Through the cellar door, a glint: a visible Max Ether.
- In Antiope's cave, beyond the brazier, marked ivy climbing a rock face to a ledge (Dionysus's Thyrsus, gift II), with an item ball on top.

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Herald | the barrier | beat 26 |
| Alethea | by the vines | beat 26 |
| Vine-dresser | the first terrace | flavor |
| Wine-cart driver | by the broken cart | lore |
| Pilgrims (2) | on the road, walking north | flavor; the Dionysia |
| Ikarios, Pythodoros, Botrys, Astylos | along the road | trainers (Part 3) |

VINE-DRESSER: To a man called Ikarios. He shared the wine with the shepherds.

VINE-DRESSER: They'd never been drunk before. They thought he'd poisoned them.

VINE-DRESSER: It went very badly for Ikarios. Wine's like that. Pour it slowly.
```

PILGRIM: That's either very good or very bad. I can't wait.

## Eleutherai (`MAP_ELEUTHERAI`)

**Layout.** About 32×26. The old border fort, Eleutherai, sits on a crag on the north side: Cyclopean walls with square towers, a gate, and inside the walls a parade ground and the garrison's watch-house. The road runs north past the foot of the crag. Beside the road, the god's roofless old temple with the empty plinth (beat 27). Three houses: the watch-house in the fort, Oinoe's house beside the temple, Lysidike's house among the sheep pens on the south side. A spring with a stone trough. No grass.

**Exits.** South edge: Route 6. North edge: the maenads' pass (`MAP_MT_KITHAIRON`). Eleutherai and the pass are one waypoint, Mt. Kithairon (`MAPSEC_MT_KITHAIRON`). **Identity:** the free town with the empty plinth. It belongs to nobody, and says so.

## Mt. Kithairon (`MAP_MT_KITHAIRON`)

Mt. Kithairon is a waypoint, not a route (`MAPSEC_MT_KITHAIRON`, per the revised `design/AETHOS_MAP.md`). Its section covers two maps: Eleutherai, the fort at the mountain's foot (above), and this one, the maenads' pass. It has grass, trainers and a desecrated shrine, as a mountain should, but no great herm: the herm for this stretch stands on Route 7.

**Layout.** About 40×44, climbing north. The road leaves Eleutherai, switchbacks up through fir forest to a pass between two rocky shoulders, and crosses a high meadow with the shepherds' fold. At the north edge the pass opens onto the mountain's north face, which is Route 7. Tree lines are thick black firs mixed with oak and wild pear, staggered 3–4 deep, with grey rock showing through. Ivy over everything near the top.

**Rhythm:** the first switchbacks (calm, a view south over the vine terraces); Lykidas the goatherd in plain view on the bend; a forced band in a fir clearing, 4 deep, walled by fir trunks and a rock face; the maenads' dancing floor (beat 28) with Euia across its only exit and Bromia off to one side; the pass fork, with the boundary stone as its sign; Pentheus's fir; the shepherds' fold (the rest point); the ivy shrine, desecrated, with its guard, Ilys, on a side ledge; the pass's north lip, with Thyrsa's walls and the camp's smoke in view far below.

**Ledges.** The road climbs, so the ledges along the switchbacks drop south toward Eleutherai: the way home is quick.

**The pass fork:** east, a side path through optional grass to Aktaion's spring (a dead end that pays: a hidden Pretty Feather and a fixed dig); north, the road on.

**Relic gates you can see:**
- **The Girdle of Herakles:** a toppled boundary drum (an old Plataean boundary shrine's column, fallen across a ledge path west of the fold), blocking a crag with a visible Max Revive.
- **Dionysus's Thyrsus** (gift II): a rock wall above the dancing floor, thick with marked ivy, leading to a high ledge with a visible Max Elixir.

**The spring path** (optional) holds the pass's TM, Venoshock, at the far side of the optional grass.

**Landmarks** (objects):
```text
[Pentheus's fir]
An enormous fir. One great branch is torn away, high up.

They say King Pentheus climbed it to spy on the maenads.

The maenads saw him. That's the end of that story.

[Aktaion's spring]
A clear pool under the firs. A rock beside it, worn smooth, like a seat.

Scratched in the rock: TURN YOUR EYES AWAY. SHE BATHES HERE.

[An arrow, stuck in a fir by the spring]
An arrow with silver fletching, driven deep into the bark.

Silver is the Huntress's. Somebody was hunting here, from a long way south.

[The boundary stone at the pass fork]
A worn boundary stone. One side says THYRSA. The other side says THYRSA.

Someone has scratched out one of them and written ELEUTHERAI. Twice.

North: down to Thyrsa. East: the spring. South: Eleutherai.
```

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Phorbas | the shepherds' fold | rest point and lore (beat 28) |
| Maenads (5, then 2) | the dancing floor | beat 28; Euia and Bromia battle |
| Lykidas, Euia, Bromia, Arimnestos, Ilys | along the road | trainers (Part 3) |

**The ivy shrine, desecrated** (per SYSTEMS.md §3, desecrated altars). A small rock shrine of Dionysus, ivy carved round a niche with a cup in it. A sickle is scratched across the cup. Ilys stands beside it (Part 3). Before Ilys is beaten:

Someone has scratched a sickle across the cup.

After Ilys, the altar menu offers PRAY; the first prayer cleanses it (+3 Dionysus Favor, `FLAG_ICHOR_ALTAR_CLEANSED_KITHAIRON`):

When it's still again, the scratches are gone. The cup smells faintly of wine.

South: Eleutherai. North: over the pass, down to Thyrsa.

[At the fold]
PHORBAS'S FOLD. Milk for the tired. Mind the dogs. There are no dogs.

## Route 7, the Kronia grounds (`MAP_ROUTE7_KRONIA_GROUNDS`)

`MAPSEC_AETHOS_ROUTE_7`. Per the revised `design/AETHOS_MAP.md`, Route 7 "descends past the Kronia grounds, a Titan feast camp, to Thyrsa". It is a full route: forced grass, checkpoints, a herm and signs, with the camp as its set piece.

**Layout.** About 40×56, descending north. Two halves:
1. **The north face** (the south half of the map): the road leaves Kithairon's pass and drops in long switchbacks down the mountain's north face, through firs thinning to oak scrub and then to pasture. The narrow defile under the north shoulder is the route's first checkpoint. Below it, Thyrsa's walls and the camp's smoke are in view the whole way down.
2. **The Asopos meadow** (the north half): the road runs straight north through the middle of the Kronia camp to the Elektran Gate in Thyrsa's wall, drawn along the north edge. The camp fills the meadow: long trestle tables under striped awnings on both sides of the road, the great domed bread oven, the Kronist stage hung with gold cloth, a ring of tents, the steward's big tent behind the stage, children's hoops, a painted banner (beat 29). The river Asopos runs along the east side, with reeds, a little sandy beach, and a reed islet in midstream.

**Rhythm:** the pass's north lip; Komos the satyr in the defile (mandatory, facing up the road), with a forced band of grass, 4 deep, directly below him, walled by the defile's rock; the switchbacks; Hagnon the pilgrim at the last switchback (mandatory), with a second forced band, 3 deep, in the pasture right after his bend, fenced by a dry-stone wall and the scrub; the great herm at the foot of the mountain, where a side path leaves east to the river; the camp (the greeting, the tables, the reader, the stage: beat 29); the gate.

**Ledges.** This is a descent, so the switchbacks' terrace ledges drop north, downhill, toward Thyrsa. The way down is quick and the way back up to Kithairon is the long road. MAP_DESIGN §1 wants ledges to drop toward the previous town; a mountain's north face can only drop one way (region A's open questions).

**Optional grass:** the riverbank meadow east of the camp and the beach path, with a reason to go in: the herm's side path ends at the beach, with a hidden Bronze Obol in the reeds and the Conch gate in view. The camp itself and the road through it have no grass.

**The tables.** Four Titanborn sit at the tables off duty, helmets pushed back, eating. Each will battle "for fun, it's a feast!" if asked: they don't stop the player, and none faces the road. They are STORY.md §5's archetypes (Part 3). The route's checkpoints are Komos and Hagnon, on the mountain; the camp is the place where nobody stops you.

**Relic gates you can see:**
- **Poseidon's Conch:** the reed islet in the Asopos, with an item ball on it (Big Pearl, a sea gift for Poseidon's altar).

**The great herm,** at the mountain's foot, at the fork to the river:
```text
A great herm at the mountain's foot, hung with fresh ivy. Someone left it bread.

North: the feast, and Thyrsa. East: the river. South: up Kithairon.
```
Anointing it sets `FLAG_ICHOR_HERM_ROUTE7`.

**Lost pilgrim** (on the north face, below the defile)
```text
PILGRIM: I followed the maenads up. I wanted to see the god.

PILGRIM: I danced all night. I don't remember where I put my sandals.

PILGRIM: I think I saw him. I think he was the one with the sandals.
```

**The Kronia's calendar day** (per SYSTEMS.md §7, Skirophorion's festival). On the Kronia itself, the grounds hold their great feast: garlands on every tent, the music doubled, the greeter's bread doubled (two Barley Cakes), and the Kronist's sermon replaced by the feast-day speech below. The day is flavor before the climax; SYSTEMS.md's Time Fractures ride it after.
```text
KRONIST: Today is Kronos's day, friends! The one day the old world remembers!

KRONIST: Look around you. Master and servant. Rich and poor. One table.

KRONIST: Soon it won't be one day a year. It'll be one day forever.

KRONIST: One day, and no tomorrow to spoil it. Eat!
```

## Thyrsa City (`MAP_THYRSA_CITY`)

**Layout.** About 56×48. A walled city on a long hill, with seven gates drawn in its walls; three of them open. The **Elektran Gate** in the south wall is the main entrance, from Route 7 and the Kronia grounds. The **Neistan Gate** in the west wall opens onto Route 8, the Kopais shore, once the Girdle shifts the drum fallen in its gateway (below). The **Proitid Gate** in the east wall opens onto the road to the Euripus and Euboia (optional; region E1). The other four are drawn shut, their arches bricked or barred, so the walls read as Thyrsa's famous seven. Five districts:
1. **The lower town**, inside the Elektran Gate. The **Asclepeion** stands on the left of the gate road, built round the spring of Dirke, its fountain house in front. The **Agora**, under striped awnings, is on the right. The Kantharos tavern, Pindaros's house and Eudora's house are in the lanes behind.
2. **The vineyards**, inside the walls along the west side: trellised vine rows (the city's grass), the old wine press, and the lane down to the Neistan Gate. Staphylos's house stands at the vineyards' head.
3. **The east hill**, where the theater's high gate opens off a terrace (a door warp to `MAP_THYRSA_THEATER`). Polos's house and Euthykles's workshop are on the terrace below it.
4. **The Kadmeia**, the old citadel on the hill's top, up a broad stair from the Agora: Manto's house on the citadel wall, Chthonia's house, and Semele's chamber, a roofless ruin wrapped in ivy, smoking faintly from a crack in its floor.
5. **The Temple of Dionysus**, at the head of the main street on the Kadmeia's crest, framed by the street all the way from the Elektran Gate. Its front is a small theater's skene with three painted doors and a pediment of masks. It is the crown.

**Exits.** The Elektran Gate (south, Route 7); the Neistan Gate (west, Route 8: shut for the festival, then blocked by a fallen drum until `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_GIRDLE`); the Proitid Gate (east, toward the Euripus and Euboia, optional); the theater (east hill, by door). **Identity:** the god's city. Ivy on every wall, masks over every door, and the biggest theater in Aethos.

**Relic gates you can see:**
- **The Girdle of Herakles:** the drum fallen in the Neistan Gate (main path, below).
- **Dionysus's Thyrsus** (gift II): marked ivy up the vineyards' old terrace wall, to a ledge over the west wall with a visible Big Nugget.

**The Neistan Gate.** Thyrsa's west gate leads to Route 8 and the long road west. Per the revised map, nobody may leave Thyrsa westward without the Girdle of Herakles: the column drums that block the way into Arkadia lie on Route 11, south of the gulf. The gate shows it in three states.

1. **During the festival** (until `FLAG_ICHOR_DIONYSIA_DONE`), two guards stand across it:
   ```text
   GUARD: Gate's shut for the festival. By the god's order.

   GUARD: Everyone stays for the play. Even the people who'd rather not.

   GUARD: Especially them. They need it most.
   ```
2. **After the Dionysia,** the god's procession carries his image round the walls, and the cart clips the gate's old column. A drum falls across the gateway. The guards stand by it, scratching their heads:
   ```text
   GUARD: The god's cart caught the gate column last night. Brought a drum down.

   GUARD: Six men couldn't shift it. We'd need Herakles. Or his belt.

   GUARD: Silenos has his belt, they say. In the skene. He'd never part with it.

   GUARD: Win it off him, and the gate's yours.
   ```
   The drum, without the Girdle (per SYSTEMS.md §1's wording): "A fallen column drum, wedged in the gateway. A strong back would shift it."
3. **With the Girdle** (`FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_GIRDLE`), the drum is the relic's first use, in a safe place, before Route 11's real blockade:
   ```text
   A fallen column drum, wedged in the gateway.

   Push it with the Girdle of Herakles?
   ```
   ?? YES/NO. YES: the player pushes the drum two tiles to the side, clear of the arch (the boulder push). Set `FLAG_ICHOR_NEISTAN_DRUM_MOVED`. The guards:
   ```text
   GUARD: …Six men. Six! And a child in a big belt.

   GUARD: Gate's open. Off you go, west. Kopais, Lebadeia, the gulf.

   GUARD: Funny play, in the end. I laughed. I think I laughed.

   GUARD: I don't remember the middle.
   ```

**The Proitid Gate** (east; optional). One guard on a stool under the arch:
```text
GUARD: The Euripus road. The bridge to Euboia's at the end of it.

GUARD: The Euripus bridge. It only opens when the current turns.
```
Region E1 writes the road beyond.

**Thyrsa interiors**

Per MAP_DESIGN §2, every door in Thyrsa opens, someone is home, and something happens inside; no two rooms share a layout. Thyrsa has seven households and four public buildings, besides the temple and the theater.

### Asclepeion (`MAP_THYRSA_CITY_ASCLEPEION`)

- **The room:** built round the spring of Dirke. The healing hall is a courtyard roofed with a vine pergola, dappled green, with the spring's basin in the middle and a channel that runs under the counter. The healer works at a counter of carved stone beside the basin. Masks of thank-offering hang from the pergola posts: patients who were actors give a mask when they're well. The statue of Asclepius stands at the basin's head, his staff wound with a serpent and, for Thyrsa, a little ivy.
- **Service:** the Ichor nurse strings. A Panacoil coils round the basin's rim: "PANACOIL: Hss. [It dips its tail in the spring, then flicks water at you. Diagnosis complete.]"

| NPC | Lines |
|---|---|
| Satyr-actor with a bandaged ankle | "Sprained it doing the kordax. The satyrs' dance." / "It's very undignified. That's the point. I'm still proud." |
| Pilgrim with a headache | "Came for the festival. Drank for the festival." / "Now I'm here for the festival's consequences." |
| Young healer | "Dirke's spring. She was a queen who was very cruel to Antiope." / "Her sons tied her to a bull. The gods made her a spring. It's very good for bruises." |

### Agora (`MAP_THYRSA_CITY_AGORA`)

- **The room:** a covered market hall off the square: two long counters at right angles, one for goods and one for offerings and wine, with festival masks pinned along a beam above the wine counter, amphorae stacked in a pyramid, and a chalk board of the day's prices. A grape-treading vat by the back door, empty.
- **Stock:** Part 6.

| NPC | Lines |
|---|---|
| General stallkeeper | the shop |
| Wine-and-offerings stallkeeper | the shop: "Wine for the god? Wine for you? It's the same wine." |
| Mask-seller (during the festival) | "Masks! Comic, tragic, satyr! Be someone else for a night!" / "Masks don't work in battle. Nothing works in battle except battling." |

### The Kantharos, a tavern (`MAP_THYRSA_CITY_TAVERN`)

- **The room:** a cellar tavern down five steps, cool and dim, under a barrel vault. Its namesake, a great two-handled wine cup, hangs over the bar. Benches round a sunken floor where the knucklebones table stands, the stone worn into a shallow bowl. A painted frieze of satyrs chasing maenads round the walls, and the maenads winning.

### Pindaros's house (`MAP_THYRSA_CITY_PINDAROS_HOUSE`)

- **Who:** Pindaros, a poet who writes victory odes for winners at the games, and keeps the old law of hospitality.
- **The room:** an upper room over a courtyard, its walls lined with pigeonholes full of scrolls, each labelled with a victor's name and the year. A writing table by the window, a lyre on a peg, and round the table three dining couches, one of them always made up for a guest. A bronze victor's tripod in the corner, his own, won long ago for a song.
- **Event:** the xenia host (per SYSTEMS.md §10): heal and rest. And a line for every laurel.

The first two lines are SYSTEMS.md's.
```text
PINDAROS: Sit. Eat first.

PINDAROS: Then tell me who you are. Not before.

[heal the party, with the heal jingle]

PINDAROS: Bread, honey, figs. A poet's table. Light on meat, heavy on adjectives.

PINDAROS: Stay, if you like. Rest till you want to wake.
```
[The rest menu (per SYSTEMS.md): DAWN / NOON / DUSK / NIGHT, each shown only if that hour is still ahead today, plus NOT NOW.]

PINDAROS: I write the whole ode when the race is over. Not before.

PINDAROS: Here. A sprig of laurel. A victor's crown starts somewhere.

### Temple of Dionysus (`MAP_THYRSA_CITY_TEMPLE_OF_DIONYSUS`)

The trial is Part 5; Lasos and Thespis are beat 31. The god's old wooden image from Eleutherai stands inside the door, on a low base, for Oinoe's garland (above). The temple's great altar of Dionysus (per SYSTEMS.md §3; offerings count double) stands in the god's orchestra by the door.

## The theater (`MAP_THYRSA_THEATER`)

**Layout.** About 40×34. The great theater cut into the east hill. The cavea is a vast fan of stone tiers, divided by stairs into six blocks of seats, with a walkway halfway up. At the bottom, the orchestra: a full circle of beaten earth with the god's altar, the thymele, at its center. Behind the orchestra, the skene, the stage building, with its three painted doors (left, the comic: ivy; center, the palace: a crown; right, the satyr: a goat), a low stage in front, the parodoi (side passages) at either end, and the god-machine, a wooden crane on the skene's roof. The player enters at the top, through the high gate from Thyrsa's terrace, and walks down. The skene's back door opens into `MAP_THYRSA_THEATER_SKENE`.

**Before the Dionysia.** Workers sweep the tiers and hang garlands. The stage is bare.
```text
WORKER: Seventeen thousand seats. I've swept every one. Twice.

WORKER: You'd think a god's theater would sweep itself. You'd be wrong.

WORKER: The masks are gone, and the play's still on. That's Thespis for you.
```
**During the Dionysia:** beat 32. **After it:** beat 33 (Kleon), then the theater stands empty. A cleaner picks up honey cakes from the tiers.
```text
CLEANER: Best Dionysia in years. Everyone says so. Nobody can tell me why.

CLEANER: Something about the satyrs. And the honey. Who brings honey to a play?
```
The thymele, after the Dionysia: the inky handprint (beat 32). The stage, any time after:
```text
The stage. Three doors: ivy, a crown, a goat.

You could do it again. You'd need an audience.
```
**Hidden item:** under the front row, a **Honey**. Somebody dropped their honey cake, and their honey.

---

## The skene (`MAP_THYRSA_THEATER_SKENE`)

- **The room:** the stage building's back, two parts. **Backstage** is a corridor behind the three doors, with the mask racks (empty pegs until beat 32, then full of Prosomime again), costume rails and a water barrel. **The prop room**, through an arch, is Silenos's kingdom: costume chests, a lion skin with the head still on (Herakles's, a costume, mostly), a painted wooden sickle, a gold mask with closed eyes, a crown of stars on cork, the god-machine's winch with its rope and hook coming down through a hatch, and a wine jar that is never empty.
- **Who:** Silenos (beat 34), Thespis (beat 32 only), a stagehand.
- **Events:** Silenos's contest (beat 34); the Prosomime statics (Part 4).

[A painted wooden sickle]
A painted wooden sickle. It's much lighter than it looked on stage.

[A gold mask]

[The lion skin]

```

## Route 8, the Kopais Shore (`MAP_ROUTE8_KOPAIS`)

`MAPSEC_AETHOS_ROUTE_8`. Thyrsa's Neistan Gate opens onto it once the player holds the Girdle (region A).

**Layout.** About 64×26 tiles, west from Thyrsa's Neistan Gate along the south shore of Lake Kopais, a great marsh lake. The lake fills the north edge: open water, then a broad band of reed beds, then the road. The south edge is the foot of Mount Phikion, grey rock and scrub, where the Sphinx sat. Halfway, an inlet of the marsh cuts across the road, and the road crosses it on a Minyan dike, a stone causeway built by the people who drained the lake in the age of heroes. Out in the water, the walled islet of Gla. At the west end the road climbs a little into Lebadeia's gorge.

**Rhythm:** the east sign and calm road; Gorgidas the fowler (first trainer, in plain view, easy); **forced reed band 1** (3 deep, the lake on the north and the Phikion cliffs on the south, no way round); the eel-smokers' fire (rest point); the dike, with Ismenias fishing across its whole width (mandatory); **forced reed band 2**, straight off the dike's west end; the great herm at the spur fork; Timoxena in the reeds (optional, facing the water); the Treasury of Minyas, a beehive tomb with a fallen column drum across its door (the Girdle); the Onchestos marker, where Atalanta raced (a daily dig spot beside it); Perses at the narrows between the reeds and a rock wall (mandatory); **forced reed band 3**, 4 deep, under the cliffs; Euphrosyne cutting reeds (optional); the view of Gla; the west sign.

**The reeds are tall grass.** They use the marsh's own tall-grass metatile (taller than meadow grass, with a slow sway) and the lake's encounter table (Part 4). Act II's bands are longer than Act I's: band 3 is four deep.

**Ledges.** The Phikion spur's goat path comes down to the road in three ledges facing east, so the climb is from the herm and the way down drops you back toward Thyrsa: a loop, and a quick way home.

**The Phikion spur** (optional): a goat path up through rocky grass (Part 4's spur table, with the rare Enigmaw by day) to the Sphinx's ledge: a flat rock high over the lake, scattered with old feathers. At the top, a visible Hyper Potion, a daily dig spot, and a sign.

**The Treasury of Minyas** (optional, the Girdle): a beehive tomb's doorway in the hillside south of the road, its lintel cracked, a fallen column drum wedged across it. With the Girdle, push the drum aside. Inside, a round, corbelled stone chamber, dark at the top, with a visible TM Ancient Power and a fixed dig spot (an Ostrakon: "ORCHOMENOS. You know what you did."). The tomb's only light comes in through the door.

**Relic gates you can see:**
- **Gla,** the walled islet, out in the lake: an item ball on its shore and a dig spot inside its broken wall (Poseidon's Conch, later in Act II). Alethea's fourth note points at it.
- The Treasury of Minyas's drum (the Girdle, this act).

## Lebadeia (`MAP_LEBADEIA`)

**Layout.** About 32×28. A hamlet in a narrow gorge where the river Herkyna comes out of the rock. The road from Route 8 enters at the east; the houses stand on either side of the river, joined by two little stone bridges; the road leaves west toward the Split Road. At the west end, under a rock face, the **precinct**: the two springs side by side (Lethe, dark and still; Mnemosyne, bright and running), the stone chair of Mnemosyne between them, the cave mouth behind a bronze grille, and a row of steps where the pilgrims sit after the descent. A grove of tall plane trees shades it all.

`MAPSEC_LEBADEIA`. One of AETHOS_MAP.md's five **healer hamlets**: the pilgrims' hall's keeper heals, the hall is its heal location, and Lebadeia is a fly target once visited (`FLAG_ICHOR_VISITED_LEBADEIA`).

**Buildings.** Three: the pilgrims' hall (the healer), Herkyna's house by the river, and the mason's house. No other house has a door, so no other house is drawn as a house: the rest of the gorge is rock, garden walls and the river. **Identity:** the springs. Everybody here has drunk from both, and nobody can agree on what that did to them.

| Cake-seller | at the bridge | flavor |
