### Asclepeion (`MAP_ASTYRA_ASCLEPEION`)

- **The room:** a mountain Asclepeion built against the rock itself. The back wall is the Akropolis's raw cliff, and a sacred spring rises from a cave mouth in it into a stone basin. A long incubation stoa runs down the east side with pallets where patients sleep and dream their cure. The counter faces the door, with Panacoil round its post. The cold hearth altar stands by the inner door. The Pithos is in a niche in the rock. A painted plaque of a snake round a staff hangs over the spring.
- **Service:** Phaedon (beat 49). Every heal in Astyra is his, and his lines are in Part 1.

| NPC | Lines |
|---|---|
| Patient on a pallet | "I'm to sleep here and dream my cure." / "I keep dreaming about a goat. I don't know what that means." / "The healer says it means I should sleep more." |
| Old soldier by the spring | "Forty years I've known how I die. A fall, the seer said." / "Now it's the same day as everyone. I feel cheated, almost." |
| Young healer | "He's here before dawn and after dark. He never takes a fee from children." / "I asked him once why he doesn't pray. He just said, 'Hold that bandage.'" |

After the raid (beat 56) the stoa's pallets hold guards and one Titanborn; the next morning they are empty and the young healer says: "We patched forty last night. He didn't sit down once."

### The Agora (`MAP_ASTYRA_AGORA`)

- **The room:** the capital's market hall, a two-aisled stoa with stalls down both sides under hanging lamps: a general counter, an offerings counter stacked with oil jars and frankincense cones, and a scroll stall of TMs. Owl coins in bowls on a moneychanger's table by the door.
- **Stock:** Part 6, Shops.

| NPC | Lines |
|---|---|
| General stallkeeper | the shop |
| Offerings seller | the shop. "Frankincense from the far east. Athena likes it. So does my wife." |
| Scroll seller | the shop. "Knowledge, by the scroll. Cheaper than the Lyceum, and you can sit down." |
| Moneychanger | "Owls! Silver owls! Bring me any you dig up. Astyra's own coin." / "Owls to Astyra, they say. Pointless, like bringing sand to the beach. I'll take them anyway." (He buys the Silver Owl at +20%.) |

### The Stoa of the Archon (`MAP_ASTYRA_STOA_OF_THE_ARCHON`)

- **The room:** a long, plain public hall, deliberately poor: stone benches in three tiers on both sides, the laws cut into stone slabs along the back wall, a plain wooden chair for the Archon on a step, and the Keeper's desk before it, with its wax tablets in tidy stacks and an inkpot. A great clay urn waits in a corner for the next vote.
- **Event:** the hearing (beat 52). Afterwards, the Council's clerk keeps the hall.
```text
> before the hearing:
CLERK: The Archon's Stoa. The laws are on the wall. All of them.

CLERK: Some of them are very old. Some of them are very long.

> after the ostracism:
CLERK: The Keeper had the decree copied out twenty times. Very neat.

CLERK: It's on every gate. Here's one, if you like. For the record.
```
[The copy is a sign window: the decree's text, and the hook under the owl.]
```text
> the Keeper's desk, after the ostracism:
The Keeper's desk. Every tablet squared to the edge.

A pot of ink. A stylus, wiped clean. A wax tablet, face down.

You turn it over. It's blank, except for one little hook in the corner.
```
After the raid the desk is empty and the clerk says: "The Keeper's gone to the Archon's house. To advise him. He's very good at advising."

### The Library (`MAP_ASTYRA_LIBRARY`)

- **The room:** a long hall lined from floor to ceiling with square scroll niches, each with a little clay tag; a wheeled ladder; reading tables down the middle under clerestory windows; a courtyard at the far end with a fig tree and a bench. Apellikon's desk by the door holds a magnifying crystal on a stand. Daphne's table is the last one, behind a wall of wax tablets. The Pandora amphora stands by the courtyard door.
- **Event:** beat 51 (Daphne; page V; the Pandora amphora).

| NPC | Lines |
|---|---|
| Apellikon | beat 51; afterwards: "I've read everything in here twice. I'd like a third library." |
| Scholar at the amphora | beat 51 |
| Student asleep on a scroll | "I'm not asleep. I'm reading with my face." |

### The Lyceum (`MAP_ASTYRA_LYCEUM`)

- **The room:** a gymnasium in a grove. A square colonnade, the *peripatos*, runs round a garden of plane trees; on one side a sand palaestra where athletes wrestle; at the head of the walk the altar of Apollo Lykeios with an unlit torch stand. Theophrastos's bench sits under the biggest plane, covered in pressed leaves.
- **Event: the walk.** The Lyceum's philosophers teach walking. Theophrastos invites you to walk the colonnade with his three best: each falls in beside you as you pass and battles you, with no stop to heal between. He waits at the end of the walk. Win all four and he gives the **Leftovers**. Lose, and you may walk again from the start. Part 3 has the trainers.
```text
THEOPHRASTOS: Ah. A walker. You've the legs of someone who walks far.

THEOPHRASTOS: We teach walking here. The mind keeps pace with the feet.

THEOPHRASTOS: Walk my colonnade. My three best will walk with you.

THEOPHRASTOS: They'll argue. Argue back. With Pokémon. It's quicker.

THEOPHRASTOS: No stopping to heal. Thinking doesn't stop to heal.
```
?? YES/NO
```text
> YES:
THEOPHRASTOS: Good. Left foot first. It's traditional. I invented it.

> NO:
THEOPHRASTOS: Sit, then. Sitting's a kind of walking that hasn't started.
```
[On a win over all four:]
```text
THEOPHRASTOS: You walked well. You argued better.

THEOPHRASTOS: Here. Aristotle's reading crystal. He left it to me with the garden.

{PLAYER} received Choice Specs!

THEOPHRASTOS: He said it lets you think about one thing at a time. Fiercely.
```
[`FLAG_ICHOR_LYCEUM_WALK_DONE`, `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_CHOICE_SPECS`.]

**The Panathenaia's torch** (SYSTEMS.md §7; calendar, optional). On the festival's day after the raid, the altar's torch stand is lit, and an athlete offers the relay: carry the flame from the Lyceum's altar to Athena's altar on the Akropolis in 160 steps on Hero (190 Mortal, 140 Spartan), by SYSTEMS.md §2's carried-flame rules. Ichor's Akademia is Daphne's grove on Kalliste, so the relay starts here.
```text
ATHLETE: The Panathenaia! The torch race. Lyceum to the rock.

ATHLETE: Keep the flame lit, and get there before it gutters.
```
[A win gives Olive Oil ×10, "an oil-jar from the city" (`FLAG_DAILY_ICHOR_PANATHENAIA`, once per festival day). Before the raid the rock is shut, and the athlete says: "No race this year. The rock's closed. The flame doesn't know where to go."]

## The Kerameikos (`MAP_ASTYRA_KERAMEIKOS`)

**The arrival.** About 40×30, between Route 16 (the west edge, over the pass from Daphni: region C1) and the Dipylon (the east edge). The Sacred Way from Eleusa ended here, and so does Ichor's: every pilgrim to the capital walks in through its dead. The road runs east along the Eridanos, a little stream in a stone channel, and the Street of Tombs lines it: grave stelai carved with seated women and standing soldiers, marble jars on plinths, a bronze bull on a family plot, and the stele of Hegeso, a woman choosing a necklace from a box her maid holds. The walls and the Dipylon's two towers close the east end, and the Akropolis shows over them from the first screen. North of the road is the potters' quarter that gave the place its name: kilns, clay pits, Brygos's workshop. South of the road, the cemetery's long grass runs among the stones. A gap in the cemetery's south wall leads down to the paupers' graves.

**Rhythm:** in from Route 16 past the first tombs; the grass among the stones beside the road (optional; Kalyptor at night); Proxenos at Hegeso's stele, facing it, off the road; the potters and Brygos; the gravedigger's lodge and the gap to the paupers' graves; the Dipylon, its dry fountain, and the city. The road itself has no grass: this is a town's outskirts, not a route. Every corner pays: a dig spot behind the bull, a visible Revive by Dexileos's monument, a hidden Bronze Obol in an empty grave-jar.

**Relic gates you can see:** a column drum (the Girdle) fallen across a family plot's gate, with a visible item inside, the plot's old offering (the Girdle is the player's since Thyrsa, so this is a reward for noticing).

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Alethea | by the road, at dusk | beat 54 |
| Archer outside the Dipylon | the gate | flavor |
| Brygos | his workshop's yard | Potter (trainer) |
| Proxenos | Hegeso's stele | Pilgrim (trainer) |
| Manes | the gravedigger's lodge | the paupers' graves |
| Mourner | a fresh grave | lore |
| Kiln boy | the kilns | flavor |

ARCHER: Everyone does. The city's that way. Mind the dead. They mind you.

[Mourner, at a fresh grave with a white jar on it]

MOURNER: Everyone said what a good death. Like it was a party she'd planned.

## The Akropolis (`MAP_ASTYRA_AKROPOLIS`)

**Layout.** About 44×36: the flat top of the rock inside its walls. From the west foot, the ramp climbs past the base of a great bronze Athena to the **Propylaia**, the gateway of columns. Beyond it, the Sacred Way runs east up the rock's spine: the **Parthenon** on the right, high on its steps; the **Old Temple's court** on the left, with Athena's olive in the Pandroseion beside the **Erechtheion** and its porch of stone maidens; the Erechtheion's **north porch** at the far side, with the trident marks and, after the raid, the salt well's stair; the **south wall's parapet**, a lookout over the whole city. The old spring stair goes down through a split in the court's floor to the north slope. Weeds and wild grass grow between fallen column drums along the north wall.

**The raid** (beat 55) is staged on this map at night: Part 5 gives the sequence, the placement and the object budget. **After the raid** the rock is open by day: the olive lies across the court with its roots in the air, the split is rubble, and the guards are gone.

**After the raid, what's here:** Athena's great altar (rites); Boutes at the north porch; the priestess of Athena; the stump; the grass between the drums (Glaukoin among the columns, a rare Hierolive by the old temple: Part 4); a column drum on the north side that the Girdle can roll, opening a ledge behind the Parthenon with a visible item; a stargazing seat on the south parapet (SYSTEMS.md §8); a daily dig spot in the Old Temple's foundations.

|---|---|---|
| Boutes | the north porch | the salt well (beat 57); the Leaf Stone |
| Pandrosa | by the stump | the priestess of Athena Polias; Athena's rite and gift I |
| Guard | the Propylaia, after the raid | flavor |
| Alethea | the fallen trunk | beats 55–57 |

**Pandrosa, the priestess of Athena Polias** (after the raid). She keeps the precinct where the olive grew, named for the princess Pandrosos.
```text
PANDROSA: I've watered that tree every morning for thirty years.

PANDROSA: This morning I watered the stump. Habit. Don't laugh.

PANDROSA: Athena takes olive oil. Pour her a little. She's had a bad night.
```
[Athena's altar teaches her rite (SYSTEMS.md §3: she loves Olive Oil). Pandrosa gives one free Olive Oil on the first visit (`FLAG_ICHOR_ATHENA_RITE`). At Athena Favor 30 she hands over **TM Calm Mind**, gift I: "Athena asked me to give you this. She says think before you hit things. Then hit them." (`FLAG_ICHOR_GIFT_ATHENA_I`.) Athena has no temple of her own among the eight; her seat is the Pantheon's, and her great altar is this one, where offerings count double.]

## Phaleron (`MAP_ASTYRA_PHALERON`)

**Layout.** About 36×24: Astyra's old harbor on the open bay, reached by the Phaleric road from the city's south gate (the north edge). A beach of coarse sand with dune grass curves round the bay; a stone quay runs out at its east end, where the *Paralos*, the Archon's sacred trireme, lies garlanded; fishers' huts and Hipponikos's net-loft stand behind the beach; a small harbor shrine of Poseidon sits on the quay's root. At the west end, under the cliff, is the sea-door arch where the salt well comes out. The open sea runs off the south edge into Route 3, Act I's sea route up the Saronic Gulf (surfable with Poseidon's Conch). Offshore, a rock islet holds a visible item: a Conch gate, seen from the beach before the player can reach it.

**Rhythm:** the gate from the city; the dune grass (optional); Euangelos counting ships on the beach; the huts; Konon on the quay; the *Paralos* and Daphne (from beat 57); the shrine.

| Old woman at the shrine | the harbor shrine | lore |

### Hipponikos's net-loft (`MAP_ASTYRA_PHALERON_NET_LOFT`)

- **Who:** Hipponikos, a careful old fisher who reads omens before he'll go out, and his grandson.
- **The room:** a boathouse with a loft: a little boat on rollers on the ground floor, nets in heaps and on the walls, a ladder to the loft where cork floats hang in strings, an altar shelf with a dozen small offerings to a dozen gods, just in case.
- **Event:** show him a Narkeray: a Damp Rock.
```text
HIPPONIKOS: I don't go out if there's an eclipse. Or a sneeze. Or a cat.

HIPPONIKOS: My grandson says I'm the most careful fisher in Phaleron.

HIPPONIKOS: He means I'm the one who doesn't fish.

HIPPONIKOS: There's a ray in the bay that numbs your hands. I've never seen one.

HIPPONIKOS: Show me one. From a safe distance.
```
[With a Narkeray in the party:]
```text
HIPPONIKOS: That's it? Flat as a dish. And that's what I've been afraid of?

HIPPONIKOS: Here. A rock from the bottom of the bay. It keeps the rain about.

{PLAYER} received a Damp Rock!
```
[`FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_DAMP_ROCK`.]
```text
GRANDSON: Grandpa says the sea's laughing since the olive fell.

GRANDSON: I think it's just waves.
```

## The optional lands, off the main road

Three places Act II never sends you, each a short walk off the main road and each worth the detour:
- **Euboia** (`MAPSEC_EUBOIA`), on foot from Thyrsa's east gate over the Euripus: the hill where a hound and a fox were turned to stone, the beach where a fleet waited for a wind, a bronze town on a bridge that opens only when the current turns, and Artemis's shrine at Amarynthos. Tuned to the Arkadia row, so it is the natural thing to do between Thyrsa and Arkadia, or on any return.
- **Route 17 and Marathon** (`MAPSEC_AETHOS_ROUTE_17`, `MAPSEC_MARATHON`), off Astyra's north-east edge: the Pentelikon quarries, the runner's road, the mound of the dead, and the harbor for the north Aegean.
- **Route 18, Halai and Cape Sounion** (`MAPSEC_AETHOS_ROUTE_18`, `MAPSEC_CAPE_SOUNION`), off Astyra's south-east edge: Hymettos's bees, Pan's cave, Phase 2's salt hamlet of Halai and its cliffs (moved here by the director), the silver mines, and Poseidon's temple on the cape where a father once read a sail wrong.

Routes 17 and 18 are open as soon as you reach Astyra (region C2 places their gates). Euboia is open from the Mask Laurel on; Thyrsa's east gate is region A's.

## Euboia (`MAPSEC_EUBOIA`)

Five maps, all in Euboia's section. The first two are on the Boeotian shore of the strait; the bridge crosses at Chalkis, the strait's narrowest point; the last two are on the island.

```
 [THYRSA] east gate (the Proitid Gate)
     |
 the Teumessos Road: the plain, the hill of the hound and the fox
     |
 AULIS: the beach, the plane tree, the old slipways
     |
 the Euripus bridge  ~~~ the current: south by day, north by night ~~~
     |
 CHALKIS: the bronze town on the strait
     |
 the Lelantine Road: vines, the old war plain
     |
 AMARYNTHOS: Artemis's shrine (a dead end)
```

| Map | Size | Joins |
|---|---|---|
| `MAP_EUBOIA_TEUMESSOS_ROAD` | 50×26, about 3.5 screens | West edge: Thyrsa's Proitid Gate. East edge: Aulis. |
| `MAP_EUBOIA_AULIS` | 30×24 | West edge: the Teumessos Road. North edge: the bridge's west end, by the strait. |
| `MAP_EUBOIA_CHALKIS` | 36×30 | The bridge across the strait (west), the town on the island side. South-east edge: the Lelantine Road. |
| `MAP_EUBOIA_LELANTINE_ROAD` | 52×24, about 3.5 screens | North-west edge: Chalkis. East edge: Amarynthos. |
| `MAP_EUBOIA_AMARYNTHOS` | 28×22 | West edge: the Lelantine Road. A dead end. |

None of these is a numbered route on the region map, so none has a great herm (SYSTEMS §4); Chalkis's bridge herm is proposed in Open questions as a fly point.

### The Teumessos Road (`MAP_EUBOIA_TEUMESSOS_ROAD`)

**Layout.** About 50×26, east from Thyrsa's Proitid Gate across the Boeotian plain. The road leaves the vineyards outside the gate, crosses a stream on a plank bridge, and climbs round the south shoulder of Teumessos, a low rocky hill crowned by two standing stones. From the hill's east side it drops through olive terraces to the strait, where Aulis's beach begins.

**Rhythm:** the gate's last vines and Melanippos (first trainer, in plain view on the road); a forced grass band in the stream meadow (3 deep, walled by the stream's reeds and a field wall); Ampelos among the vines on the south side; the climb; the hound and the fox on the hilltop (the set piece), with Kephalis on the only path past them; a second forced band on the terraces, where the road narrows between two walls; the first view of the strait.

**Ledges.** The olive terraces drop west, back toward Thyrsa: from Aulis's end, two hops take you down to the stream meadow, past the hill.

**The hill of the hound and the fox.** Two weathered standing stones on the summit, one leaping, one running just ahead of it.
```text
[The leaping stone]
A stone like a great hound in mid-leap. Its jaws are open.

[The running stone]
A stone like a fox, just out of reach. Its ears are flat.

[Examined together, the first time]
They've been a hand's width apart for longer than anyone remembers.
```
**Melanippos's sheepdog story,** if you talk to him after his battle:
```text
MELANIPPOS: That hill? A hound that caught everything it chased.

MELANIPPOS: And a fox that nothing could ever catch.

MELANIPPOS: Somebody sent the one after the other. Imagine that chase.

MELANIPPOS: Zeus couldn't stand it. So he turned them both to stone.

MELANIPPOS: Now nobody wins. My grandmother called that peace.
```

**Relic gates you can see:** a column drum (the Girdle) across a goat path up the hill's north face, with a visible item on the summit's far side (a Star Piece), and a fixed dig spot behind the running stone; a thorn thicket you can already cut (Demeter's Sickle) over a terrace with a hidden item.

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Field hand | the stream meadow | flavor |
| A traveler resting at the plank bridge | the stream | theoxenia decoy (SYSTEMS §10) |
| Melanippos, Ampelos, Kephalis | along the road | trainers (Part 3) |

**Field hand**
```text
FIELD HAND: Thyrsa's grapes, Euboia's grain, and the strait in between.

FIELD HAND: Everything here goes one way in the morning and back at night.

FIELD HAND: Even the water. Especially the water.
```
**The traveler at the bridge** (a decoy: he has a shadow, and your follower ignores him)
```text

TRAVELER: Once each way. The bridge was shut both times.
```

> YES:

TRAVELER: Here. I won't need these if I'm sitting on a bench all day.

[Give `ITEM_FRESH_WATER` ×2. Zeus Xenios +1 Favor.]

> NO:

### Aulis (`MAP_EUBOIA_AULIS`)

**Layout.** About 30×24: a crescent of sand on the strait, backed by dunes and a few houses. In the middle of the beach stands an enormous old plane tree with an altar of Zeus under it. Along the north end, rotten timber slipways run down into the water, wide enough for a hundred ships: the place where the fleet was drawn up. A small temple of Artemis stands shut on a rise. The road north climbs a short ramp to the bridge's west end.

**Identity:** the place everyone waited. The fishers here still talk about the wind as if it owes them money.

| Building | Who | Event | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Theonoe's house | the seer's family: Theonoe and her grandson Thestor | the fig count: a Wide Lens | arrival |
| The slipway shed | Ankaios, an old shipwright | the wind he's waiting for; a Mystic Water after you've crossed the bridge | arrival; after Chalkis |

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Fisher on the slipways | north end | dread |
| Children at the plane tree | the altar | lore |
| Protesilaos, Thestor | the beach, the dunes | trainers (Part 3) |

**The plane tree and the altar** (an altar of Zeus, per SYSTEMS §3)
```text
An old plane tree, wide as a house. There's an altar of Zeus under it.

A sparrow's nest in the branches. Eight chicks and their mother, carved.
```
**Children at the plane tree**
```text
CHILD: A snake climbed this tree and ate eight baby birds. And the mother.

CHILD: The seer counted. Nine birds, nine years of war.

CHILD: My brother says it's just a story. My brother's an idiot.
```
**The shut temple**

Nobody in Aulis talks about why.
```
**Fisher on the slipways** (the dread)
```text

FISHER: The water's still turning on time, at least.

FISHER: Somebody should tell the sky to look at the water.
```

#### Theonoe's house (`MAP_EUBOIA_AULIS_SEERS_HOUSE`)

- **Who:** Theonoe, very old, of the family of the seer who read the fleet's price, and her grandson Thestor, who reads birds.
- **The room:** a low house with one window on the beach. A shelf of bird skulls and feathers, sorted by size. A clay model of the plane tree with tiny bronze sparrows. A fig tree in a pot by the door, heavy with fruit. A worn stool facing the sea, where the family has watched for wind for generations.
- **Event:** the fig count, for a Wide Lens.

```text
THEONOE: Sit. You're not here for a reading. Good. We don't do those.

THEONOE: My family read the price of a wind, once.

THEONOE: The king paid it. The wind came anyway, a day later.

THEONOE: Nobody ever knew if it would have come without the price.

THEONOE: We stopped reading threads after that. Thestor reads birds.

THESTOR: Birds don't lie. They don't know how.
```

THEONOE: The other one asked: how many figs on that tree?

THEONOE: Ours guessed. The other one counted. Ours died of shame.

THEONOE: How many figs on this one? You may count. That's the lesson.

> COUNT THEM:
[The camera holds on the pot. Fourteen fig sprites appear one by one, a soft clink SE each (the tick is reserved for Elpis's music box).]

### Chalkis and the Euripus bridge (`MAP_EUBOIA_CHALKIS`)

**Layout.** About 36×30. The strait runs north to south down the west side, fast enough that its surface is animated in streaks (south by day, north by night, glassy at the turns). A wooden drawbridge crosses at the narrows, with a bronze-bound windlass at each end and a bench on the Boeotian side. On the island side, Chalkis climbs a slope: a quay where the current slaps the stones, a market of bronze (Chalkis means bronze), the spring of the town's nymph under a portico, and four houses. The Lelantine Road leaves the south-east corner.

**The tide gate** is Part 5's (the Euripus).

**Identity:** a town that runs on the water's timetable. Shops open at the turn. People finish sentences at the turn.

| Building | Who | Event | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|
| The bridge-keeper's house | Amphithea | the current's hours; a Damp Rock after three crossings | arrival |
| Chalkodon's forge | a bronzesmith | an in-game trade: Midonos "MIDAS" for an Onotis | arrival |
| The house of Abas | an old Abantian warrior | a house battle; a Razor Claw | arrival |
| Iatrokles's house | the town's healer | the rest point: a full heal | arrival |

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Phainias | the bench by the bridge | trainer (Part 3), and a philosopher's grudge against the strait |
| Kronist | the quay | the Titans' public face |
| Bronze-seller | the market | flavor |
| Children on the quay | the water's edge | flavor |

**The Kronist on the quay** (STORY §5: plain clothes, a sickle pin, unarmed)

KRONIST: That's what a life is now. Read, then lived out, then read again.

KRONIST: Kronos would let the water rest. Free bread at the Kronia, friend.

KRONIST: May your thread never be cut.
```

> SAY NOTHING:

A water clock on a stand, with notches for the turns. A slate on the wall with the day's turning hours chalked in a column and rubbed out, over and over. Coils of rope everywhere.

- **Who:** Chalkodon, a bronzesmith, and his golden donkey.

- **Who:** Abas, an old warrior of the Abantes, the long-haired spearmen of Euboia, and his granddaughter.

**Design note.** The Abantes' hair is the mirror of Kairos, the Moment, whom Astyra's statue shows with long hair in front and bald behind (STORY II-6): one you seize by the forelock, the other you never can. Nobody says so.

### The Lelantine Road (`MAP_EUBOIA_LELANTINE_ROAD`)

**Layout.** About 52×24, south-east from Chalkis across the Lelantine plain: the island's richest land, vines and olives on a wide flat floor between low hills. Halfway, the road crosses the old war ground, where Chalkis and Eretria fought over the plain for a generation and agreed, the story goes, to fight with no arrows or slings: only hand to hand. A boundary column stands there with the oath cut into it. At the east end the land rises into pines toward Amarynthos.

**Rhythm:** a calm stretch of vines out of Chalkis; Styra among the olive rows (in plain view); a forced band of tall grass in the vineyard's long rows, 4 deep, walled by stone terraces on both sides; the war ground, with Elephenor standing at the boundary column across the only gap in the old field walls (mandatory); a second forced band right after him, in the meadow by the column; a charcoal kiln in the pines, with an optional dead end behind it (Part 6); the pine slope up to the shrine.

**Ledges.** The road climbs gently toward Amarynthos; the terraces drop back west, two hops, to the vineyards near Chalkis.

**The oath column**
```text
A worn column. The oath is cut into it:

NO ARROWS. NO SLINGS. NOTHING FROM FAR OFF.

Someone has added underneath, smaller: AND NO COMPLAINING.
```
**Relic gates you can see:** a one-tile gap in a broken terrace wall with an item beyond (the Winged Talaria, Hermes Favor 60); a column drum (the Girdle) half-blocking a vineyard lane to a hidden wine press with a fixed dig spot.

| NPC | Where | Role |

| Vine-dresser | the vineyard | flavor |
| Styra, Elephenor | along the road | trainers (Part 3) |

**Vine-dresser**
```text

VINE-DRESSER: Nobody won. The grapes didn't mind either way.
```

North-west: Chalkis. East: Amarynthos.

**Every dead end pays:** the shrine's altar, the priestess's gift, the meadow's rare grass table at night (Part 4), and a hidden item at the spring.

## Route 17, the Attic Plain (`MAP_ROUTE17_ATTIC_PLAIN`)

**Layout.** About 56×28, from Astyra's north-east edge to Marathon. The road crosses the olive country of the Attic demes, passes under the shoulder of Mount Pentelikon, whose white quarries scar the slope above, and comes down through a pine pass onto the Marathon plain. A spur climbs north to the quarries.

**Rhythm:** the city's last gardens and Sosias training on the road (first trainer, plain view); a forced band of grass in the olive groves, 3 deep between field walls; Sostrate on the harvest track (mandatory, the track is the only way through the walls); the great herm at the quarry fork; the quarry spur (optional: Ochros and the marble road); a second forced band in the pine pass, right after the herm, 4 deep; the descent to Marathon's plain, and the finish stele for the runner's race (Part 5) at the Astyra end.

**Ledges.** The pine pass drops west, toward Astyra: two ledges take you back down toward the city end in a few steps.

**The quarry spur** (optional). A cart road of marble slabs climbs to the quarries, rutted by centuries of sledges. Unfinished column drums lie along it. At the top, the quarry face: white stone, ladders, and the Titan grunt Ochros with a pick.
```text
[A rutted slab]
Ruts worn into the marble by sledges.

Every column on the Akropolis came down this road.

[The quarry face]
White stone, cut in steps. Someone has chalked a sickle on it.
```
**Relic gates you can see:** an unfinished column drum (the Girdle) across the quarry's upper ledge, with a visible Hard Stone beyond and Glyphlet in the chips (Part 4); a one-tile gap in a terrace (the Winged Talaria) with an item across it.

**The great herm** (SYSTEMS §4), at the quarry fork. It doubles as the fork's sign.
```text
A great herm, hung with old garlands. Hermes's face, worn smooth.

North: the quarries. East: Marathon. West: Astyra.
```
(`FLAG_ICHOR_HERM_ROUTE17`.)

[South-west end]
ROUTE 17 · THE ATTIC PLAIN
South-west: Astyra. East: Marathon.

[The finish stele, at the Astyra end]
Here the runner from Marathon stopped. He said one word.

The word was “Rejoice.”
```

## Marathon (`MAP_MARATHON`)

**Layout.** About 36×30: a wide plain between the mountains and the sea. In the middle stands the Soros, the burial mound of the city's dead, grassed over and ringed with a low wall, with a stele at its foot. To the north-east the plain turns to marsh, reed beds where the invaders' ships were trapped. A white marble trophy stands near the marsh's edge. At the north-east corner, Schinias beach and a small harbor: the start of Route 20, the north Aegean, with the Conch. Three houses stand along the road under the mountain, with a spring beside them.

**Identity:** the plain where you can hear the battle. Every night, the story goes, you can hear horses neighing and men fighting. Nobody who's stayed to listen on purpose has come away the same.

**The rest point:** the spring of Makaria, by the houses.
```text
A cold spring under a fig tree. Your Pokémon drink and drink.

[heal the party, with the heal jingle]
```

| Building | Who | Event | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Epizelos's house | the mound's keeper, blind | the night battle; a Spell Tag | arrival; at night |
| Thersippos's house | the runner's family | the race (Part 5): TM Agility | arrival |
| Echetlos's farmhouse | a farmer with a famous plough | a story for a showing: Soft Sand | arrival |

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Boatman at Schinias | the harbor | the Conch gate to Route 20 |
| Pilgrim at the mound | the stele | lore |
| Kallikrates, Pelagon | the mound's path, the beach | trainers (Part 3) |

**The mound's stele**
```text
A plain stele at the foot of the mound. One line of names after another.

There are no titles. Just names, and the tribe each one came from.
```
**The trophy** (Ares's altar, per SYSTEMS §3: "Offer a battle", not a thing)
```text
A white marble trophy: a stone helmet, a stone shield, a stone spear.

It's an altar of Ares. He doesn't want things. He wants a fight.
```
**Pilgrim at the mound**
```text
PILGRIM: My great-grandfather's in there. One of a hundred and ninety-two.

PILGRIM: Nobody wrote down how he died. Just that he did, here, on purpose.

PILGRIM: I like that better than a prophecy.
```
**Boatman at Schinias** (the Conch gate)
```text
BOATMAN: North from here it's islands all the way. Skyros. Lemnos.

BOATMAN: I'd take you, but I don't go past the reeds anymore.

> without the Conch:
BOATMAN: If you had a way on the water, you wouldn't need me.

> with the Conch:
BOATMAN: Is that a conch? Then you don't need me. Mind the north wind.
```

#### Epizelos's house (`MAP_MARATHON_EPIZELOS_HOUSE`)

- **Who:** Epizelos, the old keeper of the mound, blind from birth, named for an ancestor who went blind on this plain.
- **The room:** a dim one-room house with its shutters closed, because the owner doesn't need the light. Everything within reach of the bed is arranged by touch: cups in a row, a staff by the door, a basket of clay votive soldiers he makes for pilgrims. A bronze helmet on a peg, dented above the eye.
- **Event:** the night battle. Stand at the foot of the mound after dark (Part 5) and come back to him; he gives a Spell Tag.

```text
EPIZELOS: You're looking at the helmet. Everyone does.

EPIZELOS: My ancestor wore it, the day of the battle. He took no wound.

EPIZELOS: A giant in bronze walked past him and killed the man beside him.

EPIZELOS: After that he never saw anything again. Not a thing. All his life.

EPIZELOS: He said he didn't mind. He'd seen enough for one life.
```
> after you hear the battle at night (`FLAG_ICHOR_MARATHON_HEARD_BATTLE`):
```text
EPIZELOS: You heard them. I can tell. You're breathing like a runner.

EPIZELOS: Every night. Horses and bronze. I hear it in my sleep.

EPIZELOS: Take one of my soldiers. Clay. It keeps the restless ones busy.
```
[Give `ITEM_SPELL_TAG`. `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_EPIZELOS_TAG`.]

**Design note.** A man who fought, took no wound, and saw a bronze giant and went blind for life, "and didn't mind": a quiet echo of Hyperion's true oracle, "You'll end your days in the dark, and be glad of it" (STORY §4, tablet 7). The player can't know that yet.

#### Thersippos's house (`MAP_MARATHON_RUNNERS_HOUSE`)

- **Who:** Thersippos, a runner of the old road, and his mother, who times him.
- **The room:** a narrow house with a long straight floor, because Thersippos practises starts in it. A water clock on the table, sandals hung in pairs from the rafters, a laurel wreath dried to brown over the door, and a painted sign on the wall: a stick figure running from a mound to a city, very fast.
- **Event:** the race (Part 5). He's at home until you've been to the mound; then he waits at the Marathon end of Route 17.

```text
THERSIPPOS: Somebody ran from here to the city once, to say we'd won.

THERSIPPOS: Said “Rejoice!” and dropped dead. Famous for it.

THERSIPPOS: I'm going to run it and not drop dead. Nobody's famous for that.

MOTHER: Somebody should be.

THERSIPPOS: Race me. You've got those winged sandals. It's only fair.
```
> after the race, won:
```text
MOTHER: He's sulking. He'll stop by supper. Well run, love.
```

#### Echetlos's farmhouse (`MAP_MARATHON_FARMHOUSE`)

- **Who:** Echetlos, a farmer whose family has kept the same plough for generations, and his wife.
- **The room:** a farmhouse with a threshing floor painted in a circle on the beaten earth inside the door. An enormous old ploughshare mounted on the wall like a trophy. Seed jars, a loom, a cat on the sill, and a muddy pair of boots that nobody is allowed to move.
- **Event:** a story for a showing. Show him a Ground-type, and he tells the story of the plough and gives Soft Sand.

```text
ECHETLOS: That ploughshare? A man came out of the fields the day of the battle.

ECHETLOS: Nobody knew him. He fought with a plough. Cut down dozens.

ECHETLOS: Afterward they couldn't find him. Not among the dead, not anywhere.

ECHETLOS: The oracle said call him Plough-man, and honor him. So we do.

ECHETLOS: You got anything that likes digging? I'd like to see one work.
```
?? Show him a Ground-type Pokémon? (party check)
```text
> a Ground-type:
ECHETLOS: Look at that. Straight furrows. A natural.

ECHETLOS: Sand from my best field. It'll never let you down.

[Give `ITEM_SOFT_SAND`. `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_ECHETLOS_SAND`.]

> none:
ECHETLOS: Bring me a digger some day. I like a good furrow.
```

**Signs**
```text
[The road]
MARATHON. Here the city's dead lie together.

[Schinias]
North: the open sea, and the northern islands.
```

## Route 18, the Sounion Coast, and Halai

**Phase 2's Halai Shore comes here** (director's ruling, 2026-11-14). The revised map put Emporion at Corinth, so Phase 2's optional coast east of Emporion's Coast Gate (its Route 5, Halai and Route 6) no longer had a place in Act I. The real Halai was a salt deme on the coast south-east of Athens, on the road to Sounion, so the hamlet, its three huts, its trainers, its items and its gates move onto Route 18 and the cape. Phase 2's words are kept, with what's changed for Act II marked. Aigialeus's Good Rod stays in Act I (world-act1 gives it to a fisher on Act I's Route 5), so his hut has a new event.

Route 18 is three maps in `MAPSEC_AETHOS_ROUTE_18`, then the cape:

| Map | Size | Joins |
|---|---|---|
| `MAP_ROUTE18_SOUNION_COAST` | 44×30, about 3 screens | North-west edge: Astyra. South-east edge: Halai. Phase 2's Halai Beach is its southern half. |
| `MAP_HALAI` | 24×20 | North-west edge: the Sounion Coast. South edge: the Halai Cliffs. |
| `MAP_ROUTE18_HALAI_CLIFFS` | 40×30, about 3 screens | North edge: Halai. South edge: Cape Sounion. Phase 2's Halai Cliffs, with the Laurion mines added. |
| `MAP_CAPE_SOUNION` (`MAPSEC_CAPE_SOUNION`) | 32×28 | North edge: the Halai Cliffs. The cape's tip: the Salt Grotto. |

The section's one great herm stands on the beach by the first boats, where Phase 2 had Route 5's (`FLAG_ICHOR_HERM_ROUTE18`; Phase 2's `FLAG_ICHOR_HERM_ROUTE5` and `_ROUTE6` go, Part 8).

### The Sounion Coast (`MAP_ROUTE18_SOUNION_COAST`)

**Layout.** About 44×30, south-east from Astyra's edge. The road first crosses the bare thyme slopes of Mount Hymettos, where the bees are, passes the cave of Pan and the Nymphs in the hillside, then drops to the sea: Phase 2's long curving beach, with fishing boats drawn up on the sand, tide pools at the waterline and low cliffs inland. Halai's roofs show at the south-east end.

**Rhythm:** a calm stretch of thyme scrub and hives; Kerinthos at his hives, first trainer, in plain view; a forced band of grass on the thyme slope, 3 deep, walled by rock outcrops; the cave of Pan (the set piece), with Battos at its mouth, mandatory, because the road squeezes past between two boulders; the descent to the beach and the great herm by the first boats; Asphalion on the beach path in plain view; Phase 2's dune-grass band across the beach (4 deep now, walled by the cliff and the boats); the tide pools (hidden items); Krison running laps on the sand, his sight line across the beach; a second dune band; Halai ahead.

**Ledges.** The slope drops north-west, back toward the city, in three hops from the cave.

**The cave of Pan and the Nymphs.** A real cave (at Vari). A man carved its walls by hand long ago: steps, a garden bed, reliefs of the nymphs dancing. His name is still cut by the entrance.
```text
[The carved name]
ARCHEDEMOS, THE NYMPH-STRUCK, MADE THIS.

[The garden bed inside]
A garden bed cut in the rock. Someone still plants thyme in it.

[The relief]
Three nymphs dancing in a ring, and a goat-legged piper. Pan.

They've been dancing since before your grandmother was born.
```
**The great herm** (SYSTEMS §4), by the first boats. It doubles as the fork's sign.
```text
A great herm, hung with old garlands. Hermes's face, worn smooth.

North-west: Astyra. South-east: Halai and the cape.
```
**The backward hoofprints** (Phase 2's, the Hermes amphora's lead, per SYSTEMS §5: "Hermes steals the cattle"). Once that amphora is complete, hoofprint metatiles appear on the beach (clear `FLAG_ICHOR_HIDE_HOOFPRINTS`), leading the wrong way along the sand to a crack in the cliff that wasn't marked before: the Grotto of the Twelve (`MAP_ROUTE18_GROTTO_OF_THE_TWELVE`).
```text
Hoofprints in the sand. Dozens. They all point back the way they came.

Someone walked a whole herd here backward, so nobody could follow.
```
**The Grotto of the Twelve.** In the Homeric Hymn, the baby Hermes hid Apollo's stolen cattle in a cave, roasted two, and cut the meat into twelve portions: the first sacrifice to the Twelve. The grotto holds a low stone altar with twelve hollows worn into it.
```text
A stone altar with twelve hollows, worn smooth.

Twelve shares. One for every god at the table.

Pray here?
```
?? YES/NO. YES, once: "You pray to all of them at once. Somewhere, twelve people turn their heads." Every one of the Twelve gains +2 Favor; Hestia, who takes the first share, gains +1 more. `FLAG_ICHOR_TWELVE_ALTAR_PRAYED`. A visible item: TM Thief, for the god of thieves.

**Relic gates you can see:** an islet offshore with an item ball (the Conch), visible from the beach; a column drum (the Girdle) across a path up the cliff to a shrine of the Nymphs with a hidden item.

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Kerinthos | his hive hut | a household (below), and a trainer |
| A footsore runner | the beach road | theoxenia decoy (SYSTEMS §10) |
| Kerinthos, Battos, Asphalion, Krison | along the road | trainers (Part 3) |

**The footsore runner** (a decoy: a shadow, and your follower ignores her)
```text
RUNNER: Is this the way to the cape? I've a message for the temple.

RUNNER: I've run since dawn and I think my feet have left without me.
```
?? Give her a Potion for her feet? YES/NO
```text
> YES:
RUNNER: Oh, that's cold! That's wonderful. Thank you.

RUNNER: Here. A runner's charm. They say it makes you quicker. It doesn't.

[Give `ITEM_QUICK_POWDER`. Zeus Xenios +1 Favor.]

> NO:
RUNNER: No, fair enough. I'll limp gloriously.
```
[`FLAG_ICHOR_DECOY_ROUTE18`.]

#### Kerinthos's hive hut (`MAP_ROUTE18_HIVE_HUT`)

- **Who:** Kerinthos, a beekeeper of Hymettos.
- **The room:** a stone hut whose back wall is a row of clay hive-pipes set into the stone, so the bees come and go through the wall and hum in the room all day. Honeycomb draining on a slanted board, smoke-pots, a veil on a peg, and a single stool, because nobody else will sit in here.
- **Event:** show him a Melibee and he gives Honey; once a day after, he gives one more.

```text
KERINTHOS: Hymettos thyme. The best honey in the world. Ask anyone.

KERINTHOS: Ask the bees. They'll tell you. Loudly.

KERINTHOS: You've got a bee? Let me see your bee. I miss new bees.
```
?? Show him a Melibee? (party check)
```text
> a Melibee:
KERINTHOS: Oh, look at her. Look at that buzz. She's a forager, that one.

KERINTHOS: Here. Three jars. For her, really. You can carry them.

[Give `ITEM_HONEY` ×3. `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_KERINTHOS_HONEY`. From then on, once a day: `ITEM_HONEY` ×1 (`FLAG_DAILY_ICHOR_KERINTHOS`).]

> none:
KERINTHOS: No bee? A shame. Every house should have a bee.
```
> once a day, after:
```text
KERINTHOS: One jar. The bees said you'd be back. They hum it before you come.
```
**Design note.** Bees that hum before a visitor comes are a small, innocent echo of Mom's Melisseer, which hums tomorrow (STORY §2). Kerinthos is just a beekeeper; nothing here points at Mom.

North-west: Astyra. South-east: Halai and Cape Sounion.

[The cave mouth]

### Halai (`MAP_HALAI`)

Phase 2's hamlet, moved here whole. **Layout.** A salt hamlet of three whitewashed huts on a spit of sand, about 24×20. Square salt pans flooded with seawater, white heaps raked up beside them, drying racks of fish and octopus, a stone spring under a tamarisk tree (the rest point), and the road on south to the cliffs. **Identity:** white salt, and the slowest work in Aethos.

**The spring.**
```text
A cold spring in a stone basin, under a tamarisk.

You and your Pokémon drink.

You feel rested.
```
[Heal the party.]

**Outdoors**
```text
SALT-WORKER: Let the sea in. Let the sun take the water. Rake up what's left.

SALT-WORKER: It's the slowest job in Aethos. I love it.
```
**Act II's addition outdoors,** a salt-worker's line for the dread:
```text
SALT-WORKER: The salt came in early this year. And then again. Twice.

SALT-WORKER: My grandmother says the sea's in a hurry. I say good.
```

Three households, each with a door, an occupant and an event:

| House | Who | Event | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Aigialeus's hut | an old fisher | his grandfather's hook, stolen by the snatchers: Dive Balls, and the old man on the cape's rock | arrival |
| Halmyris's hut | the salt-worker's grandmother | swap salt and shells for a Shell Bell | arrival |
| Sagene's hut | a net-maker and her daughter | show her a Narkeray for a Big Pearl; the hoofprint lore | arrival; the hoofprints after the Hermes amphora |

#### Aigialeus's hut (`MAP_HALAI_FISHERS_HUT`)

- **Who:** Aigialeus, an old fisher who learned the trade beside Glaukos of Akti.
- **The room:** a boat on trestles fills half the hut. Nets hang from the rafters, a bed is squeezed into the corner, and rods of every length lean by the door. A hook-shaped mark on the doorpost where something used to hang.
- **Event (new for Act II):** a request. The snatchers on the Halai Cliffs stole his grandfather's bronze hook from the doorpost; it's in a nest on a cliff ledge. Bring it back for three Dive Balls and a story about the rock off the cape.

```text
AIGIALEUS: You fish? With that? That's an old rod.

AIGIALEUS: Glaukos's, by the look of it. Out of Akti.

AIGIALEUS: He and I learned on the same rock. He got the sea. I got the shore.

AIGIALEUS: See that mark on the post? My grandfather's bronze hook hung there.

AIGIALEUS: A snatcher took it. Bright things. They can't help themselves.

AIGIALEUS: It's in a nest on the cliffs, I'd bet my boat. I can't climb now.
```
[If the player has no Old Rod, the first two lines become "AIGIALEUS: You fish? No? Everyone fishes eventually."]

The nest is an object on a ledge of the Halai Cliffs (below). With the hook returned (`FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_AIGIALEUS_HOOK` set at the nest):
```text
AIGIALEUS: That's it! Green with age, and still sharp.

AIGIALEUS: Here. Balls for the water. You'll want them, with a conch.

AIGIALEUS: And a thing Glaukos used to say. The sea keeps the honest ones.

AIGIALEUS: There's an old fellow fishes off the rock under the cape shrine.

AIGIALEUS: Never says a word. Never gets wet. Glaukos would've liked him.
```
[Give `ITEM_DIVE_BALL` ×3. `FLAG_ICHOR_AIGIALEUS_HOOK_RETURNED`.]
```text
> after:
AIGIALEUS: There's rays out past the point. Flat as plates.

AIGIALEUS: Don't grab one. I did once. My hand's still thinking about it.
```
**Design note.** The old man off the cape is Poseidon's Act III theoxenia, which tests the player with Glaukos's rod (SYSTEMS §10). Two people on this coast now mention him; neither knows what they're saying.

#### Halmyris's hut (`MAP_HALAI_SALT_HUT`)

- **Who:** Halmyris, the salt-worker's grandmother, who strings shells by the fire.
- **The room:** a low hut lined with salt jars in rows, a curtain of strung shells over the inner door that clicks when you pass, a salt rake by the hearth, and a half-strung shell bell on her lap.
- **Event:** an item swap. Bring her two Shoal Salt and two Shoal Shell (hidden on the beach, in Halai and on the cape), and she strings you a Shell Bell. `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_SHELL_BELL`.
```text

HALMYRIS: Bring me two of each and I'll string you one.

HALMYRIS: It rings when your Pokémon hits something. Heals it a little.

HALMYRIS: Don't ask me how. I'm old, I'm not a priestess.

> with two Shoal Salt and two Shoal Shell:
HALMYRIS: There we are. Salt and shell. Listen.

[A soft chime SE.]

{PLAYER} received a Shell Bell!

> after:
HALMYRIS: My grandson rakes salt all day and calls it love. I call it a bad back.
```

#### Sagene's hut (`MAP_HALAI_NET_HUT`)

- **Who:** Sagene, a net-maker, and her daughter Galene.
- **The room:** a net stretched on a frame across the whole room, so you walk around it; baskets of cork floats; shuttles on hooks; and Galene's corner, a shelf of shells and one dried starfish she has named.
- **Events:** a "show me" request, and the hoofprint lore after the Hermes amphora. `FLAG_ICHOR_SHOWED_SAGENE_RAY`.

### The Halai Cliffs (`MAP_ROUTE18_HALAI_CLIFFS`)

Phase 2's Route 6, with Laurion's silver mines added on its inland side. **Layout.** About 40×30. The road climbs from Halai onto sea cliffs where snatchers nest, then runs south along the coast to the neck of Cape Sounion. Inland, a spur climbs into the hills to the old silver mines of Laurion, where the city's silver comes from, the coins called owls. The cliff-top pasture is optional grass behind marble rubble (the Bronze Hammer).

**Rhythm:** the climb; a forced band on the cliff path at its narrowest, 4 deep, and Kymon across it, mandatory; the snatchers' nest on a ledge (Aigialeus's hook); the pasture (optional); the mine spur and Chous (optional); a second forced band on the coastal scrub right after the spur; the cape's neck.

**Ledges.** The cliff path climbs south; two ledges drop back north to Halai.

**The snatchers' nest** (Aigialeus's request), on a ledge reached by a short side path:
```text
A snatcher's nest, lined with salt crystals, a sandal strap and a coin.

And a bronze hook, green with age.
```
[Sets `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_AIGIALEUS_HOOK`. Before talking to Aigialeus, the same text ends "Somebody's going to want that back."]

**The silver mines** (the spur). Laurion's adits run into the hills. One is sealed by a great 2×2 boulder (Hephaestus's Hammer, Hephaestus Favor 60: shown now, opened later); the other is open, and Chous guards it.
```text
[The sealed adit]
A great boulder plugs the old mine.

Someone has scratched “OWLS” on it, and an arrow pointing in.

[The open adit]
Cold air from inside, and the smell of lamp-smoke.
```

**Relic gates you can see:**
- Marble rubble across the cliff-top path (the Bronze Hammer, Act I): the pasture beyond has its densest grass and a visible Magnet.
- The great boulder at the mine (Hephaestus's Hammer, later).
- An islet with an item ball, across open water (Poseidon's Conch): the Thunder Stone Phase 2 promised.

|---|---|---|

| Kymon, Chous | the cliff path, the mine | trainers (Part 3) |

MINER: The Titans say in the golden age there's no money. Just bread.

## Cape Sounion (`MAP_CAPE_SOUNION`)

**Layout.** About 32×28: the narrow end of Attica, a headland of red rock and scrub. A path climbs from the cape's neck past a small sanctuary of Athena on a lower rise and a ruined watchtower (Phase 2's), with the lookout's hut beside it, to the temple of Poseidon on the summit, white columns against the sea, with the great altar in front of its steps. On the seaward side the cliff falls straight down: Aegeus's leap. Below it, reached only with the Conch, a flat sea-rock under a cape shrine, empty. At the cape's very tip, a dark sea-cave: the Salt Grotto (Phase 2's). The temple keeper's house stands below the temple. Tall grass on the cape's scrub; islets offshore.

**Every dead end pays:** the altars, the lookout's story and gift, the Salt Grotto, the islets (with the Conch), the hidden Heart Scale at the cape's tip, and a fixed dig spot by the lower sanctuary.

**The altars** (SYSTEMS §3). Phase 2's cape shrine of Poseidon is now his great altar before the temple; sea gifts are his loved offering.
```text
[Poseidon's great altar]
The altar of Poseidon, before his temple. Salt crusts the stone.

[Athena's lower shrine]
An owl stele in Athena's small sanctuary.

She's keeping an eye on her uncle's temple.
```
**Aegeus's leap**
```text
The cliff drops straight into the sea. The water below is very blue.

The sea down there has a king's name.
```
**The empty sea-rock** (visible from the cliff; reachable with the Conch; empty in Act II)
```text
A flat rock under a little cape shrine. Gulls stand on it. Nobody else.
```
**The Salt Grotto** (`MAP_CAPE_SOUNION_SALT_GROTTO`, Phase 2's). Dark; the Torch is needed. One small cave: a tide pool chamber with two braziers to light, Karkitox and Cairnolith now (Part 4), a Big Pearl (visible), a Star Piece (hidden), and a fixed dig spot (a sherd for the Hermes amphora).
```text
[cave mouth, without the Torch]
A sea cave, pitch black inside. Water slaps somewhere in the dark.

You'd want a light.
```

| Building | Who | Event | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|
| The lookout's hut | Phaiax and his son Nausithoos | Aegeus's sail; a Zoom Lens | arrival |
| The temple keeper's house | the keeper and the acolyte Phrontis | Poseidon's rite; Shoal Salt for an offering | arrival |

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Fisher on the cape path | the cliff path | the Act III hook |
| Naubolos, Nausithoos, Phrontis | the cape | trainers (Part 3) |

**Fisher on the cape path** (Poseidon's theoxenia is here in Act III, after Laurel 7, per SYSTEMS §10; this is its seed)
```text
FISHER: See that rock down there, under the little shrine?

FISHER: An old man fishes off it some days. Never seen him come or go.

FISHER: Never seen him wet, either. Odd, in this spray.
```

#### The lookout's hut (`MAP_CAPE_SOUNION_LOOKOUT`)

- **Who:** Phaiax, the cape's lookout, and his son Nausithoos, who'd rather be a sailor.
- **The room:** a wind-battered hut built against the ruined watchtower's last wall, with one big window on the sea and a ledge under it worn smooth by elbows. Two flags on a pole by the door, one white, one black. A tally board of ships seen, years of scratches. A brazier for the beacon, cold.
- **Event:** Aegeus's sail, and a Zoom Lens.

```text
PHAIAX: A king stood on this cliff, watching for his son's ship.

PHAIAX: The boy had promised: a white sail if he lived. Black if he didn't.

PHAIAX: The ship came. The sail was black. The king jumped.

PHAIAX: The boy was alive. He'd only forgotten to change the sail.

PHAIAX: So we keep a watch here still. And we read every sail twice.

NAUSITHOOS: Three times, he means. He reads them three times.
```
?? Read the sail on the horizon? YES/NO
```text
> YES:
[The camera pans to the sea. A small ship object with a dark sail crosses the horizon.]

PHAIAX: Dark sail. What do you make of it?
```
?? BAD NEWS / LOOK AGAIN
```text
> BAD NEWS:
PHAIAX: That's what he thought, too. Look again.

> LOOK AGAIN:
[The ship turns broadside. The sail is a fishing net hung out to dry, weighted with black floats.]

PHAIAX: A net drying on the mast. A fisher with the day's catch.

PHAIAX: Good eyes. Better, a good second look. Here.
```
[Give `ITEM_ZOOM_LENS`. `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_PHAIAX_LENS`. BAD NEWS loops back to LOOK AGAIN; nobody fails, they just learn.]

**Design note.** A father who read his child's fate in a sail, and read it wrong: the act's theme, and a quiet hindsight for Lakonia, where a mother heard death in a verse that said only "glorious" (STORY III-5). No one draws the line.

#### The temple keeper's house (`MAP_CAPE_SOUNION_TEMPLE_HOUSE`)

- **Who:** the temple's keeper, an old woman, and Phrontis, the temple's acolyte, named for a helmsman buried on this cape.
- **The room:** a whitewashed room full of the sea's offerings: shells, sea-glass, a bronze anchor-stone, nets mended into a tapestry of fish, and a little shrine with a clay trident. A salt-crusted window. A jar of sea water at the door for visitors to touch their lips to.
- **Event:** she teaches Poseidon's offerings (SYSTEMS §3) and gives Shoal Salt the first time you make one at the great altar.

```text
KEEPER: Poseidon likes the sea's own things. Pearls, shells, salt.

KEEPER: Or wine, or barley, if you're a sailor and broke.

KEEPER: Bring him something from the water. He notices that.
```
> after an offering at the great altar:
```text
KEEPER: He took it. The waves under the cliff went quiet. They do that.

KEEPER: Here. Salt from the rocks below. For next time.
```
[Give `ITEM_SHOAL_SALT` ×2. `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_SOUNION_SALT`.]

**Signs**
```text
[The cape's neck]
CAPE SOUNION. Poseidon's temple. Mind the cliff. The cliff won't mind you.

[The cliff]
Here Aegeus watched for a sail.
```

## The *Paralos* (`MAP_PARALOS_DECK`)

**Layout.** 24×14, open sea on every side: the bow (west) with its painted eye and bronze ram, the bronze tripod amidships wound with laurel, the mast, the steering oars and Peisias at the stern (east). Garlands run along both rails. No hatch: the rowers are below and stay below.

| Lookout | the bow | beat 59 |
| Daphne | the stern, on a coil of rope | beats 58–59 |
| Thrason, Agathon | amidships, the bow | trainers (Part 3) |

CHORUS BOY: We're cranes. We go in, and in, and in, and then out.

CHORUS BOY: Last year Pamphilos went in and never came out. He cried.

CHORUS BOY: Master Nikias says if we're good we can see the lions.

**The ferry, after the first voyage.** From the second time the player boards, Peisias offers the run: "PEISIAS: The tribute round never ends. Where to?" ?? PHALERON / DELOS / KALDERA / STAY. Each is a fade and a warp, as Nausikles's ferry in Phase 2. With Daedalus's Wings the ferry is a convenience, not a need.

## Delos (`MAP_DELOS`)

**Layout.** 40×36, a low granite island. The sacred harbor is on the west shore. From it a paved sacred way runs east past the Terrace of the Lions and the round dry lake to the temples of Apollo and the Keraton, the altar of horns. Leto's palm stands walled in stone beside the lake. North of the harbor, the merchants' quarter: narrow lanes, the House of the Dolphins, Anios's house and the priests' hall. Mount Kynthos rises in the island's south-east, with a stepped path to the cave-shrine and the summit altar of Zeus and Athena. Grass grows only on Kynthos's slopes, among the rocks. **Identity:** the island where nothing begins and nothing ends. There is no graveyard, and the dancer at the horns.

**Rhythm.** The harbor and its herm; the sacred way and its landmarks; the merchants' quarter; then the climb up Kynthos, with a forced grass band across the stepped path (3 deep, walled by granite boulders), Eudoros on the switchback in plain view, a second band, Opis by the cave mouth (optional, facing the cave), and the summit with its altar and the view: east to Mykonos, south to the long dark line of Kalliste.

**Exits.** The sacred harbor: the *Paralos*, and, with the Conch, the water of Route 2 (sea, Act I's lane), which Delos sits beside (`MAPSEC_DELOS`; the region map gates it by the Conch). Delos is not a fly target: it has a rest point but no Asclepeion.

**The crane dance.** The dancer at the Keraton (beat 58) will practice with the player once a day after the first meeting: the two steps she shows, in, and turning back. `FLAG_ICHOR_DELOS_CRANE_PRACTICE` records that the player has danced them; AETHOS_MAP.md suggests that practicing here helps at Ariadne's Choros in the Labyrinth (LABYRINTH.md §5.7), so the flag is there for that ring's designer to read. Nothing here shows more of the dance than two steps.

**Relic gates you can see:** Rheneia, the islet across the narrow strait where Delians go to be born and to die, with a small white house and a visible item on its jetty (Poseidon's Conch; Big Pearl). On Kynthos, a split in the granite with an item ball across it (the Winged Talaria's gap; Star Piece).

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Anios | head of the sacred way | the high priest; beat 58 |
| The dancer | the Keraton | beat 58 |
| Daphne | the quay | beat 58 |
| Kronist | merchants' quarter | the Titans' public face |
| Stallkeeper | merchants' quarter | a small stall (Part 6) |
| Pilgrim at the lake | the lake's edge | flavor |
| Old pilgrim | the Lions | lore |
| Boatman | the strait's jetty | the Rheneia boat; lore |
| Lost pilgrim | the harbor crossroads | a theoxenia decoy |
| Eudoros, Opis | Kynthos | trainers (Part 3) |

**A herm** stands at the harbor crossroads, where the sacred way and the merchants' lane meet. It is a signpost, not a great herm (islands have none): "North: the merchants. East: the god's way. South: Kynthos."

**Kronist** (merchants' quarter, by the stall)

KRONIST: You see? It can be done. It's been done for a thousand years.

KRONIST: Kronos only wants Delos everywhere. Is that so terrible?

KRONIST: May your thread never be cut.

> if spoken to again:

```

```

### The priests' hall (`MAP_DELOS_PRIESTS_HALL`)

- **The room:** a long cool hall of whitewashed stone with benches along both walls, a basin of seawater by the door for pilgrims to wash their hands, a lyre hung on a peg, and at the far end a bronze stand of laurel. A row of empty sickbeds, made up and never used.
- **Event:** the rest point. The priests heal.

PRIEST: Sit. Nobody's allowed to die here. We take that very seriously.

[heal the party, with the heal jingle]

- **Who:** the three daughters of Anios, the high priest: Oino, Spermo and Elais. In myth the god gave them the gift of turning whatever they touched into wine, grain and oil.
- **The room:** a priest's house with a courtyard. Three stools at three small tables, each laid with one thing: a wine jug, a basket of barley, a jar of oil. A cistern in the middle, and a wall painting of three doves.

- **Who:** Mnesimachos, a ship-owner who has spent his whole fortune on one floor.

## Route 19, Home Waters (`MAP_ROUTE19_HOME_WATERS`, `MAPSEC_AETHOS_ROUTE_19`)

Sea, 40×60, about 4 screens running south. The story trireme's lane (beat 59's morning) and, with Poseidon's Conch, the player's own. Per `design/AETHOS_MAP.md`: "Home waters, past Paros", from Elaia's south shore to Kaldera.

**Layout.** The north end is the water under Kalliste's south cliffs, below Elaia: the island's dark headlands, a sea cave half under the water, and a strip of shingle where the slice's Elaia meets the sea. South of it the sea widens, with Paros's coast along the west edge: a bay with a harbor (the warp to `MAP_PAROS`) and white quarry scars on the hills above it. Then a chain of reefs and islets making three narrows, and at the south end, Kaldera's ring of cliffs, red and black, with the north cliff landing (Kaldera's north edge) at a gap in the rocks.

**Rhythm.** Home's cliffs and Skyllias, the first diver, in plain view; Paros's bay (rest at the island's spring, and the island to explore); the first narrows between two reefs (Kolymbas's sight line crosses it, mandatory); a bird islet with a dig spot and a visible TM; Euthymos in a moored boat, optional; the second narrows (Pontonoos's boat across the lane, mandatory); open water with Gripos on a sea-rock, optional; the third narrows (Kymaios swims a loop across the only channel, mandatory); Kaldera's landing.

**Relic gates you can see:** the sea cave under Kalliste's cliffs, half drowned, with a glint far inside (the Nereid Pearl's Dive, post-game); a whirlpool turning round an islet with a visible PP Up on it (Triton's Conch, post-game).

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Fisher on the bird islet | the bird islet | lore |
| Skyllias, Kolymbas, Euthymos, Pontonoos, Gripos, Kymaios | along the lane | trainers (Part 3) |

```text

FISHER: My father fished this water. His father. All the way back.

FISHER: Lately the tide runs the wrong way here at night. Toward home.

FISHER: Like it's trying to get back to something.
```

## Paros (`MAP_PAROS`, `MAPSEC_PAROS`)

Optional. 36×30, reached from Route 19's bay with the Conch. Per `design/AETHOS_MAP.md`: marble quarried by lamplight, the stone Galatea was carved from; a dark quarry for the Torch, and a sculptor who knew Galatea.

**Layout.** A small whitewashed harbor on a round bay, with a quay, a few boats, three houses and a sculptor's yard full of half-cut blocks. A path climbs east through olive terraces and a short grass band to the hills, where the quarries cut white scars into the slope. The great quarry's mouth is a square black doorway in the rock, with oil-lamp niches carved round it: the way down into `MAP_PAROS_QUARRY`. By the path, a spring under a myrtle bush with a shrine of Aphrodite: the island's rest point. **Identity:** the white stone everyone in Aethos prays in front of, cut by men who never see the sun.

**Rhythm.** The quay; the houses and the yard; the terraces and the grass band (3 deep, between terrace walls); Lysias the apprentice by the quarry mouth (optional; Part 3); the quarry.

## The Caldera Road (`MAP_KALDERA_CALDERA_ROAD`)

Part of Kaldera's section (`MAPSEC_KALDERA`), not a numbered route, so it has no great herm (AETHOS_MAP.md). It is route-shaped all the same, and follows MAP_DESIGN §1: forced grass, checkpoints, ledges, dead ends that pay.

**Layout.** 32×56, about 5 screens, climbing north up the caldera's inner wall from the old port to Kaldera on the rim. The south end is the old port: a stone quay where the *Paralos* moors, a second berth (for Act III's Kythera trireme), the harbor wall, a shrine of Poseidon, and a strip of black sand running east. From the quay a stair of switchbacks climbs the cliff in bands: the black lava band at the bottom, a red band of warm ash slopes with pumice scrub and grazing herds, and a pale band of white pumice cliffs below the rim. The donkey-men keep their donkeys at the foot of the stair.

**Rhythm:** the quay and the desecrated shrine with its guard; the black sand and Leandros the diver (first trainer, easy, in plain view); the first forced band, warm ash grass across the first switchback (3 deep, walled by the cliff and a drop); Hippias the smith on the second switchback, his sight line across the only path (mandatory); the stair's widest landing, where the goat path leaves (the set piece: the view across the lagoon to Nea Kameni smoking); the second forced band right after the landing (4 deep, between the cliff and the herd wall), with Taurivet herds grazing; the warm hollow's mouth, a side spot; Thoas the sailor, optional, facing the sea on a ledge; the pale band and the last switchback; the rim.

**Ledges.** The switchbacks have one-way pumice ledges dropping south toward the old port: the trip down is quick, the climb works. None strands a player: every ledge lands on the stair.

**The goat path.** A two-way scramble cutting the corner from the widest landing straight up to the pale band. It's open to everyone from the start; it's the tinker's test in beat 67.

**The warm hollow** (`MAP_KALDERA_WARM_HOLLOW`, a small named spot, 16×12). A gap in the red band behind a steaming vent leads into a sheltered hollow where the ground is warm to the touch and the grass grows green. The herd's calves shelter here. It has its own table (Part 4): Kaminoo, the first stage, rare, by day, at 31, as the dex and the director's ruling require. A visible Charcoal by the vent and a daily dig spot.
```text
[Mouth of the hollow]
A gap in the red rock. Warm air breathes out of it, and the smell of grass.

[Inside]
The ground is warm under your feet, like a hearth after supper.
```

**Relic gates you can see:** a door in the ash cliff with no handle, only a hollow shaped like a double axe, and painted plaster round it (the Labrys, Act III: the buried town); a great 2×2 boulder of fused pumice closing a side cave with a glint inside (Hephaestus's Hammer, Favor 60); the black sand's tide cave, reached only by water (Poseidon's Conch: a hidden Pearl inside).

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Donkey-man | the foot of the stair | lore; the ride up |
| Kisseris | at Poseidon's shrine | the desecrated altar's guard (Part 3) |
| Thirsty porter | the third switchback | a theoxenia decoy |
| Herder | the herd wall | lore |
| Leandros, Hippias, Thoas | along the stair | trainers (Part 3) |
| The tinker | the bottom switchback, after Laurel 6 | beat 67 |
| Daphne | the harbor wall | beats 64–65 |

**The desecrated shrine** (SYSTEMS.md §3). A small shrine of Poseidon at the end of the quay, where sailors leave sea gifts. A sickle is scratched across the god's carved trident. Kisseris guards it (Part 3). Before the guard is beaten:
```text

## Kaldera (`MAP_KALDERA`)

**Layout.** 48×40. A white town strung along the caldera's rim, with the lagoon a long drop below and Nea Kameni smoking in the middle of it. The houses are cut back into the soft white pumice, so each has a whitewashed front, a low vault and a roof you can almost step onto from the lane above. Four parts, south to north:
1. **The top of the stair.** The **Asclepeion** stands right at the head of the Caldera Road, the first door you reach. The Agora's stall is beside it.
2. **The rim lane,** with the augur on the rim wall, the tavern, the xenia host's house, and the households.
3. **The forge-temple of Hephaestus** on the highest point of the rim, its chimney always smoking, the hammer always going. Beside it, the **rim forge**, an open-air forge under a roof on posts, where the tinker's test ends (beat 67), and behind it the **slag yard**, heaps of cooling scrap and cinders, the town's only wild ground (Part 4).
4. **The rim stair** down the inner cliff to the **inner shore's jetty** (Talos's boat to the Telchines' forge and Nea Kameni), and, at the town's north end, the path to the **north cliff landing** (Route 19, the Conch).

**Identity:** the hammer. You hear Talos's forge on every screen of the town, once every 4 seconds, and it stops only once: when he puts the hammer down to give you the laurel.

**Houses.** Five households, each with its own door and its own room (Kaldera interiors, below). No other house has a door, so no other house is drawn as one: the rest of the rim is walls, vaults, cisterns, stairs and washing lines.

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Theoklymenos | the rim wall | the augur: the daily omen |
| Kronist | by the Agora stall | the Titans' public face |
| Woman with a water jar | the top of the stair | beat 60 |
| Pumice-cutter | the rim lane | flavor |
| Child with a Kapnub | the rim lane | flavor |
| Old sailor | the rim wall | lore: the mountain |
| Kalamis | the temple door | beat 61 |
| Hephaestion the smith | the slag yard | optional trainer (Part 3) |

### Asclepeion (`MAP_KALDERA_ASCLEPEION`)

- **The room:** a cave-house Asclepeion cut back into the pumice, long and vaulted, cool after the sun. Behind the counter a natural warm spring rises into a stone basin, steaming faintly, where patients soak their feet. Sulfur-yellow stains on the rock. The Pithos stands in a niche cut into the wall. A Panacoil drapes itself over the warm basin's rim.
- **Service:** the slice's Ichor healer strings.

| NPC | Lines |
|---|---|
| Patient soaking his feet | "The mountain's spring. Hot, and it smells like eggs." / "Cures everything. Except the smell." |
| Climber | "Walked up the stair. Five hundred and some steps." / "I counted. I wish I hadn't." |
| Healer (after `FLAG_ICHOR_ERUPTION_DONE`) | "Burns, all morning. Ash in everyone's eyes." / "A Titan boy came in with his hands blistered. He'd been carrying something cold." |

### Agora stall (`MAP_KALDERA_AGORA`)

- **The room:** a vaulted shop with shelves cut into the white rock: rows of small bronze votives, pumice blocks for scrubbing, jars of black-sand glaze, and coils of rope. A bronze bell on the counter.
```text
STALLKEEPER: Bronze votives, cast next door. Talos's offcuts. The god loves them.

STALLKEEPER: Pumice for your floors, if you've got floors.
```

### The Anvil, a tavern (`MAP_KALDERA_TAVERN`)

- **The room:** a fighters' tavern. Low and long, a bench along the rim-side window, a stone floor with the faint chalked square of an old wrestling ring still on it, wine amphorae in a rack, and on the back wall, hung from a nail like a trophy, a scuffed leather wristband as wide as a hand. The knucklebones table sits in the old ring's corner.

- **Who:** Euanthe, the oldest woman on the rim, who raised Hyperion when his mother died.

## The open Aegean (optional): Routes 20 and 21 and their islands

Poseidon's Conch (beat 57) opens the whole sea at once. AETHOS_MAP.md asks that "every painted island can be visited", and these seven are the ones off the story's lanes. None of them is on the main path, none of them gates anything, and all of them are tuned for Act III: a player who sails out the day they get the Conch will find the islands a few levels ahead of them, the way Emerald's Route 127 is. That is the reward and the warning both.

Each island is built to feel different, and each has one thing to *do* that is its own:

| Island | `MAPSEC` | Reached from | What it is | Its thing to do |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Skyros | `MAPSEC_SKYROS` | Route 20 | a goat island of white cliffs and one hilltop hall | find the hero hidden among the dancers |
| Lemnos | `MAPSEC_LEMNOS` | Route 20 | a red volcanic island where a god once landed | Hephaestus's rite at the crater, and Philoktetes's cave |
| Samothrake | `MAPSEC_SAMOTHRAKE` | Route 20 | a dark granite mountain in a gray sea | the Mysteries of the Great Gods: confess, and be initiated |
| Ikaria | `MAPSEC_IKARIA` | Route 21 | a steep green island of hot springs and very old people | the feather hunt on the shingle where a boy fell |
| Samos | `MAPSEC_SAMOS` | Route 21 | a rich harbor town under a marble temple | Eupalinos's tunnel, dug from both ends |
| Chios | `MAPSEC_CHIOS` | Route 21 | terraced vines, mastic trees and a stone seat | the bard's three stories |
| Lesbos | `MAPSEC_LESBOS` | Route 21 | a long olive island with a singing beach | the singing stones where Orpheus's head came ashore |

**Levels** rise with distance from home: the first island on each route is wild 38–42, the last 40–44. Trainers are 40–45.

**Getting there.** Route 20 leaves from Marathon's harbor (region E1 builds Marathon: its quay's east edge is Route 20's south edge). Route 21 leaves from Akti's waters, past the islet shrine the slice already shows from the quay (the slice's Conch gate):

**Akti, the slice's islet** (a new sign on the shrine's landing, and one new line for the slice's old fisher at the end of the pier, after `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_POSEIDONS_CONCH`):
```text
[The islet's landing]
EAST: the open sea. Ikaria two days out, with a kind wind.
Samos, Chios and Lesbos beyond. Poseidon keep you.

OLD FISHER: You've got the god's shell. I can see it in your walk.

OLD FISHER: East of the islet, the water goes dark and deep.

OLD FISHER: Islands all the way to the sunrise.
```

## Route 20, the north Aegean (`MAP_ROUTE20_NORTH_AEGEAN`, `MAPSEC_AETHOS_ROUTE_20`)

**Layout.** Sea, about 40×88, running north from Marathon's harbor up the outside of Euboia's long east coast, then north-east past Skyros, Lemnos and Samothrake. The water darkens from Attic blue to a Thracian gray as you go. Three set pieces break the open water:
1. **Cape Kaphereus,** Euboia's cruel south-east cape, in view to the west for the first two screens. A beacon burns on its cliff even by day. In myth the old king Nauplios lit false fires here to wreck the Greek fleet coming home from Troy. A sailor warns you off it.
2. **The supply islet,** a bare rock halfway to Skyros, where a Titan boat is taking on water. Two Titanborn guard the casks.
3. **The Lemnos channel,** where the sea narrows between Lemnos and a cluster of islets: currents (rapid water tiles, one-way) carry you east toward Samothrake unless you hug the islets, which each hold an item.

**Islands** are reached by warping from their beaches: Skyros's west bay, Lemnos's harbor of Myrina, Samothrake's north shore. **Rhythm:** Marathon's quay, the cape and its sailor, open water with divers, the supply islet, Skyros, a long open stretch, Lemnos, the channel, Samothrake at the top.

| Where | What | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Off Cape Kaphereus | SAILOR Naubates, on an anchored boat | trainer; the false beacon |
| Open water | DIVER Kalymnios, on a cork float | trainer |
| The supply islet | GRUNTS Iaspis and Achates | trainers (Part 3) |
| An islet off Skyros | a rock with a lone fig | a visible item |
| The Lemnos channel | three islets | items; one dig spot |
| South of Samothrake | SAILOR Eurylochos, bailing a fishing boat | trainer |

**Naubates, before the battle** (see Part 3), then after:
```text
NAUBATES: That fire on the cape? Don't steer by it. Never steer by it.

NAUBATES: An old king lit fires there once to drown a fleet. His son had died.

NAUBATES: He wanted company.

NAUBATES: Somebody keeps it lit still. Nobody knows who. Nobody goes to ask.
```
**The beacon,** checked from the water by the cape's rocks:
```text
A fire on the cliff, burning in daylight.

It's very bright. It seems to say: this way, this way, this way.
```
**The supply islet,** before the grunts (they stand by a stack of water casks with sickle marks):
```text
A Titan boat, moored at the rock. Water casks stacked on the shore.

Each cask is stamped with a sickle.

Someone has written “KNOSSA” on the last one, and scratched it out.
```
(The scratched-out word is a light seed for Act III's requisitioned ships; nothing more is said.)

**Signs**
```text
[South end, by Marathon's harbor]
ROUTE 20 · THE NORTH AEGEAN
North: Skyros, Lemnos, Samothrake. A long way. Bring water.

[A buoy at the Lemnos channel]
CURRENT RUNS EAST. Keep to the islets, or be carried.
```
