## Skyros (`MAP_SKYROS`, `MAPSEC_SKYROS`)

**Layout.** About 36×32. A white goat island: a sheltered west bay where you land, a steep path up through thyme and grazing goats to a hilltop village of flat-roofed houses, and on the summit King Lykomedes's old hall. On the east side, a sheer cliff with a burial mound at its edge: Theseus's grave. Small sure-footed ponies graze the bay meadow; they are scenery, and they won't let you near them.

**Rhythm.** The bay; Aipolos the goatherd on the path (the first trainer, easy, in plain view); a forced band of grass between dry-stone walls on the climb (3 deep); the village; Lykomedes's hall; a branch east along the cliff to the grave (optional grass, a dig spot, the night table). **Ledges** drop from the village straight back to the bay.

**Identity:** the island where a hero once hid as a girl. The thing to do is in Part 5, "The dancers of Skyros".

| Building | Who | Event | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lykomedes's hall | Deidameia and the dancers | the dancers' puzzle; a battle; Muscle Band | arrival |
| Mnasyllos's hut | a goatherd boy and his rooster | an in-game trade | arrival |

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Aipolos | the climb | trainer (Part 3) |
| An old woman spinning | a village doorstep | lore |
| A pony | the bay meadow | flavor |

**The old woman spinning**
```text
OLD WOMAN: The king's daughters used to dance in that hall.

OLD WOMAN: Six of them, and one more.

OLD WOMAN: The one more had very big feet. Nobody said anything.

OLD WOMAN: It was a king's house.
```
**A pony** (it backs off two tiles whenever you step toward it)
```text
A shaggy little pony.

It looks at you as if you're too big for the island.
```
**Theseus's grave** (a mound at the cliff's edge, with a plain stone):
```text
THESEUS, SON OF AIGEUS.

He came here old, and the king pushed him off this cliff.

Underneath, smaller, someone has scratched: “He went home the long way.”
```
At night Skyros's table carries Kalyptor, drifting among the stones by the grave (Part 4).

**Signs**
```text
[The bay]
SKYROS. Goats, ponies, wind. Mind all three.
```

### Lykomedes's hall (`MAP_SKYROS_LYKOMEDES_HALL`)

- **Who:** Deidameia, very old, the last of a family that has kept the king's hall since there was a king; and six dancers in long veils who practise here for the island's festival.
- **The room:** a long megaron with a round hearth in the middle, four wooden columns, a painted floor worn to bare plaster in a ring where generations have danced, and along one wall a bench of laid-out gifts: a mirror, a comb, jewelry in a box, a spindle, and a single spear. A war-horn hangs on a peg by the door.
- **Event:** the dancers' puzzle (Part 5). It can be played any number of times until you win; then the disguised dancer battles you and Deidameia gives the reward.
```text
DEIDAMEIA: You've come to watch the dancing? Sit by the hearth.

DEIDAMEIA: Once, a hero hid in this hall dressed as one of the king's daughters.

DEIDAMEIA: His mother wanted him out of the war.

DEIDAMEIA: A clever man came with gifts. Jewels for girls, and one spear.

DEIDAMEIA: Then he blew a war-horn at the door.

DEIDAMEIA: The girls ran. One of them reached for the spear.

DEIDAMEIA: My dancers keep the story. One of them is a boy today.

DEIDAMEIA: Find him, and I'll give you something.
```
```text
> after the puzzle and the battle:
DEIDAMEIA: You saw him. Most people only see the veils.

DEIDAMEIA: Here. A dancer's armband.

DEIDAMEIA: It made the king's daughters strong enough to lift him.

DEIDAMEIA: The real hero? Gone to the Games, the old women say.

DEIDAMEIA: He never could stay out of a contest.
```
[Give `ITEM_MUSCLE_BAND`. `FLAG_ICHOR_SKYROS_HERO_FOUND`.]

### Mnasyllos's hut (`MAP_SKYROS_GOATHERDS_HUT`)

- **Who:** Mnasyllos, a goatherd boy, and a Hoplektor that crows at the wrong times.
- **The room:** a one-room stone hut half dug into the hillside, a goat pen through a low door at the back, cheese hanging in cloth from the rafters, a straw bed, a milking stool, and on a high shelf a bronze helmet far too big for him, with a crest.
- **Event:** an in-game trade.
```text
MNASYLLOS: My grandfather won this rooster in a bet. It thinks it's at Troy.

MNASYLLOS: It crows at the goats like they're the enemy. They are not the enemy.

MNASYLLOS: They are goats.

MNASYLLOS: I want a proper goat-pokémon. One that sparks when it's happy.
```
?? Trade a Kerazap for his Hoplektor? YES/NO. YES: in-game trade, Hoplektor nicknamed **PELIDES**, Lv 40, holding a White Herb. `FLAG_ICHOR_TRADED_PELIDES`.
```text
> after the trade:
MNASYLLOS: “Pelides.” Son of Peleus. Grandfather named him.

MNASYLLOS: Grandfather was dramatic.

MNASYLLOS: The goats are so happy. Look at them. Sparking.
```
**The helmet on the shelf:**
```text
A bronze helmet with a horsehair crest, too big for anyone here.

“FOUND ON THE BEACH,” says a scratched label. “BELONGS TO A HERO.

ASK FIRST.”
```

## Lemnos (`MAP_LEMNOS`, `MAPSEC_LEMNOS`)

**Layout.** About 40×34. A red-earth volcanic island: the harbor village of Myrina under a crag, a road east across hot brown fields with steam rising from cracks, up the slope of **Mosychlos**, a low smoking crater with Hephaestus's altar on its rim. On the north coast, a sea cave: **Philoktetes's cave** (`MAP_LEMNOS_PHILOKTETES_CAVE`).

**Rhythm.** Myrina's quay; the village (two households); SMITH Akmon at the village's edge in plain view; the steaming fields with a forced band of dry grass between lava walls (4 deep, walled by hot rock); the crater road up to the altar; a fork north to the cave (optional grass, a dig spot). **Ledges** drop from the crater road back toward Myrina.

**Identity:** where Hephaestus fell. Every islander has an opinion about how.

| Building | Who | Event | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|
| The Sintian forge | Kadmilos the smith | a battle, then a gift of votives | arrival |
| Iphinoe's house | an earth-digger | the Lemnian earth | arrival |

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Akmon | the village's edge | trainer (Part 3) |
| A child | the quay | lore |
| A farmer | the hot fields | lore |

**A child on the quay**
```text
CHILD: A god fell on our island!

CHILD: A whole day falling, from the morning till the sun went down.

CHILD: He was lame after. Grandfather says the fall did it.

CHILD: Grandmother says he was lame before, and that's why they threw him.

CHILD: They don't talk at dinner.
```
**A farmer in the hot fields**
```text
FARMER: Don't stand still on the red ground. Your sandals'll cook.

FARMER: The god keeps his forge just under the field. We grow very good onions.
```
**Hephaestus's altar,** on Mosychlos's rim: a bronze-plated altar over a vent, warm to the touch. Per SYSTEMS §3, the altar menu, with his one-line sign:
```text
An altar of Hephaestus over a breathing crack in the earth.

You pray to Hephaestus.

Under your feet, something knocks twice, like a hammer.
```
[Daily prayer `FLAG_DAILY_ICHOR_PRAYED_HEPHAESTUS`. Offerings count single here; his great altar is Kaldera's.]

**Signs**
```text
[The quay]
LEMNOS · MYRINA. Where the god landed. Mind the hot ground.

[The north fork]
NORTH: the sea cave. Nobody lives there now. Somebody did, a long time.
```

### The Sintian forge (`MAP_LEMNOS_SINTIAN_FORGE`)

- **Who:** Kadmilos, a smith whose family have been smiths on Lemnos "since the god taught us", and his forge.
- **The room:** a forge set right over a vent: no bellows, the earth's own heat comes up through a stone grate under the hearth. Molds in the sand floor, a rack of tongs, a half-finished bronze cauldron on a stand, and a wall shrine with a little clay figure of a lame man and two women holding him up.
- **Event:** a battle (he is a SMITH, Part 3), then a gift.
```text
KADMILOS: The god fell here, and my great-great-whatever caught him.

KADMILOS: That's the story we tell.

KADMILOS: He stayed nine years and taught us bronze.

KADMILOS: Then he went home and never wrote.

KADMILOS: Battle me.

KADMILOS: If your Pokémon can stand the heat in here, they can stand anything.
```
```text
> after the battle:
KADMILOS: Good metal in that team. Take these.

KADMILOS: Leave them on his altar at the crater.

KADMILOS: He likes bronze. He made the first of everything, and nobody thanks him.
```
[Give `ITEM_BRONZE_VOTIVE` ×3. `FLAG_ICHOR_LEMNOS_VOTIVES`.]

**The wall shrine:**
```text
A clay figure: a lame man, and two women holding him up by the arms.

The figure is very old. Someone has mended the man's leg with wax.
```

### Iphinoe's house (`MAP_LEMNOS_EARTH_DIGGERS_HOUSE`)

- **Who:** Iphinoe, who digs the island's red healing earth one day a year, by old custom, and stamps it into little tablets.
- **The room:** a low house with a courtyard open to the sky, the floor stacked with drying red-clay tablets in rows on reed mats, a bronze seal hanging by the door, baskets of red earth, and a sickbed where a neighbor's son lies with a bandaged foot.
- **Event:** the Lemnian earth: once, a gift of healing tablets.
```text
IPHINOE: Lemnian earth. Red as a wound. It closes wounds.

IPHINOE: We dig it one day a year, with prayers.

IPHINOE: Then I stamp it with the god's seal so nobody cheats.

IPHINOE: The boy there trod on something in the sea. He'll be fine.

IPHINOE: He's had three tablets.

BOY: I'm having a fourth.

IPHINOE: You are not. Here, traveler. For your Pokémon, wherever you're going.
```
[Give `ITEM_FULL_HEAL` ×3 (the item's text is the tablets'). `FLAG_ICHOR_LEMNIAN_EARTH`.]

### Philoktetes's cave (`MAP_LEMNOS_PHILOKTETES_CAVE`)

A small two-room sea cave on the north coast, lit through a hole in its roof, so it needs no Torch. A stone bed with old rags, a rack on the wall shaped to hold a bow and a quiver, both empty, and a heap of bird bones. Wild encounters in the inner room (Part 4).
```text
[The stone bed]
A stone bed.

The rags on it still smell, faintly, of a wound that wouldn't heal.

[The empty bow rack]
A rack for a great bow. Empty.

Scratched beside it, in a careful hand:

“HE GAVE IT TO ME FOR LIGHTING HIS PYRE. I WOULD HAVE LIT IT ANYWAY.”

[Under the bird bones]
Something sharp among the bones: a barbed bronze arrowhead, still bright.
```
[The arrowhead is `ITEM_RAZOR_CLAW`, a visible item under the bones. `FLAG_ICHOR_ITEM_LEMNOS_CAVE_RAZOR_CLAW`.]

The scratched line is Philoktetes's: Herakles gave him the bow for lighting his funeral pyre. It is the Labors' seed, and nothing else is said.

## Samothrake (`MAP_SAMOTHRAKE`, `MAPSEC_SAMOTHRAKE`)

**Layout.** About 38×40, mostly mountain. A shingle beach on the north shore, a ravine path up through plane trees to the **Sanctuary of the Great Gods** on its terraces (the Hall of the Initiates, a round building, an altar court), and on a spur above the sanctuary a marble **Winged Victory** on the prow of a stone ship, wings spread into the wind. Above everything, the path climbs on to the bare peak of **Mount Saos**, where Poseidon sat to watch the war at Troy.

**Rhythm.** The beach and Dardanos's hut; the ravine with a forced band of fern and grass under the planes (3 deep, walled by the ravine's sides), INITIATE Kabeira at the sanctuary steps (mandatory, her sight line across the ravine's top); the sanctuary; the spur to the Victory; the long optional climb to the peak (grass all the way, no trainers; at the top only the view and an item). **Ledges** drop from the sanctuary terraces to the beach.

**Identity:** the island sailors come to so the sea won't kill them. The thing to do is in Part 5, "The Great Gods".

| Building | Who | Event | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|
| The Hall of the Initiates | the Koes, the priest who hears confessions | the initiation | arrival |
| Dardanos's hut | a fisherman | a cynic's joke and a gift | arrival |

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Kabeira | the sanctuary steps | trainer (Part 3) |
| Two sailors | the altar court | lore |

**Two sailors in the altar court**
```text
SAILOR: I've been initiated twice. Once for me. Once for my boat.

SAILOR: The purple band goes round your waist.

SAILOR: If you go over the side, the gods hold you up.

SAILOR: Has it worked? I've never gone over the side. So, yes.
```
**The Winged Victory,** on the spur:
```text
A marble woman with wings, on the prow of a stone ship.

She leans into the wind.

Her head is gone. Her wings are perfect.

She looks like she's about to arrive.
```
Hidden at her feet: a Big Pearl (Part 6).

**The peak of Mount Saos:**
```text
The top of the mountain.

Far to the east, a long low coast and the smoke of a city.

Poseidon sat here once to watch a war.

Someone has left a shell on the summit stone.
```
[A visible Shoal Shell on the summit stone, and the best view in the open Aegean.]

**Signs**
```text
[The beach]
SAMOTHRAKE. The Great Gods keep the sailors. Ask at the sanctuary.

[The sanctuary steps]
THE UNINITIATED MAY WALK IN THE COURT. NOT FURTHER.
```

### The Hall of the Initiates (`MAP_SAMOTHRAKE_HALL_OF_INITIATES`)

- **Who:** the Koes, an old priest whose one duty is to hear the confession every initiate makes before the rite; two acolytes with torches.
- **The room:** a tall, narrow hall of dark stone, lit only by torches in iron brackets, with benches down both sides for the initiates, a stone basin of sea water at the far end, a hanging bronze gong, and a shelf of folded purple bands. Behind a heavy curtain, a small inner room with a pit for libations.
- **Event:** the initiation (Part 5). Once.

### Dardanos's hut (`MAP_SAMOTHRAKE_FISHERS_HUT`)

- **Who:** Dardanos, an old fisherman with no purple band, who has never been initiated and is very proud of it.
- **The room:** a driftwood hut on the shingle, an upturned boat as a table, nets in heaps, a smoked-fish rack, and a wall covered in sailors' votive plaques he has picked up off the beach: little painted boards of ships, each one a thank-you to the Great Gods.
- **Event:** a gift, and the island's oldest joke (it was Diagoras's, a famous unbeliever's).
```text
DARDANOS: Look at all these.

DARDANOS: Thank-yous to the Great Gods, from every sailor who was saved.

DARDANOS: Very moving.

DARDANOS: Now, where are the plaques from all the sailors who drowned?

DARDANOS: Hm? None? Funny, that.

DARDANOS: Don't tell the Koes I said so. He likes me. I bring him fish.
```
```text
> after the initiation (FLAG_ICHOR_SAMOTHRAKE_INITIATED):
DARDANOS: Got your band, have you? Well. It looks nice on you.

DARDANOS: Here.

DARDANOS: If the gods hold you up, you'll want a snack while they do.
```
[Give `ITEM_SHOAL_SALT` ×2 and `ITEM_ORAN_BERRY` ×3. `FLAG_ICHOR_DARDANOS_GIFT`.]

## Route 21, the east Aegean (`MAP_ROUTE21_EAST_AEGEAN`, `MAPSEC_AETHOS_ROUTE_21`)

**Layout.** Sea, about 76×48. It leaves Akti's islet east into deep blue water, reaches Ikaria at its south-east corner, then turns north up the line of big islands that lie close against the Lydian shore: Samos, Chios, Lesbos, with the mainland's mountains always in view to the east (painted as an uncrossable border: that coast is not Aethos's). The water is warmer and busier than the north's: sponge divers' boats, fishing caiques, and one wreck.

**Set pieces.**
1. **The shipwrecked sailor,** on a sandbar islet a screen east of Akti: a theoxenia decoy (Part 2's line below; SYSTEMS §10).
2. **The sponge grounds,** a shallow stretch of pale water south of Samos where two divers work from boats.
3. **The strait of Mykale,** where Samos almost touches the mainland: a narrow channel, a Titanborn's boat moored by the Heraion's beach (Sardion is on Samos itself; the boat is just there).

**Islands** are reached by warping from their harbors: Ikaria's Therma beach, Samos's harbor, Chios's harbor, Lesbos's Methymna.

| Where | What | Role |
|---|---|---|
| The sandbar islet | a shipwrecked sailor | a theoxenia decoy |
| Open water east of Akti | DIVER Bythia, on a float | trainer (first, easy) |
| The sponge grounds | DIVER Kymothoe, and FISHER Eupeithes on a caique | trainers |
| An islet off Chios | a ruined lookout | a visible item, a dig spot |
| South of Lesbos | a drifting amphora caught on a buoy | a visible item |

**The shipwrecked sailor** (a decoy: he has a shadow, and your follower ignores him; per SYSTEMS §10 kindness still pays):
```text
SAILOR: Water. Please.

SAILOR: Three days on this sand with nothing but the sea to drink.
```
?? Give him a Fresh Water? YES/NO
```text
> YES:
SAILOR: Gods bless you. Gods bless your boat. You don't have a boat.

SAILOR: Gods bless you twice.

SAILOR: Here. It washed up beside me. Pretty, isn't it? I can't eat it.

> NO:
SAILOR: …I'll ask the next one. There's always a next one.
```
[YES: lose one Fresh Water, receive a Pearl, Zeus Xenios +1 Favor. `FLAG_ICHOR_DECOY_ROUTE21`. The sailor is gone on the next map load; a fishing boat came for him.]

**Signs**
```text
[West end, by Akti's islet]
ROUTE 21 · THE EAST AEGEAN
East: Ikaria. North, along the Lydian shore: Samos, Chios, Lesbos.

[A buoy off the sponge grounds]
SPONGE GROUNDS. Divers below. Don't drop anything on them.
```

## Ikaria (`MAP_IKARIA`, `MAPSEC_IKARIA`)

**Layout.** About 34×34. A steep, green, wind-bent island. You land at **Therma**, a little bay where hot springs steam out of the rocks into the sea. A path climbs through pine and thyme to a scattered village of stone houses with slate roofs and old people sitting outside them. On the north side, a long gray shingle beach under a cliff: the place where, the islanders say, the boy fell. The cliff top is the **dawn roost**, where sea-birds gather at first light.

**Rhythm.** Therma's bay and the spring house; FISHER Halios on the path above the bay (in plain view, easy); a forced band of wind-flattened grass on the climb (3 deep, walled by terraces); the village (Doliche's house); the cliff path down to the shingle (the feather hunt, three daily dig spots); up to the roost. **Ledges** drop from the village to Therma.

**Identity:** the island where people live a very long time, and where a boy didn't. The thing to do is in Part 5, "The feathers of Ikaria".

| Building | Who | Event | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|
| The spring house | Hydria, its keeper | heals (a rest point) | arrival |
| Doliche's house | an old widow | the feather hunt's reward; a seed for Daedalus | arrival |

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Three old men on a bench | the village | lore (the long-lived) |
| A shepherdess | the cliff path | lore |

**The three old men on a bench**
```text
OLD MAN: How old am I? Ninety-one. He's ninety-six. He won't say.

OLD MAN: Ninety-eight.

OLD MAN: We don't hurry here. You hurry, you get somewhere sooner. Then what?
```
After `FLAG_ICHOR_HEARD_PROCLAMATION` (Astyra's same-day sign has reached the islands):
```text
OLD MAN: A seer came through. Said all our threads end on one day.

OLD MAN: Same day as yours.

OLD MAN: Ninety-eight years I've been ending some day.

OLD MAN: One more doesn't frighten me.
```
**The shepherdess**
```text
SHEPHERDESS: The sea here is called the Ikarian. After a boy.

SHEPHERDESS: Wax wings. He went too near the sun.

SHEPHERDESS: We found the feathers for a week after.
```
**The dawn roost** (the cliff top, mornings): sea-birds in rows on the rocks, a Galenyon in every gap. Once the Icarus amphora is complete (SYSTEMS §5, #6: its lead is "a sea-bird's dawn roost, and a seed for Daedalus"), the roost has one more visitor in harsh sunlight: a static Ikaroth (Part 4).
```text
[The roost, at dawn, before the amphora]
Sea-birds by the hundred, facing the sunrise, all perfectly still.

[after the Icarus amphora is complete, in the morning]
Among the sea-birds, one creature with wings like a boy's.

It holds its arms out to the sun.
```

### The spring house (`MAP_IKARIA_SPRING_HOUSE`)

- **Who:** Hydria, who keeps the hot spring, and two very old bathers.
- **The room:** a stone bathhouse built over the spring: a steaming pool sunk in the floor, stone ledges to sit on, towels on pegs, a niche with a statue of Asclepius missing its nose, and a window to the sea.
- **Event:** a rest point. Soaking heals the party.
```text
HYDRIA: In you go. Your Pokémon too. The water's older than the island.

[heal the party]

HYDRIA: People come to live long here. They ask me the secret.

HYDRIA: I tell them: sleep after lunch, and nobody here ever asks how long.

HYDRIA: Then they go home and hurry.
```
**The bathers**
```text
BATHER: A hundred and two. Don't splash.
```

### Doliche's house (`MAP_IKARIA_WIDOWS_HOUSE`)

- **Who:** Doliche, a fisherman's widow, the oldest woman on Ikaria, who keeps the island's story of the boy.
- **The room:** a single room with a raised sleeping platform, a loom with a fishing-net pattern woven into it, a huge clay oven in the corner, strings of dried figs, and on the wall above the bed a small wooden box with a glass-clear lid and a single burned feather inside.
- **Event:** the feather hunt's reward (Part 5); and, once, the seed for Daedalus.
```text
DOLICHE: My grandmother's grandmother buried him.

DOLICHE: On the shingle, under the cliff. A boy who fell out of the sky.

DOLICHE: His father circled overhead for a whole day, crying.

DOLICHE: Then he flew south and never came back.

DOLICHE: She kept one feather. That one, in the box.

DOLICHE: It's still a little warm, I swear it.
```
[The box on the wall:]
```text
A single feather in a little box.

The quill end is melted, as if by a candle.
```
(Daedalus is never named. "He flew south" is all; Knossa is south.)

## Samos (`MAP_SAMOS`, `MAPSEC_SAMOS`)

**Layout.** About 46×36. Samos is rich and knows it. The harbor town is on the east, behind a great stone mole; its houses climb a hill to an old wall. Over the hill, a road runs west across a plain to the **Heraion**, Hera's huge temple by a marsh where she was born under a willow. Through the hill between them runs **Eupalinos's tunnel** (`MAP_SAMOS_EUPALINOS_TUNNEL`): its north mouth is behind the town, its south mouth on the Heraion road. Across the strait to the east, the dark ridge of Mount Latmos on the mainland, where a shepherd sleeps forever.

**Rhythm.** The mole and harbor; the town (three households); PHILOSOPHER Philolaos in the stoa by the harbor (in plain view); the tunnel's north mouth, or the long way over the hill road with a forced band of grass (4 deep, walled by the town wall and a ravine); the Heraion plain (optional grass, a dig spot); the Heraion and its desecrated wellhead, guarded by GRUNT Sardion. **Ledges** drop from the hill road back to the town.

**Identity:** two halves that met in the middle. The tunnel was dug from both ends at once, and it is the thing to do (Part 5, "Eupalinos's tunnel"); once it's joined, it is the island's shortcut.

| Building | Who | Event | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Naustrophos's house | the tunnel's keeper | how to join the tunnel | arrival |
| Mnesarchos's house | a philosopher who won't eat beans | a riddle, a TM | arrival |
| Maiandrios's stall | a fishmonger | a fish with a ring in it: the King's Rock | arrival |

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Philolaos | the harbor stoa | trainer (Part 3) |
| A merchant | the mole | lore |
| Sardion | the Heraion | trainer (Part 3); the altar's guard |

**The merchant on the mole**
```text
MERCHANT: Samos had a tyrant once so lucky it frightened him.

MERCHANT: Everything he touched turned out well.

MERCHANT: So he threw his best ring in the sea, to give the gods something.

MERCHANT: Next day it came back in a fish.

MERCHANT: Ask Maiandrios about the fish.

MERCHANT: He'll tell you it was his great-grandfather's.

MERCHANT: Everyone's great-grandfather sold that fish.
```
**Mount Latmos,** checked from the Heraion's beach:
```text
Across the strait, a dark ridge.

A shepherd sleeps up there, they say, and has for a thousand years.

The moon loved him and asked for him never to wake. So he doesn't.
```
(At night the Heraion plain's grass has a rare Amnoze, Part 4.)

**Hera's wellhead,** at the Heraion, desecrated (SYSTEMS §3): a marble well-curb under a willow, a sickle scratched into it. Before Sardion is beaten:
```text
Hera's wellhead, under the willow where she was born.

Someone has scratched a sickle deep into the marble.
```
After the battle, the first prayer cleanses it (+3 Hera Favor, `FLAG_ICHOR_ALTAR_CLEANSED_SAMOS`):
```text
You pray to Hera.

A peacock somewhere screams once, and the scratches are gone.
```
From then on it is Hera's altar (SYSTEMS §3: she loves the Pomeg Berry; `FLAG_DAILY_ICHOR_PRAYED_HERA`). Cancer is placed at Hera Favor 30, per SYSTEMS §8.

**Signs**
```text
[The mole]
SAMOS. The harbor, the tunnel, the temple.

Not in that order, unless you like walking.

[The tunnel's north mouth]
EUPALINOS'S TUNNEL. Dug from both ends. They met. Mostly.

[The Heraion road]
WEST: the Heraion. Hera was born here, under the willow. Be polite.
```

### Naustrophos's house (`MAP_SAMOS_TUNNEL_KEEPERS_HOUSE`)

- **Who:** Naustrophos, whose family have kept the tunnel's water channel clean since it was dug.
- **The room:** a narrow house built into the hill, with a trapdoor in the floor down to a stone water channel you can hear running; plans of the tunnel scratched on wax boards along every wall, two of them, one for each crew; a surveyor's staff and string by the door.
- **Event:** he explains the tunnel and asks you to join it (Part 5). After you do, a thank-you.
```text
NAUSTROPHOS: My ancestor dug that tunnel.

NAUSTROPHOS: Two crews, one at each end of the hill, digging toward each other.

NAUSTROPHOS: A whole year in the dark. They met in the middle. Nearly.

NAUSTROPHOS: Off by the height of a man.

NAUSTROPHOS: The kink in the middle's still blocked with rubble.

NAUSTROPHOS: Clear it from the south side and the tunnel's whole.
```
```text
> after FLAG_ICHOR_SAMOS_TUNNEL_JOINED:
NAUSTROPHOS: You heard it? The water running all the way through?

NAUSTROPHOS: A thousand years I've been waiting for that sound.

NAUSTROPHOS: Not me personally. You know what I mean. Here.
```
[Give **TM Dig** (Balance assigns its number). `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_TM_DIG_SAMOS`.]

### Mnesarchos's house (`MAP_SAMOS_PHILOSOPHERS_HOUSE`)

- **Who:** Mnesarchos, a philosopher of the school that counts everything and eats no beans.
- **The room:** a bare white room with a triangle drawn in charcoal on the floor and pebbles laid along its sides in rows (three, four, five); a lyre with one string; a bowl of lentils, conspicuously not beans; and a sign on the larder door.
- **Event:** a riddle; a reward.
```text
MNESARCHOS: Everything is number. The lyre's notes. The stars. You. Especially you.

MNESARCHOS: A riddle. A triangle with a square corner.

MNESARCHOS: Its short sides are three paces and four.

MNESARCHOS: How long is the long side?
```
?? Multichoice: FIVE / SIX / SEVEN
```text
> FIVE:
MNESARCHOS: Five! The world is in order. I was worried for a moment there.

MNESARCHOS: Take this. It's about thinking very hard. We do a lot of that.

> SIX / SEVEN:
MNESARCHOS: Count the pebbles on the floor. Then come back. There's no hurry.

MNESARCHOS: Numbers wait.
```
[FIVE: give **TM Zen Headbutt**. `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_TM_ZEN_HEADBUTT`.]

**The larder sign:**
```text
NO BEANS. NOT EVEN ONE. WE KNOW WHAT YOU DID, BEANS.
```

### Maiandrios's stall (`MAP_SAMOS_FISHMONGERS`)

- **Who:** Maiandrios, a fishmonger, whose great-grandfather "definitely" sold the tyrant the fish with the ring in it.
- **The room:** a stall-and-house in one: a marble slab counter with fish laid out on fig leaves, baskets of ice-cold sea water, a scale, and behind a curtain a cramped room with a cot and a framed bronze ring on the wall, which is not the ring.
- **Event:** buy a fish for 500; the first fish has a ring inside: the King's Rock. Later fish are just fish (sell value only).
```text
MAIANDRIOS: Fresh fish! Fish with history!

MAIANDRIOS: My great-grandfather sold the tyrant his ring back, inside a fish.

MAIANDRIOS: Five hundred for a fish. You never know what's inside.
```
?? Buy a fish for 500? YES/NO
```text
> YES, the first time:
MAIANDRIOS: Gut it yourself. I'm not paid for that.

[Something hard inside the fish: a heavy stone ring, like a little crown.]

{PLAYER} found a King's Rock!

MAIANDRIOS: …That's not mine. That's not anyone's. Keep it. Don't tell my wife.

> YES, after:
MAIANDRIOS: A fish. Just a fish. Very good fish. No history at all.
```
[First purchase: `ITEM_KINGS_ROCK`, `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_KINGS_ROCK`. Later purchases give a Pearl, which sells for about what the fish cost: the stall is a once-only reward, not a shop.]

Part 5 has its plan and play.

## Chios (`MAP_CHIOS`, `MAPSEC_CHIOS`)

**Layout.** About 38×34. Terraced hills of vines in the north and mastic trees in the south, with little white tears of resin on their bark. The harbor town between. Above the town on a hill, a big flat rock with a seat cut in it: **the bard's stone**, where the blind singer of the old stories is said to have taught. In the vineyard terraces, a wine-press and the house of the island's old wine family.

**Rhythm.** The harbor; the town (two households); VINTNER Maron in the vineyard terraces, his sight line across the terrace stair (mandatory); the vines, with a forced band of grass between the rows (4 deep); the bard's stone (the thing to do, Part 5, "The bard's three stories"); the mastic groves (optional grass, a dig spot). **Ledges** drop from the terraces to the harbor.

**Identity:** the island of the bards. Everyone here can tell you a story, and most of them do.

| Building | Who | Event | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kynaithos's house | an old bard of the guild that keeps the songs | the three stories; Artemis's lead; Wise Glasses | arrival |
| Merope's house | a vintner | three berries for three Wine | arrival |

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Maron | the terraces | trainer (Part 3) |
| A mastic gatherer | the groves | lore and a gift |
| A boy | the harbor | lore |

**The mastic gatherer**
```text
GATHERER: The trees weep. We collect the tears. It's for chewing.

GATHERER: Keeps your breath sweet.

GATHERER: The gods like it too. Here, put a pinch on any altar.

GATHERER: They'll take it for incense.
```
[Once: give `ITEM_FRANKINCENSE` ×2 (the mastic stands in for incense). `FLAG_ICHOR_MASTIC_GIFT`.]

**A boy at the harbor**
```text
BOY: Seven cities say the bard was born in them. We say he was born here.

BOY: We have the stone. They don't have a stone. That's how you know.
```

### Kynaithos's house (`MAP_CHIOS_BARDS_HOUSE`)

- **Who:** Kynaithos, an old singer of the guild that keeps the songs, and his grandchildren, who have heard every story too many times.
- **The room:** a long room whose walls are lined with niches of rolled scrolls nobody reads, because everything is in his head; a high chair for him by the hearth and low stools for listeners in a half-ring; a staff leaning in the corner; a lyre with a cracked arm.
- **Event:** he tells the stories at the bard's stone, not indoors (Part 5). Indoors, his line and his grandchildren's.
```text
KYNAITHOS: Not in here. Stories want sky. Come up to the stone.

GRANDDAUGHTER: He's going to do the one about the giant.

GRANDSON: He always does the one about the giant.
```

### Merope's house (`MAP_CHIOS_VINTNERS_HOUSE`)

- **Who:** Merope, of the old wine family whose first king taught Chios to make wine, and her treading-floor.
- **The room:** a house built round a stone treading-floor sunk in the middle of the main room, stained purple to the knee; tall jars along the walls up to the rafters; a family shrine to Dionysus with a little bronze cup; grape-cluster beams.
- **Event:** an item swap: three berries for three Wine.
```text
MEROPE: My family's first king was the wine god's own son.

MEROPE: That's why our wine is the best.

MEROPE: Also because we tread it barefoot and sing very rude songs.

MEROPE: Bring me three berries, any kind. I'll give you three jars.

MEROPE: A fair trade, and a good one.
```
?? Give three berries for three Wine? YES/NO (any three berries from the bag)
```text
> YES:
MEROPE: Good fruit. Here. Pour a little out for the god before you drink.

MEROPE: He notices.
```
[Repeatable once a day: `FLAG_DAILY_ICHOR_MEROPE_WINE`. Three berries become `ITEM_WINE` ×3.]

**The family shrine:**
```text
A little bronze cup on the shrine. It's full, as if someone just poured.
```

## Lesbos (`MAP_LESBOS`, `MAPSEC_LESBOS`)

**Layout.** About 52×34, the largest of the seven: two cells on the map. A long olive island. You land at **Methymna** in the north-east, a harbor town on a castle hill. The road runs west through olive groves (wide, with a lot of grass) and a petrified forest of stone tree-trunks on a bare hillside, to **Antissa** on the west coast: a beach of round stones where, the islanders say, Orpheus's head and lyre washed ashore, still singing, and a small shrine above it.

**Rhythm.** Methymna's harbor and Terpandros's house; HARVESTER Kleis in the groves (in plain view, easy for the band); the olive groves, with a long forced band (5 deep, the widest in the open Aegean, walled by grove terraces) and optional grass around them; the stone forest (a dig spot, a hidden item in a hollow trunk); Antissa's beach and the shrine (the thing to do, Part 5, "The singing stones"). **Ledges** drop from the grove terraces east toward Methymna.

**Identity:** the island where a song came ashore and kept going. Lesbos is also where a boy riding a dolphin was carried home, so the Conch is welcome here.

| Building | Who | Event | Opens |
|---|---|---|---|
| Terpandros's house | a lyre-maker | the dolphin rider's story; a gift if you hold the Conch | arrival |
| The shrine of the head | Pittakos, its keeper | the singing stones; the Orpheus amphora's lead | arrival |

| NPC | Where | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Kleis | the olive groves | trainer (Part 3) |
| An olive press worker | the groves | lore |
| A child at the stone forest | the hillside | lore |

**The olive press worker**
```text
WORKER: Our olives are the best in the sea. Don't tell Chios.

WORKER: Chios thinks it's the wine.

WORKER: It is the wine. Don't tell Chios that either.
```
**The child at the stone forest**
```text
CHILD: The trees turned to stone a long time ago.

CHILD: Grandmother says they listened to a song so hard they forgot to move.

CHILD: I listen to songs. I move. Look.
```

### Terpandros's house (`MAP_LESBOS_LYRE_PLAYERS_HOUSE`)

- **Who:** Terpandros, a maker and player of lyres, descended from the singer who was thrown overboard and carried to shore by a dolphin.
- **The room:** a workshop-house: tortoise shells drying on the roof beams, lyre arms half-carved on a bench, gut strings coiled on pegs, a curtained bed, and a floor mosaic of a man riding a dolphin, holding a lyre over his head to keep it dry.
- **Event:** the dolphin story; if you carry Poseidon's Conch, a gift.
```text
TERPANDROS: Sailors threw my ancestor over the side for his gold.

TERPANDROS: He asked to sing one last song first.

TERPANDROS: A dolphin came up under him, still singing, and carried him home.

TERPANDROS: The song never stopped.
```
```text
> with Poseidon's Conch:
TERPANDROS: That's a shell from the god's own sea.

TERPANDROS: You've ridden one too, haven't you? A dolphin.

TERPANDROS: Then you're family. Take this.

TERPANDROS: It's from a shell like yours, ground fine.
```
[With `FLAG_ICHOR_GOT_POSEIDONS_CONCH` (always true here; the line is written for a post-game return too): give `ITEM_MYSTIC_WATER`. `FLAG_ICHOR_TERPANDROS_GIFT`.]

### The shrine of the head (`MAP_LESBOS_SHRINE_OF_THE_HEAD`)

- **Who:** Pittakos, the shrine's keeper, a sensible man stuck with a mystical job.
- **The room:** a small round shrine over the beach: a stone niche at the back with an empty bronze stand where a lyre once hung, offerings of flowers and shells, a bench, and a window over the singing stones below.
- **Event:** the singing stones are outside on the beach (Part 5); indoors, the lore, and the amphora's lead.
```text
PITTAKOS: The head came ashore here, singing, and the lyre with it.

PITTAKOS: The lyre went up to the gods. The head stayed.

PITTAKOS: For a long while it sang prophecies. Then it stopped.

PITTAKOS: The god of the lyre told it to, they say. Bad for business.

PITTAKOS: Now the stones on the beach sing a little, when the wind's right.

PITTAKOS: Go and listen.
```
```text
> with the Orpheus amphora complete (SYSTEMS §5, #8):
PITTAKOS: You've seen the pot. The singer and the animals.

PITTAKOS: Then you know the song isn't finished.

PITTAKOS: The stones sing its first line and stop.

PITTAKOS: Someone, somewhere, knows the rest.

PITTAKOS: Not on this island. Not yet. Come back when the world's a little older.
```
(The lead completes in the post-game, per AETHOS_MAP; this line is its waypoint. `FLAG_ICHOR_ORPHEUS_LEAD_LESBOS`.)

# Part 3. Trainers

Format: the `src/data/trainers.party` syntax, as in the slice and Phase 2. Moves are listed only where they differ from the default (the last four level-up moves in the dex learnset), and every listed move is in the species' dex learnset at or below that level; a boss's TM moves are marked. Species constants exist once the dex is implemented.

**Conventions for Phase 3.** Act II's trainers are a step stronger than Act I's.
- Route trainers and Titanborn grunts: IVs 9, AI Check Bad Move.
- Acolytes: IVs 12, AI Basic Trainer.
- Kleon: IVs 12, his ace 18, AI Basic Trainer. His battles are no-whiteout (`FLAG_ICHOR_NO_WHITEOUT`), with a loss branch, as in Phase 2.
- Hierophants and admins: IVs 18, aces 27, AI Basic Trainer. Two Super Potions for Thespis; two Hyper Potions from Kallisto on, and for Rhea and Hyperion.
- Spartan difficulty needs its own boss teams from Balance, as in the slice and Phase 2.

**Kleon's ids** are named for the player's starter, as in Phase 2: `TRAINER_ICHOR_KLEON_3_KYNDER` means the player chose Kynder, so Kleon leads Thalamare.

## New trainer classes

Class names fit `TrainerClass.name[13]`. Each class needs a front portrait and an overworld walker; the walkers can share palette families as noted. Act II introduces thirteen.

The rest of the road west uses classes that already exist: Fisher, Pilgrim, Harvester, Augur, Goatherd, Shepherd, Runner, Merchant and Titanborn.

Region C1 also uses RUNNER, HARVESTER, HOPLITE, MERCHANT, PILGRIM, GOATHERD, SHEPHERD, JESTER, FISHER, POTTER and Titanborn (all existing), MAENAD (region A's), and ATHLETE (region C2's) for the judge of the Nemean games, who comes before Astyra on the road: whichever region's file lands first defines the class (open questions).

Region D's other trainers use existing classes: Sailor, Pilgrim, Fisher, Titanborn, Titan Admin, Hierophant, and Huntress (introduced by region B2).

**Conventions** (the contract): route trainers and grunts IVs 9, AI Check Bad Move; smiths IVs 12, AI Basic Trainer; Talos and Hyperion IVs 18, aces 27, two Hyper Potions, AI Basic Trainer. Moves are listed only where they differ from the default (the last four level-up moves at that level), and every listed move is in the species' dex level-up learnset at or below its level. Spartan teams come from Balance.

A ` / ` inside a trainer's line marks a box break.

As the contract: route trainers and Titanborn IVs 9, AI Check Bad Move; acolytes IVs 12, AI Basic Trainer; Thespis IVs 18, ace 27, two Super Potions, AI Basic Trainer; Kleon IVs 12, ace 18, AI Basic Trainer. Moves are listed only where they differ from the default (the last four level-up moves in the dex learnset at that level), and every listed move is in the species' learnset at or below that level unless the block says TM.

- **Botrykit** leads: the god's panther cub, quick and hungry, and Moxie grows with every faint.
- **Karkitox** is the shell that's a hard face over a soft body: a mask in crab form. It's his answer to Kynder players.
- **Prosomime** comes out looking like Thyrsivy. Illusion copies the last Pokémon in his party, so the Masked Player's mask plays his ace until it's hit. Hypnosis and Encore make it a tease, not a hitter.
- **Thyrsivy** is the thyrsus itself. Toxic, then Venoshock for double damage; Liquid Ooze punishes Giga Drain and Leech Seed; Black Sludge keeps it standing. Thyrsivy evolves from Ampelix at 32, so it is legal here.
- **The matchups:**
  - Nebrel players (Kladoe by now) are weak to the whole team; their answers are Lophops, Kerazap and the Halcyling gift, and Kladoe's Fairy moves are resisted by Poison too. This is the Kladoe player's hard laurel, as Chloe was the Hipling player's.
  - Kynder players (Dikyon) burn Thyrsivy and bite Prosomime; Karkitox is their wall.
  - Hipling players (Thalamare) have Bulldoze, which hits three of the four, and Thyrsivy is their threat.
- Defeat text: "Curtain! …And what a curtain."

| Kerazap | Route 9's pastures, the goatherds | Amalthea's goats; Aigion is "goat-town" |
| Melibee | Route 9, under Delphoi | the Delphic bee's first stage, which the dex puts in Delphoi's laurel groves |
| Melisseer | Kirrha's trade | the Delphic bee, Mom's kind |
| Enigmaw | the Sphinx's rocks, Route 9 | the dex's sphinx on the mountain road toward Delphoi; the Sphinx's Phikion stands over the Kopais (†, Route 8) |
| Chelonet | hills | the dex's hill tortoise |
| Cairnolith, Pebblith, Spalunk | rocks, the cave | the dex's mountain-road stones and diggers |
| Raknit | the cave, the reeds | webs in dark places (†: the dex has it in Arkadia and Astyra) |
| Persenyx | the cave's black pool, at night | the Kore's dark form, by the water of forgetting (†) |
| Harpelle | Route 9's cliffs, trainers | the dex's sea-cliff harpy (†: Parnassos's cliffs rather than Emporion's) |
| Ketofry, Kynoketos, Narkeray | fishing, trainers | the dex's every-water fish, headland serpent and crossing ray |

- **Harpelle** leads with Tailwind: the hunt starts by getting the wind behind it. Unnerve, its hidden ability, keeps the player's Berries in their pockets.
- **Lykanax** is Lykaon, the wolf-king of the mountain above Arkadia. Intimidate on the switch-in, Noble Roar after, so the player's physical hitters feel the night.
- **Oinopard** is the panther that runs with the hunt; Poison Touch makes every contact a risk.
- **Kaprodon**, the boar that only grows up in Arkadia, is the battering ram: Reckless Double-Edge. It's slow, and it's the player's window.
- **Starkos, the ace,** is Kallisto herself in the myth: the bear who became the Great Bear. Thick Fat takes the edge off the Fire and Ice moves most players reach for against a bear; Moonlight lets her outlast. Play Rough is the Fairy half, so a Dark-resisting Fighting type doesn't get a free win.
- **The matchups:**
  - Nebrel players have Daphnyad by now (Grass/Fairy, from 34), which resists Dark and hits it hard with Fairy moves. Harpelle's Acrobatics and Oinopard's Poison Jab are their threats.
  - Kynder players have Dikyon (Fire): neutral throughout, but Thick Fat blunts their best move on the ace. Their answers are Fighting moves and Galenyon or Narkeray from the coasts.
  - Hipling players have Thalamare (Water): neutral, with Kaprodon's Stomping Tantrum the threat. Seismare at 36 adds Ground, and the battle is the most even.
- Her defeat text: "…Clean. Like an arrow you never heard."

Gift I, at Artemis Favor 30, is TM Night Slash, handed over by Kallisto in person (beat 44).

| Species | Where | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Onotis | Routes 13–15, Nemea | the plain's donkeys and the vine rows |
| Chelonet | everywhere | hill tortoises; the lyre's shell |
| Kerazap | Routes 13–14, Nemea, Daphni, Route 16 | hill pastures |
| Gelasable | everywhere, mostly at night | farms; the laughing weasel |
| Kaplet | Routes 13–15 | farm pigs; Ambrosia's "silver pig"; Trygaios's sow |
| Cairnolith | Routes 13–14, Nemea, Route 16 | mountain roads; the Argolid's Cyclopean stones |
| Harpelle | Routes 13–16 | cliffs and rooftops |
| Hyphantis † | Route 14, Nemea and Route 16 at night | the Tretos pass's webs |
| Lykanax † | Route 13 at night | wolves come down from Arkadia |
| Basilops † | Routes 13–14 (1%) | the self-made king of birds, rare on the passes |
| Nemecub (static), Nemeleon † | Nemea, Routes 13–14 | the Lion's valley |
| Thyrsivy † | Nemea (1%, dusk) | Nemea's vines, the blood of Herakles |
| Stachypter, Elapling †, Korantha, Persenyx † | Route 15 | the first wheat and the Kore's plain outside Eleusa, evolved for the band |
| Basilops, Plouteras, Galenyon, Melibee | Route 15 | Phase 2's Rheitoi table, evolved for the band |
| Kynoketos, Karkitox † | Route 15's streams (rods) | the Rheitoi's salt water |
| Melibee, Melisseer † | Daphni | bees in Apollo's laurels, as at Delphoi |
| Plouteras † | Route 16 (rare) | a digger under walls |
| Glaukoin, Sophowl † | Route 16, Daphni at night | Athena's owls in her sacred olives |
| Ophidrop | Ambrosia's trade; healers' teams | Asclepius's sacred snakes |
| Chelyra, Narkeray, Midonos, Oinopard, Hoplomex | trainers only | a healer's harp, a ray for headaches, a merchant's gold, a maenad's panther, hoplites |

## The Lyceum walk, levels 36–37

The peripatetic gauntlet (Part 2, the Lyceum). The three walkers stand at the colonnade's corners facing along the walk, each with sight 4 across its width, so the walk can't be done without them. No heal between. Theophrastos waits at the end under the plane tree. Losing ends the walk; the walkers reset, and the player may try again.

**ATHLETE Autolykos.** First corner. Autolykos was the Athenian boy who won the pankration at Olympia, and the rich man's feast thrown for him is the setting of Xenophon's *Symposium*.
```text
Before: AUTOLYKOS: Walk faster! Thinking's a sprint, not a stroll!
Defeat: AUTOLYKOS: Out-thought. And out-run. Both. Ugh.
After:  AUTOLYKOS: I won at Olympia at fifteen. They threw me a feast. I slept through it.
```

|---|---|---|

| Hipling (Seismare) | Daphnyad | Grass beats Water and Ground |

- **The ace is in its final stage.** STORY.md §2's table says "Starter, stage 2 (39)", but every Aethos starter's last stage arrives by 36 (Kladoe at 34, Dikyon and Thalamare at 36), so at 39 it must be final (Open questions).
- **Alekrow is 35, not STORY.md's 36,** because it evolves into Hoplektor at 36. He has Hoplektor at Knossa.
- **Nemeleon is added** to STORY.md's four: he has one at Knossa, and his Nemecub from Thyrsa evolved at 30.
- **The pic.** `Pic: Kleon Titan` is his portrait with the bronze Titan helmet pushed back on his head like a cap. He never pulls it down.

Defeat text: "…That's not- it's written. It's WRITTEN." (STORY.md §7.3)

## Rhea of the Titans, levels 38–40

Per STORY.md §2: Ground, and every slot tells her story. She is the Titans' Ground, the tunnels and the chain, and she fights the way Lakonians speak: very little. Her look: a full bronze Corinthian helmet with the sickle on its cheek-pieces, a red-brown Lakonian cloak, a chain wrapped round her forearm. Her portrait and walker are new and faceless.

- **Cairnolith** is a grave-heap, carried for the two children she buried, and the swaddled stone Rhea gave Kronos. It leads with Stealth Rock: she lays the ground before anyone moves.
- **Plouteras** is the blind god of wealth, Demeter's child, and it digs. Body Slam is learned at 36.
- **Geogrip** is Antaeus, a son strong only while he touched his mother. Ingrain roots it to the ground, as she'd root her son if she could.
- **Kourodin,** her ace, is the shield-dancers who hid a baby's cries from Kronos. Punk Rock and Hyper Voice: the clash of bronze, loud enough to hide anything. Teeter Dance is the dance. It lives in the Lakonian battle school (dex #104), a fair clue to where she comes from, and nobody says so.
- **The matchups:** Hipling and Nebrel players have the edge on three of four; Kourodin's Steel walls Daphnyad and resists Fairy. Kynder players face four Ground or Fighting threats and should lean on Water and Flying catches, Narkeray above all.

Defeat text: "Hm. Good." (STORY.md §7.3)

Rhea's ace sits at 40, the top of BALANCE.md's Astyra boss band; Kleon's 39 sits inside it. The night's order is two doubles, Kleon, then Rhea: the climb's levels rise step by step to her.

- **Midonos** is the donkey Hephaestus rode home to Olympus, drunk (the fifth amphora's myth). Heavy Metal doubles its weight, and Iron Defense first makes Heavy Slam worse every turn.
- **Telkanvil** is a Telchine, the sea-smiths whose forge is under the cliff. Steelworker powers its Iron Head.
- **Taurivet** is one of the Khalkotauroi, the fire-breathing bronze bulls Hephaestus made. Flame Body punishes contact.
- **Belornis** is the bronze bird of Stymphalia: Hephaestus forged the rattles Herakles used to drive them off. Skill Link makes Pin Missile hit five times, and Spikes go down first.
- **Kolossard** is Talos the bronze giant, whose name the Hierophant took: "Nobody pushes a bronze man off anything." It sets Stealth Rock and brings the house down.
- **The matchups** (starters at their final stage by now):
  - Pylakyon (Fire/Ghost) players have the edge: Fire beats most of the team, and Ghost shrugs off Hyper Voice. Kolossard's Rock Slide and Bulldoze are the threat.
  - Seismare (Water/Ground) players do well too, against everything but Telkanvil and Belornis.
  - Daphnyad (Grass/Fairy) players are weak to the whole team. Their answers are Kaldera's own: Taurivet from the slopes, Kapnub from the islet, Promethex from Lampadion's trade, Chelonet from the islands.

Defeat text: "…That'll hold."

## Hyperion of the Titans, second battle, levels 42–44

**His team** (STORY.md §2, Kaldera: "Taurivet; Laolith; Pyrapod; Gigantomb (ace, about 44)"): light and fire around a buried giant, his ace the thing he fears. One level above Kaldera's boss band, because he fights after the Forge Laurel, as he fought after Chloe's in Phase 2.

- **Taurivet** leads with Anger Point: a crit and it maxes its Attack. Hyperion's temper, in a bull.
- **Laolith** is the Titans' own: a stone from Kronion Hill, traded through the crews until it grew fists. Rock Head takes the recoil out of Double-Edge.
- **Pyrapod** is the Delphic tripod, and it holds an Everstone, so it never becomes the prophet-flame it would grow into: "Some fires shouldn't turn into prophets." Will-O-Wisp burns your physical hitters.
- **Gigantomb** is the giant buried under an island, breathing smoke (dex #84, "Admin Hyperion's ace"). He sends it out in the white flash (beat 63). Solid Rock blunts super-effective hits.
- **No Apotheosis** (LABYRINTH.md).
- **The matchups:**
  - Seismare (Water/Ground) players have the edge throughout.
  - Pylakyon (Fire/Ghost) players are neutral; Laolith's and Gigantomb's Rock Slide is the threat, and Ghost can't be touched by Double-Edge.
  - Daphnyad (Grass/Fairy) players are weak to three of four. Fairy beats Laolith; the rest want Telkanvil, Narkeray, Kynoketos, Galenyon or Chelonet, all caught in this region.

Defeat text: "HA! Good! Even in the light! Who ARE you?"

## The open Aegean (optional), levels 40–45

Eighteen trainers across two sea routes and seven islands, all optional, all tuned for Act III as AETHOS_MAP asks. They reuse existing classes (SAILOR, FISHER, GOATHERD, HOPLITE, INITIATE, HARVESTER and Titanborn from the slice and Phase 2; DIVER and SMITH from region D; VINTNER from region A; PHILOSOPHER from region C2). Every team keeps the Act II conventions (IVs 9, AI Check Bad Move) and the default moves, the last four level-up moves in the dex learnset, except where noted. The grunts are STORY §5 archetypes. Levels rise with distance from the mainland: 40–41 on the first island of each route, 43–44 on the last.

# Part 4. Wild encounters

In `src/data/wild_encounters.json` terms, as in the slice and Phase 2. Land slots are 20/20/10/10/10/10/5/5/4/4/1/1. `OW_TIME_OF_DAY_ENCOUNTERS` is TRUE, so each map defines `_Morning` (used for morning, day and evening) and, where it differs, `_Night`. Fishing and water fall back to `_Morning`.

**Levels follow `design/BALANCE.md`** (the front matter's table): Thyrsa's row on Routes 7–8 and in Thyrsa, Arkadia's from Route 9 to the Pool of Mnemosyne, Astyra's from Route 13 to the salt well, Kaldera's from the *Paralos* on. No map's band is wider than 5, and the bands rise along the road. From Astyra on, lines that evolve below a map's band appear evolved (BALANCE.md), with their first stages only at the small spots the dex names.

**Deviations from the dex's habitats** are marked †, and listed in Open questions.

## Region A: the Kithairon crossing and Thyrsa

In `src/data/wild_encounters.json` terms, as in Phase 2. Land slots are 20/20/10/10/10/10/5/5/4/4/1/1. `_Morning` covers morning, day and evening; `_Night` is night. Fishing and water fall back to `_Morning`.

**Levels** are BALANCE.md's **Thyrsa** row (wild 21–28). The stage starts near Chloe's ace minus 4 and rises along the road; no band is wider than 5.

**No early evolved forms** (BALANCE.md, the director's ruling of 2026-11-14): no wild Pokémon here appears evolved below its evolution level. Cairnolith (from 25) appears only at 25 and up; Midonos (Nugget, 25 and up) only at 25 and up; Galenyon (24) only at 24 and up; Elapling (17) and Gelasable (20) are well clear. Thyrsivy (32) is never wild in region A: it comes only as an augury static (below). Deviations from the dex's habitats are marked †, and listed in region A's open questions.

## The Arkadian climb and Arkadia

Land slots are 20/20/10/10/10/10/5/5/4/4/1/1. `_Morning` covers morning, day and evening; `_Night` is the night table. Levels follow BALANCE.md's **Arkadia** row (wild 26–33): the climb starts near Thespis's ace (32) minus 3 and rises to 33 at the Pool. No band is wider than 5.

**Arkadia comes alive at night.** Its signature species (Lykopup, Amnoze, Kaprodon, the night half of Arkoby and Chelyra) are night-weighted, so the night tables are the rich ones, and the day tables are the mountain roads' ordinary mix.

**Checked against BALANCE.md's rule on evolved forms:** no wild Pokémon here is evolved below its evolution level. Lykanax appears only at 32–33 (Lykopup evolves at 30, at night), Cairnolith from 29 (25), Gelasable (20) and Kynoketos (20). Chelyra (a move evolution) and Kaprodon (a place evolution) follow their dex habitats: Kyllene's high meadows, and Arkadia's moonlit cypresses at night. Raknit and Lykopup appear at and above their evolution levels (29 and 30), as Emerald's unevolved late wild Pokémon do; it's legal under the rule, and the evolved Hyphantis stays in Astyra, as the dex has it.

## Routes 13–16, Nemea and Daphni

Every map here is BALANCE.md's **Astyra** row (wild 30–36). The stage starts at Kallisto's ace (37) minus 4, so the bands run 32–35 on Route 13 and 33–36 from Route 15 on. No band is wider than 4. Thria has no grass. Act I's Route 4, Hecate's Hollow and Route 5, which the player walks back through between Emporion and Eleusa (beat 46), keep their Act I tables.

**Evolved forms.** Two rulings apply:
- From Astyra on, a line whose evolution level sits below the band appears evolved. So the spider comes as Hyphantis, the hoopoe as Basilops, the wolf (at night) as Lykanax, the lion as Nemeleon, the mole as Plouteras, the wheat-serpent as Stachypter, the olive as Elapling, the vine as Thyrsivy.
- No wild Pokémon appears evolved below its evolution level (BALANCE.md, 2026-11-14). Every evolved form below is checked against the dex: Hyphantis (from Raknit at 29) from 33; Lykanax (Lykopup, 30) from 33; Basilops (Lophops, 32) from 33; Nemeleon (Nemecub, 30) at 35; Plouteras (Spalunk, 32) from 33; Stachypter (Stachyss, 30) from 34; Elapling (Elaleaf, 17), Thyrsivy (Ampelix, 32) at 35; Korantha and Persenyx (Rhoaril, 28) at 35–36; Sophowl (Glaukoin, 33) at 34–35; Harpelle (26), Cairnolith (25), Gelasable (20), Galenyon (24), Kynoketos (20) and Karkitox (28) well above.
- **Two capped or gender-locked lines.** Glaukoin is capped at 33, the band's low end, as the dex caps it on the Akropolis. Melibee evolves only when female, so it appears as itself; its evolved form, Melisseer, is a 1% slot.
- The Old Rod keeps its low levels (Ketofry, Karkipool), the rod's own character.

**Deviations from the dex's habitats** are marked † and listed in the open questions.

Every evolved form here sits above its evolution level: Hoplomex 22, Cairnolith 25, Gelasable 20, Galenyon 24, Harpelle 26.

Astyra and its spokes are BALANCE.md's **Astyra** row (wild 30–36). Kallisto's ace was 37, so the city's bands start near 33 and rise to the salt well; two small spots sit lower on purpose (the paupers' graves and the city's gardens), as the director's ruling allows for first stages.

**Two rules checked on every slot.**
- **No evolved form below its evolution level** (BALANCE.md, on main): Kalyptor is never under 30, Sophowl never under 33, Hyphantis never under 29, Plouteras never under 32, Galenyon never under 24, Gelasable never under 20, Harpelle never under 26, Kynoketos never under 20, Cairnolith never under 25.
- **No first stage above its evolution level** (the late-area ruling): from Astyra on, a line whose evolution level is below the band appears evolved. So Raknit appears only at 27–28, Spalunk at 31 or under, Lophops at 31 or under, Obolorn at 28 and Ophidrop at 30 or under (it evolves on its first level-up knowing Heal Pulse, learned at 30), and all of them only at the paupers' graves or in the city's gardens. Glaukoin is capped at 33, its evolution level, as dex DECISIONS has it. Chelonet is left out: it evolves on the level-up after it learns Sing at 24.

## The optional lands

**Euboia** sits on BALANCE's Arkadia row (Thyrsa's ace 32, minus 4, rising along the island to 32); Routes 17–18, Marathon, Halai and Sounion sit on the Astyra row, where lines that evolve below a map's band appear evolved (Basilops, not Lophops; Karkitox, not Karkipool; Hyphantis, not Raknit; Galenyon, not Halcyling; Plouteras, not Spalunk). No wild Pokémon is evolved below its evolution level.

**Euboia isn't in the dex,** so every species on it is a borrowing (†): the tables take the mainland's Boeotian species (from Thyrsa's vineyards and the Kopais shore) and, at Amarynthos, Artemis's Arkadian ones. Open questions 2. Elsewhere † marks the usual deviations from a dex habitat.

## The voyage, Route 19, Paros and Kaldera

Land slots are 20/20/10/10/10/10/5/5/4/4/1/1, with `_Morning` (morning, day and evening) and `_Night`. Every map here is BALANCE.md's **Kaldera** row (wild 34–40). No band is wider than 5, and the bands rise from the voyage to the islet.

**No early evolved forms** (BALANCE.md, the director's rule): every table was checked against the dex's "Evolves from X at level N". Galenyon is never under 24, Kynoketos never under 20, Harpelle never under 26, Cairnolith never under 25, Taurivet never under 33, Telkanvil never under 34, Gigantomb never under 35. **First stages stay under their evolution level:** Telpup is capped at 34 and Kapnub at 35 (dex DECISIONS), Kaminoo lives only in the warm hollow at 31, Ketofry only on the Old Rod, Karkipool only on the Old and Good Rods. Lophops and Pebblith, whose evolutions sit below this band and live elsewhere, are left out.

**Deviations from the dex's habitats** are marked † and listed in Open questions.
